folder: Clinical Medicine and Surgery I Exam 1

items.section_title: 7.2 · Objective a — Abnormal wound healing: keloid and hypertrophic scar
items.html: Post-surgical advice for keloid-prone patients. Avoid stretching the immature scar, avoid hot baths, keep the wound clean, and avoid body piercings; stretching provokes scar inflammation and overgrowth, and hot baths can aggravate surgery-induced inflammation.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 20

src.question: What post-surgical advice is given to a patient prone to keloids?
src.key: Avoid stretching the immature scar, avoid hot baths, keep the wound clean, and avoid body piercings
src.explanation: Correct — hot baths can aggravate surgery-induced inflammation.

also.key: Do not stretch the immature scar, avoid hot baths, keep it clean
also.explanation: Correct — stretching provokes scar inflammation and overgrowth, and hot baths can aggravate surgery-induced inflammation.

items.section_title: 7.3 · Objective a — Cutaneous horn and skin tags
items.html: Cutaneous horn management. It depends on the underlying etiology, with excision to the standard for the tumor type and location if malignant; treat what is at the base, not the horn.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 28

src.question: What determines the management of a cutaneous horn?
src.key: The underlying etiology, with excision to the standard for the tumor type and location if malignant
src.explanation: Correct — you treat what is at the base, not the horn.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: Cherry angiomas. Patients should be told that new lesions will likely develop and there is no way to prevent them; treatment is not necessary unless they bother the patient.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 87

src.question: What should a patient be told about cherry angiomas?
src.key: New lesions will likely develop and there is no way to prevent them
src.explanation: Correct — treatment is not necessary unless they bother the patient.

also.key: New lesions will likely develop and there is no way to prevent them
also.explanation: Correct — treatment is not necessary unless they bother him.

items.section_title: 7.1 · Objective a — Corns, calluses, and the wart that mimics them
items.html: Calluses. They typically develop on the palms of the hands or the balls of the feet; if the process is acute and severe, a blister forms.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 6

src.question: Where do calluses typically develop, and what happens if the process is acute and severe?
src.key: On the palms of the hands or the balls of the feet; a blister forms
src.explanation: Correct — a blister is the acute end of the same friction process.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: History in spider angiomas. Cover pregnancies, hormone use, alcohol history, and medications that carry a risk of liver damage, because the lesion can be a marker of estrogen excess or liver disease.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 90

src.question: What should the history cover in a patient with spider angiomas?
src.key: Pregnancies, hormone use, alcohol history, and medications that carry a risk of liver damage
src.explanation: Correct — the lesion can be a marker of estrogen excess or liver disease.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: Nevus flammeus over time. Early, it is a flat blanchable patch, well-circumscribed, pink to red to purple, usually unilateral with fairly sharp midline cutoffs; later the vasculature dilates and it may become a raised, thickened plaque of deeper color.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 80

src.question: What does nevus flammeus look like early in life, and later?
src.key: Early, a flat blanchable patch; later, a raised thickened plaque of deeper color
src.explanation: Correct — early it is well-circumscribed and macular, pink to red to purple, usually unilateral with fairly sharp midline cutoffs, and it darkens with crying, fever or overheating. Later the vasculature dilates and it may become a raised, thickened, deep-red to purple plaque.

items.section_title: 7.2 · Objective a — Abnormal wound healing: keloid and hypertrophic scar
items.html: Radiation for keloids. It may be used during the first two weeks after the keloid has been excised, as an adjunct to surgery rather than a primary treatment.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 18

src.question: When may radiation be used for a keloid?
src.key: During the first two weeks after the keloid has been excised
src.explanation: Correct — it is an adjunct to surgery rather than a primary treatment.

items.section_title: 7.4 · Objective a — Pressure injury and pilonidal disease
items.html: Pilonidal disease education. Maintain good hygiene, and seek care if an abscess occurs; recurrence is common, so this is ongoing advice.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 43

src.question: What patient education is given for pilonidal disease?
src.key: Maintain good hygiene, and seek care if an abscess occurs
src.explanation: Correct — recurrence is common, so this is ongoing advice.

items.section_title: 7.5 · Objective a — The nodules that must be told from a cancer
items.html: Epidermoid cyst testing. Laboratory testing is usually not required, because the diagnosis is clinical.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 55

src.question: What laboratory testing does an epidermoid cyst require?
src.key: Usually none
src.explanation: Correct — the diagnosis is clinical.

items.section_title: 7.2 · Objective a — Abnormal wound healing: keloid and hypertrophic scar
items.html: Compression therapy for keloids. The regimen is 25 millimeters of mercury, round the clock, for six to twelve months; the mechanism is not understood but possibly induces tissue hypoxia with fibroblast degeneration and subsequent collagen degradation.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 17

src.question: A patient is offered compression therapy for a keloid. Which regimen is correct?
src.key: Twenty-five millimeters of mercury, round the clock, six to twelve months
src.explanation: Correct — the mechanism is not understood, but it possibly induces tissue hypoxia with fibroblast degeneration and subsequent collagen degradation.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: Natural course of a raised red plaque in an infant. Most involute on their own over several years: complete involution in fifty percent by age five, seventy percent by seven and ninety percent by nine, so serial observation is often all that is needed.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 66

src.question: A 6-week-old former preterm girl has a bright red raised plaque on her scalp. Her mother says the area first looked pale, then developed fine red lines, and now asks whether it will need surgery. Which is the most appropriate answer?
src.key: Most involute on their own over several years
src.explanation: Correct — complete involution in fifty percent by age five, seventy percent by seven and ninety percent by nine, so serial observation is often all that is needed.

items.section_title: 7.4 · Objective a — Pressure injury and pilonidal disease
items.html: Pilonidal disease testing. No diagnostic testing is usually needed; the diagnosis is clinical.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 43

src.question: Which diagnostic testing does this patient's pilonidal disease require?
src.key: None; the diagnosis is clinical
src.explanation: Correct — no testing is usually needed.

items.section_title: 7.5 · Objective a — The nodules that must be told from a cancer
items.html: Epidermoid cyst contents. It is often called a sebaceous cyst because the material looks like sebum, but the contents are keratin, not sebum.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 53

src.question: A 45-year-old man has a firm, movable, round nodule on his upper back with a small central pore that expresses cream-colored pasty material. He asks whether it is a sebaceous cyst full of oil. Which is the most appropriate response?
src.key: The contents are keratin, not sebum
src.explanation: Correct — it is often called a sebaceous cyst because the material looks like sebum, but the contents are keratin.

items.section_title: 7.2 · Objective a — Abnormal wound healing: keloid and hypertrophic scar
items.html: Surgical excision of a keloid alone. Recurrence is fifty to one hundred percent and the recurrent lesion is often larger than the original, so excision is never done alone and steroid injection follows; combination therapy has the best success rates.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 18

src.question: A 26-year-old with a keloid on the sternum wants it removed. Which is the most appropriate advice about surgical excision alone?
src.key: Recurrence is fifty to one hundred percent, so steroid injection follows
src.explanation: Correct — the recurrent lesion is often larger than the original, which is why excision is never done alone. Combination therapy has the best success rates.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: History in spider angiomas. Take alcohol use, liver-damaging medication and hormone use, and ask about pregnancies too; spider angiomas track estrogen excess and cirrhosis or liver failure.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 90

src.question: A 44-year-old man has several small vascular lesions with a central punctum and radiating vessels across his upper chest and arms. Which history is most important to take?
src.key: Alcohol use, liver-damaging medications, and hormone use
src.explanation: Correct — ask about pregnancies too. Spider angiomas track estrogen excess and cirrhosis or liver failure.

items.section_title: 7.1 · Objective a — Corns, calluses, and the wart that mimics them
items.html: Preventing callus recurrence. Well-fitting shoes and socks and pads inside the shoe remove the friction so the lesion stops re-forming; tight shoes, high heels and wearing shoes without socks are named as causes.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 10

src.question: A 29-year-old asks how to stop her calluses coming back. Which is the most appropriate advice?
src.key: Well-fitting shoes and socks, and pads inside the shoe
src.explanation: Correct — remove the friction and the lesion stops re-forming. Tight shoes and high heels are named as causes, as is wearing shoes without socks.

items.section_title: 7.3 · Objective a — Cutaneous horn and skin tags
items.html: Cutaneous horn epidemiology. It is seen in Caucasians over fifty, on the head, neck and upper extremities, such as a lesion on the ear.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 26

src.question: Four patients each have a hard, hornlike keratotic projection. Which of them best matches the epidemiology of cutaneous horn?
src.key: A 62-year-old Caucasian with a lesion on the ear
src.explanation: Correct — Caucasians over fifty, on head, neck and upper extremities.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: Excision of a bleeding red papule. Surgical excision has the lowest recurrence rate and also provides histopathologic analysis, at the cost of the highest rate of scarring.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 95

src.question: A 16-year-old has a moist, bright red papule with an epithelial collarette on the finger pad of her left fourth digit that bleeds readily. She wants it removed and asks which option is least likely to come back. Which is the most appropriate answer?
src.key: Surgical excision, though it scars the most
src.explanation: Correct — it has the lowest recurrence rate and also provides histopathologic analysis, at the cost of the highest rate of scarring.

items.section_title: 7.2 · Objective a — Abnormal wound healing: keloid and hypertrophic scar
items.html: Raised scar confined to the incision. A raised, firm, red scar that stops exactly at the edges of the original incision should stay stable and then flatten with time, which is why observation is reasonable.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 21

src.question: A 30-year-old man had an appendicectomy five weeks ago. The scar is raised, firm and red but stops exactly at the edges of the original incision. He asks what will happen to it over the next year. Which is the most appropriate answer?
src.key: It should stay stable and then flatten with time
src.explanation: Correct — that natural history is the reason observation is reasonable.

items.section_title: 7.7 · Objectives a & b — Neurofibromatosis, and the remaining lesions
items.html: Uncertain basal cell carcinoma. The next step is dermoscopy, with biopsy if concern remains.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 111

src.question: You are not certain whether one of those lesions is a basal cell carcinoma. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Dermoscopy, which can distinguish the two, with biopsy if concern remains
src.explanation: Correct — patients often present worried about exactly this.

items.section_title: 1.1 · Objective a — Compare and contrast sensitivity and specificity
items.html: Sensitivity. It is related to fewer false-negatives and does not address false-positives.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 6

src.question: Sensitivity is specifically related to fewer of which type of erroneous result?
src.key: Fewer false-negatives
src.explanation: Sensitivity is related to fewer false-negatives, and does not address false-positives.

items.section_title: 1.1 · Objective a — Compare and contrast sensitivity and specificity
items.html: Highly sensitive test. A negative result is most useful for ruling the disease out in that patient (SnNout: high Sensitivity and a Negative result help rule out a disease).
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 6

src.question: A highly sensitive test with a negative result is most useful for which purpose?
src.key: Ruling the disease out in that patient
src.explanation: SnNout: a test with high Sensitivity and a Negative result helps rule out a disease.

items.section_title: 6.4 · Objective b — The yeasts: candidal intertrigo and pityriasis versicolor
items.html: Cutaneous candidiasis appearance. It is beefy red in the depth of the fold, with satellite papules scattered beyond the edge.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 69

src.question: Name the condition shown.
src.key: Cutaneous candidiasis
src.explanation: BEEFY RED in the depth of the fold with SATELLITE papules scattered beyond the edge.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Highest-mortality epidermolysis bullosa subtype. Junctional epidermolysis bullosa, especially the Herlitz subtype, carries the highest mortality, so early palliative care integration is appropriate in severe Herlitz disease.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 29

src.question: Which epidermolysis bullosa subtype carries the highest mortality?
src.key: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa, especially the Herlitz subtype
src.explanation: which is why early palliative care integration is appropriate in severe Herlitz disease.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective c — Alopecia
items.html: Male-pattern hair loss. Dihydrotestosterone is the androgen chiefly responsible; it is an androgen-dependent trait with a strong paternal influence on risk.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 145

src.question: Which androgen is chiefly responsible for male-pattern hair loss?
src.key: Dihydrotestosterone
src.explanation: Correct — male-pattern hair loss is an androgen-dependent trait with a strong paternal influence on risk.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Ulceration versus erosion. Ulceration is full-thickness loss extending to the dermis or deeper, whereas an erosion loses only the epidermis; depth is the discriminator and determines whether the lesion can scar.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 17

src.question: What distinguishes an ulceration from an erosion?
src.key: An ulceration is full-thickness loss extending to the dermis or deeper; an erosion loses only the epidermis
src.explanation: Correct — depth is the discriminator, and it determines whether the lesion can scar.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Hyperhidrosis counseling. It is not about poor hygiene or anxiety; suggest moisture-wicking clothing, which reduces impairment, and set realistic expectations, including botulinum toxin retreatment every three to six months.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 76

src.question: Which points should the conversation with a hyperhidrosis patient cover?
src.key: That it is not about poor hygiene or anxiety, with moisture-wicking clothing suggested and realistic expectations set
src.explanation: Correct — hyperhidrosis is a medical condition, moisture-wicking clothing reduces impairment, and realistic expectations include botulinum toxin retreatment every three to six months.

items.section_title: 7.5 · Objective a — The nodules that must be told from a cancer
items.html: Squamous cell carcinoma risk factors. Besides sun exposure and immunosuppression: chronic wounds, scars or prior radiation fields; certain genetic diseases; and mucosal or genital disease.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 21

src.question: Besides sun exposure and immunosuppression, which risk factors apply to squamous cell carcinoma?
src.key: Chronic wounds, scars or prior radiation fields; certain genetic diseases; and mucosal or genital disease
src.explanation: Correct — the three additional categories as listed.

items.section_title: 9.8 · Objective 11 — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Diagnosing squamous cell carcinoma. Use shave, punch or excisional biopsy sampling sufficient depth to separate in situ from invasive disease, because they carry different treatment, margins and risk.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 23

src.question: How is a suspected squamous cell carcinoma diagnosed, and what must the sample achieve?
src.key: Shave, punch or excisional biopsy sampling sufficient depth to separate in situ from invasive disease
src.explanation: Correct — depth is the point, because in situ and invasive carry different treatment, margins and risk.

items.section_title: 6.4 · Objective b — The yeasts: candidal intertrigo and pityriasis versicolor
items.html: Recurrent candidal intertrigo. Recurrent or extensive disease prompts evaluation for diabetes and immunosuppression.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 72

src.question: A patient has recurrent, extensive candidal intertrigo. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Evaluate for diabetes and immunosuppression
src.explanation: Correct — recurrent or extensive disease prompts this.

items.section_title: 9.2 · Objective 1 — Actinic keratosis
items.html: Concerning actinic keratosis. Induration, tenderness and bleeding are the concerning features named for progression; biopsy the lesion to exclude invasive squamous cell carcinoma.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 113

src.question: A 66-year-old woman has an actinic keratosis on the cheek that has become indurated, tender and has bled twice. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Biopsy the lesion to exclude invasive squamous cell carcinoma
src.explanation: Correct — induration, tenderness and bleeding are the concerning features named for progression.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Psoriatic arthritis radiograph. The expected finding is a pencil-in-a-cup deformity; psoriatic arthritis is associated with HLA-B27 and affects the distal and proximal interphalangeal joints while sparing the metacarpophalangeals.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 161

src.question: A 44-year-old with psoriasis has painful, stiff fingers each morning for over an hour, easing with activity. Examination shows a swollen sausage-shaped third digit, and the nails show pitting and separation of the plate from the bed. Which radiographic finding would you expect?
src.key: Pencil-in-a-cup deformity
src.explanation: Correct — psoriatic arthritis, associated with HLA-B27, affecting the distal and proximal interphalangeal joints while sparing the metacarpophalangeals.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Resistant dermatophytosis. Suspect it when disease is widespread, intensely inflammatory, epidemiologically linked, or refractory to an adequate terbinafine course; obtain species identification and susceptibility testing when available.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 29

src.question: When should resistant dermatophytosis be suspected?
src.key: Widespread, intensely inflammatory, linked, or terbinafine-refractory
src.explanation: Correct — epidemiologically linked cases and failure of an adequate terbinafine course both count. Obtain species identification and susceptibility testing when available.

items.section_title: 3.2 · Objective a — Lesions that signal systemic disease
items.html: Dermatitis herpetiformis distribution. The eruption is symmetric on the knees, elbows, buttocks and back, with intensely pruritic papules and vesicles that group in a herpetiform pattern.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 18

src.question: Where is the eruption of dermatitis herpetiformis distributed?
src.key: Symmetrically on the knees, elbows, buttocks and back
src.explanation: Correct — intensely pruritic papules and vesicles that group in a herpetiform pattern.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Confirming Kaposi sarcoma. Biopsy a representative lesion; human herpesvirus 8-associated findings on histology support the diagnosis.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 65

src.question: How is Kaposi sarcoma confirmed, and what supports the diagnosis on histology?
src.key: Biopsy of a representative lesion, with human herpesvirus 8-associated findings supporting it
src.explanation: Correct — the virus links the histology back to the cause.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Primary hyperhidrosis. It is a medical condition rather than a problem of hygiene or anxiety, with quality-of-life impairment comparable to severe psoriasis.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 76

src.question: A 24-year-old woman with primary hyperhidrosis says she has been told repeatedly that she just needs to wash more and relax. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: Primary hyperhidrosis is a medical condition rather than a problem of hygiene or anxiety
src.explanation: Correct — primary hyperhidrosis is not caused by poor hygiene or anxiety; it is a medical condition, with quality-of-life impairment comparable to severe psoriasis.

items.section_title: 6.6 · Objective b — Herpes simplex and herpetic whitlow
items.html: Dermatitis herpetiformis immunology. Immunoglobulin A antibodies against epidermal transglutaminase form complexes that deposit in the dermal papillae; complement and neutrophils are then activated, producing subepidermal blisters.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 16

src.question: What is the immunological basis of dermatitis herpetiformis?
src.key: Immunoglobulin A antibodies against epidermal transglutaminase, forming complexes that deposit in the dermal papillae
src.explanation: Correct — complement and neutrophils are then activated, producing subepidermal blisters.

items.section_title: 6.5 · Objective b — Varicella and herpes zoster
items.html: Herpes zoster scarring. It scars when deeper epidermal or dermal layers are compromised by excoriation or secondary infection; otherwise it typically heals without visible sequelae.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 99

src.question: When does herpes zoster scar?
src.key: When deeper epidermal or dermal layers are compromised by excoriation or secondary infection
src.explanation: Correct — it typically heals without visible sequelae otherwise.

items.section_title: 4.4 · Objective a — Paronychia and necrotizing fasciitis
items.html: Laboratory studies in necrotizing fasciitis. Send complete blood count with differential, chemistry, arterial blood gas, urinalysis, and blood and tissue cultures, but they must not delay surgical intervention, because it is a surgical emergency with high mortality.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 128

src.question: A 52-year-old man with suspected necrotizing fasciitis is being prepared for theater. Which laboratory studies should be sent?
src.key: Complete blood count with differential, chemistry, arterial blood gas, urinalysis, and blood and tissue cultures
src.explanation: Correct — they are sent, but they must not delay the surgical intervention itself.

also.key: They should not delay surgical intervention, because this is a surgical emergency with high mortality
also.explanation: Blood count, chemistry, arterial blood gas, urinalysis and cultures are all sent.

items.section_title: 6.5 · Objective b — Varicella and herpes zoster
items.html: Polymerase chain reaction in herpes zoster. Use it for atypical, disseminated, vaccine-modified or immunocompromised presentations, on vesicle fluid, scab, or cells from the lesion base; typical unilateral dermatomal vesicles are diagnosed clinically.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 105

src.question: When should polymerase chain reaction be used in suspected herpes zoster, and from what?
src.key: For atypical, disseminated, vaccine-modified or immunocompromised presentations; from vesicle fluid, scab, or cells from the lesion base
src.explanation: Correct — typical unilateral dermatomal vesicles are diagnosed clinically.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective c — Alopecia
items.html: Minoxidil. It is primarily effective in the crown region of the scalp; it prevents further loss and may produce regrowth, working best with finasteride.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 148

src.question: Where is minoxidil primarily effective?
src.key: In the crown region of the scalp
src.explanation: Correct — it prevents further loss and may produce regrowth, working best with finasteride.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Preventing hot tub folliculitis. Maintain continuous water filtration, monitor disinfectant levels and change the water often; showering after contact does not prevent the infection.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 53

src.question: A 42-year-old man whose two children developed hot tub folliculitis last month asks how to stop it happening again. Which is the most appropriate advice?
src.key: Maintain continuous water filtration, monitor disinfectant levels and change the water often
src.explanation: Showering after contact does not prevent the infection.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Counseling during scabies treatment. Excessive washing with harsh soap can worsen skin irritation and should be stopped; the permethrin course itself is what treats the infestation.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 19

src.question: A 45-year-old man treated for scabies has scrubbed his skin with a strong antibacterial soap several times a day and now has widespread irritation. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: Excessive washing with harsh soap can worsen the skin irritation and should be stopped
src.explanation: Correct — the permethrin course itself is what treats the infestation.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Kaposi sarcoma immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome. It is especially dangerous in patients with visceral disease; endemic or visceral disease with this syndrome can be aggressive and rapidly fatal.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 63

src.question: In which patients is Kaposi sarcoma immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome especially dangerous?
src.key: Those with visceral disease
src.explanation: Correct — endemic or visceral disease and this syndrome can be aggressive and rapidly fatal.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective c — Alopecia
items.html: Scalp biopsy in alopecia. It is performed when scarring alopecia, diffuse atypical loss or persistent diagnostic uncertainty remains after clinical and dermoscopic assessment.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 139

src.question: A 35-year-old man has patchy hair loss with an unusual scarred appearance in one area and diffuse atypical loss elsewhere, and the picture remains unclear after dermoscopy. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Scalp biopsy
src.explanation: Correct — biopsy is performed when scarring alopecia, diffuse atypical loss or persistent diagnostic uncertainty remains after clinical and dermoscopic assessment.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Hot tub folliculitis course. It is usually self-limiting, clearing in two to ten days; ciprofloxacin is reserved for widespread or resistant cases.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 52

src.question: What is the natural course of hot tub folliculitis?
src.key: Usually self-limiting, clearing in two to ten days
src.explanation: Correct — ciprofloxacin is reserved for widespread or resistant cases.

items.section_title: 4.4 · Objective a — Paronychia and necrotizing fasciitis
items.html: Testing in acute paronychia. It is usually a clinical diagnosis, so testing is directed rather than routine: Gram stain and culture for the bacterial cause, potassium hydroxide for candida, and Tzanck smear for herpetic whitlow.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 118

src.question: Which tests may be used in acute paronychia and what does each exclude?
src.key: Gram stain and culture for the bacterial cause, potassium hydroxide for candida, Tzanck smear for herpetic whitlow
src.explanation: It is usually a clinical diagnosis, so testing is directed rather than routine.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Preventing erythrasma recurrence. Keep the area clean and dry, avoid excessive heat and moisture, and maintain a healthy body weight, alongside good general hygiene.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 84

src.question: A 60-year-old man treated for erythrasma asks how to stop it returning. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: Keep the area clean and dry, avoid excessive heat and moisture, and maintain a healthy body weight
src.explanation: alongside good general hygiene.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Acanthosis nigricans counseling. It is a metabolic warning sign of insulin resistance rather than a hygiene problem, and losing even 5 to 10% of body weight improves the findings.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 25

src.question: A 17-year-old girl with acanthosis nigricans is embarrassed and has been scrubbing her neck daily, believing it is dirt. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: The change is a metabolic warning sign rather than a hygiene problem, and 5 to 10% weight loss improves it
src.explanation: Correct — acanthosis nigricans is a metabolic warning sign, not a hygiene issue, and even a 5 to 10% reduction in body weight improves the findings.

also.key: It is a metabolic warning sign rather than a hygiene problem, and 5 to 10% weight loss improves the findings
also.explanation: Correct — acanthosis nigricans signals insulin resistance rather than poor hygiene, and losing even 5 to 10% of body weight improves the findings.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Most common acanthosis nigricans. Hyperinsulinemia stimulates keratinocyte and fibroblast proliferation through insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor cross-activation; this insulin-resistant or benign form is the commonest, and malignant, drug-induced and endocrine forms make up the rest.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 22

src.question: What mechanism underlies the most common form of acanthosis nigricans?
src.key: Hyperinsulinemia stimulating keratinocyte and fibroblast proliferation through insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor cross-activation
src.explanation: Correct — the insulin-resistant or benign form is the commonest.

also.key: Hyperinsulinemia stimulating keratinocyte and fibroblast proliferation through insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor cross-activation
also.explanation: Malignant, drug-induced and endocrine forms make up the rest.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Severe or extensive allergic contact dermatitis. Treat with high-dose oral corticosteroids tapered over two to three weeks, because early discontinuation causes high rates of rebound; limited eruptions can be managed with high-potency topical steroids.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 89

src.question: How are severe or extensive allergic contact dermatitis eruptions treated?
src.key: High-dose oral corticosteroids tapered over two to three weeks, because early discontinuation causes high rates of rebound
src.explanation: Limited eruptions can be managed with high-potency topical steroids.

also.key: High-dose oral corticosteroids tapered over two to three weeks
also.explanation: Correct — extensive disease needs systemic therapy, and early discontinuation causes high rates of rebound.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Macule. It is a flat lesion less than one centimeter, without elevation or depression; a patch is the same lesion larger than one centimeter.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 10

src.question: How is a macule defined?
src.key: A flat lesion less than one centimeter, without elevation or depression
src.explanation: A patch is the same lesion larger than one centimeter.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Polymorphous light eruption presentation. Papules appear thirty minutes to hours after exposure on the décolletage, forearms and dorsal hands, sparing chronically exposed skin, resolving in seven to ten days without scarring and recurring each spring.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 105

src.question: How does polymorphous light eruption typically present?
src.key: Papules appearing thirty minutes to hours after exposure on the décolletage, forearms and dorsal hands, sparing chronically exposed skin
src.explanation: resolving in seven to ten days without scarring and recurring each spring.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Epidermolysis bullosa referrals. Referral is needed to essentially every specialty, given the multisystem burden; palliative care, genetics and family support are all involved.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 31

src.question: How broad is the referral requirement in epidermolysis bullosa?
src.key: Essentially every specialty, given the multisystem burden
src.explanation: Correct — palliative care, genetics and family support are all involved.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Urushiol lesions. They are intensely pruritic vesicular lesions in linear distributions, erupting within 4 to 96 hours and persisting up to 3 weeks; the linear pattern comes from grazing the plant in passing.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 87

src.question: How do urushiol lesions present, and over what time course?
src.key: Intensely pruritic vesicular lesions in linear distributions, erupting within 4 to 96 hours and persisting up to 3 weeks
src.explanation: Correct — the linear pattern comes from grazing the plant in passing.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Hardening in polymorphous light eruption. This is improvement through the summer as tolerance develops after repeated exposure; prophylactic narrowband ultraviolet B in spring is the most effective preventive strategy.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 104

src.question: What is the hardening phenomenon in polymorphous light eruption?
src.key: Improvement through the summer as tolerance develops after repeated exposure
src.explanation: which is also why prophylactic narrowband ultraviolet B in spring is the most effective preventive strategy.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Facility-associated scabies. It is a particular concern because residents are elderly and immunosuppressed, and a hospital epidemic can follow their admission; it is difficult to eradicate once healthcare workers are infested.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 5

src.question: Why is facility-associated scabies a particular concern?
src.key: Residents are elderly and immunosuppressed, and a hospital epidemic can follow their admission
src.explanation: and it is difficult to eradicate once healthcare workers are infested.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Objective a — Tick-borne illness
items.html: Rocky Mountain spotted fever. Rickettsia rickettsii, carried by dog ticks, wood ticks and rodents, causes it; risk is higher in males, adults 40 to 64, children under 10 and rural dwellers. It is prevalent in southeastern and south central states in spring and early summer.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 81

src.question: Which risk factors are named for Rocky Mountain spotted fever?
src.key: Male sex, adults aged 40 to 64, children under 10, and rural dwelling
src.explanation: Correct — it is prevalent in southeastern and south central states in spring and early summer.

also.key: Rickettsia rickettsii, carried by dog ticks, wood ticks and rodents; risk is higher in males, adults 40 to 64, children under 10 and rural dwellers
also.explanation: Correct — it is prevalent in southeastern and south central states in spring and early summer.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Sunburn management. Do not pop blisters, because intact blisters are protective; use cool rather than cold water.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 96

src.question: Which measure is specifically advised against in the management of sunburn?
src.key: Popping blisters, because intact blisters are protective
src.explanation: Correct — cool rather than cold water is also specified.

items.section_title: 8.5 · Objective b — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Treating freckles. Start with sun protection and counseling, then topical depigmenting agents, with intense pulsed light or laser if needed; the topical options are hydroquinone, retinoids, alpha-hydroxy acids and botanicals.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 7

src.question: A 24-year-old woman with freckles across her cheeks asks what will reduce them. Which is the most appropriate treatment plan?
src.key: Sun protection and counseling first, then topical depigmenting agents, with intense pulsed light or laser if needed
src.explanation: Correct — hydroquinone, retinoids, alpha-hydroxy acids and botanicals are the topical options.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective c — Alopecia
items.html: Finasteride. It is an oral 5-alpha-reductase type 2 inhibitor; about 2% of men report reduced libido and erectile function, reversible on stopping. It works best combined with minoxidil, is not indicated in women and is contraindicated in pregnancy.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 148

src.question: A 36-year-old man wishes to treat male-pattern hair loss and asks about finasteride. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: About 2% of men report reduced libido and erectile function, and these effects reverse when the drug is stopped
src.explanation: It works best combined with minoxidil, and it is not indicated in women and contraindicated in pregnancy.

also.key: An oral 5-alpha-reductase type 2 inhibitor; about 2% of men report reduced libido and erectile function, reversible on stopping, and it is not indicated in women and contraindicated in pregnancy
also.explanation: and it works best combined with minoxidil.

items.section_title: 2.6 · Common dermatologic pharmacology
items.html: Biopsy of lichen simplex chronicus. Biopsy a plaque that is atypical, unilateral, nodular, ulcerated or treatment-resistant, to exclude neoplasia or another inflammatory disorder.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 182

src.question: When should a lichen simplex chronicus plaque be biopsied?
src.key: When it is atypical, unilateral, nodular, ulcerated or treatment-resistant
src.explanation: Correct — the purpose is to exclude neoplasia or another inflammatory disorder.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma prognosis. Tumors, erythroderma and lymphadenopathy worsen prognosis; survival is not reduced in limited patch-stage disease.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 76

src.question: Which cutaneous T-cell lymphoma features worsen prognosis, and which carries the best?
src.key: Tumors, erythroderma and lymphadenopathy worsen it; limited patch disease does not reduce survival
src.explanation: Correct — survival is not reduced in limited patch-stage disease.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective c — Alopecia
items.html: Supportive care in alopecia areata. Psychological support, with support groups offered, is one of the most important considerations.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 140

src.question: Which supportive measure is described as one of the most important considerations in alopecia areata?
src.key: Psychological support, with support groups offered
src.explanation: Correct — the visible nature of the condition carries real psychological weight.

items.section_title: 9.2 · Objective 1 — Actinic keratosis
items.html: Actinic keratosis versus early squamous cell carcinoma. Squamous cell carcinoma must be excluded when a lesion is thick, indurated, ulcerated, enlarging, painful, bleeding, persistent or recurrent.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 13

src.question: Which lesion features make early squamous cell carcinoma the distinction to exclude in an actinic keratosis?
src.key: Thick, indurated, ulcerated, enlarging, painful, bleeding, persistent or recurrent
src.explanation: Correct — these are the features that shift the concern to carcinoma.

items.section_title: 5.3 · Objective a — Cutaneous larva migrans and cercarial dermatitis
items.html: Cercarial dermatitis systemic features. Headaches, fever and lymphangitis can accompany it; pain and swelling peak at forty-eight to seventy-two hours.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 90

src.question: Which systemic features can accompany cercarial dermatitis?
src.key: Headaches, fever and lymphangitis
src.explanation: Correct — pain and swelling peak at forty-eight to seventy-two hours.

items.section_title: 4.4 · Objective a — Paronychia and necrotizing fasciitis
items.html: Testing in classic erysipelas. No laboratory or imaging studies are routine; the diagnosis is clinical and blood and tissue cultures have very low yield. Leukocytosis and raised inflammatory markers are common but not diagnostic.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 103

src.question: Which laboratory and imaging studies are appropriate in classic erysipelas?
src.key: None routinely — the diagnosis is clinical, and blood and tissue cultures have very low yield
src.explanation: Leukocytosis and raised inflammatory markers are common but not diagnostic.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Purulent wound testing. Order bacterial culture and sensitivity: the culture names the organism and the sensitivity directs the antibiotic.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 29

src.question: A 52-year-old man has a purulent wound and the clinician wants to know both what is growing and what will treat it. Which test should be ordered?
src.key: Bacterial culture and sensitivity
src.explanation: Correct — the culture names the organism and the sensitivity directs the antibiotic.

items.section_title: 9.2 · Objective 1 — Actinic keratosis
items.html: Thickened, indurated, bleeding actinic keratosis. Order a shave or punch biopsy, because induration and bleeding raise concern for squamous cell carcinoma and are not part of a typical actinic keratosis.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 13

src.question: One of that 71-year-old's scalp lesions is now thickened, indurated and has bled twice. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Order a shave or punch biopsy, because induration and bleeding raise concern for squamous cell carcinoma
src.explanation: Correct — those features are not part of a typical actinic keratosis.

items.section_title: 6.2 · Objective b — The dermatophytes, by body site
items.html: Imidazole antifungals. They block ergosterol synthesis, as clotrimazole and ketoconazole do; ergosterol is a vital component of the fungal cell membrane, so blocking it halts growth and replication.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 5

src.question: How does the imidazole class work, and what are two examples?
src.key: It blocks ergosterol synthesis; clotrimazole and ketoconazole
src.explanation: Correct — ergosterol is a vital component of the fungal cell membrane, so blocking it halts growth and replication. The names end in -azole.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Fixed drug eruption versus erythema multiforme. Fixed drug eruption recurs at the same site, leaves residual hyperpigmentation, and has few lesions without three concentric zones; the three-zone target defines an erythema multiforme lesion.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 10

src.question: Which features separate a fixed drug eruption from erythema multiforme?
src.key: It recurs at the same site, leaves residual hyperpigmentation, and has few lesions without three concentric zones
src.explanation: Correct — the three-zone target is what defines an erythema multiforme lesion.

items.section_title: 9.7 · Objective 1 — Nail unit neoplasms
items.html: Biopsy of a suspicious nail lesion. It requires prompt referral to a dermatologist experienced in nail-unit biopsy, with the biopsy sampling the correct site.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 93

src.question: What does a biopsy for a suspicious nail lesion require?
src.key: Prompt referral to a dermatologist experienced in nail-unit biopsy, with the biopsy sampling the correct site
src.explanation: Correct — the referral is to someone experienced in the nail unit specifically.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Polymorphous light eruption workup. An antinuclear antibody panel including anti-Ro and anti-La is described as mandatory before the diagnosis is accepted, because lupus can present identically and must be excluded.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 106

src.question: A 35-year-old woman has a clinically typical polymorphous light eruption. Which investigation is described as mandatory before the diagnosis is accepted?
src.key: An antinuclear antibody panel including anti-Ro and anti-La
src.explanation: Correct — lupus must be excluded because it can present identically.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Specimens in serious cellulitis. Take blood cultures and a skin punch biopsy, alongside a complete blood count and creatine phosphokinase, with imaging considered for underlying fasciitis or osteomyelitis.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 109

src.question: Which specimens are taken in serious cellulitis?
src.key: Blood cultures and a skin punch biopsy
src.explanation: alongside a complete blood count and creatine phosphokinase.

also.key: Blood cultures, punch biopsy, complete blood count and creatine phosphokinase
also.explanation: with imaging considered for underlying fasciitis or osteomyelitis.

items.section_title: 5.2 · Objective a — Bedbugs, fleas, stings and caterpillars
items.html: Bedbug bites. The usual reaction is wheals and papules with a hemorrhagic punctum; a bullous reaction occurs particularly in sensitized patients.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 33

src.question: Which reaction to bedbug bites occurs particularly in sensitized patients?
src.key: A bullous reaction
src.explanation: Correct — the usual reaction is wheals and papules with a hemorrhagic punctum.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Granuloma annulare counseling. It is benign and self-limiting, with about half resolving within two years and no malignant potential, so treatment is for cosmesis or discomfort.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 52

src.question: The parent of a child with a single asymptomatic granuloma annulare ring asks whether treatment is needed. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: It is benign and self-limiting, with about half resolving within two years, so treatment is for cosmesis or discomfort
src.explanation: and there is no malignant potential.

items.section_title: 6.2 · Objective b — The dermatophytes, by body site
items.html: Pustular beard eruption with firmly anchored hairs. Bacterial culture helps separate it from tinea barbae by ruling out bacterial folliculitis.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 21

src.question: A man with a pustular beard eruption has hairs that are firmly anchored and do not pull out easily. Which test helps separate this from tinea barbae?
src.key: Bacterial culture
src.explanation: Correct — used to rule out bacterial folliculitis.

items.section_title: 8.1 · Objective a — Ephelides, lentigines and solar lentigo
items.html: Solar lentigo versus lentigo maligna. Solar lentigo has uniform pigmentation, whereas lentigo maligna is asymmetric with irregular border and color; dermoscopy is essential, and solar lentigo shows finger-like projections and a moth-eaten border.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 111

src.question: What distinguishes solar lentigo from lentigo maligna?
src.key: Solar lentigo has uniform pigmentation; lentigo maligna is asymmetric with irregular border and color
src.explanation: and dermoscopy is essential — solar lentigo shows finger-like projections and a moth-eaten border.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Seborrheic dermatitis treatment. The mainstay is topical antifungals such as ketoconazole, with steroids used early to reduce inflammation; scalp disease uses ketoconazole or selenium sulfide shampoo, and facial disease uses ketoconazole cream or lotion.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 95

src.question: What is the mainstay of treatment for seborrheic dermatitis?
src.key: Topical antifungals such as ketoconazole, with steroids used early to reduce inflammation
src.explanation: Scalp disease uses ketoconazole or selenium sulfide shampoo; facial disease uses ketoconazole cream or lotion.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective c — Alopecia
items.html: Female-pattern hair loss treatment. Options are limited; oral antiandrogens such as combined oral contraceptives may be considered, and finasteride is not indicated in women.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 148

src.question: A 48-year-old woman has diffuse thinning over the central and parietal scalp with her frontal hairline preserved. Which is the most appropriate treatment consideration?
src.key: Oral antiandrogens such as combined oral contraceptives may be considered, since treatment options are limited
src.explanation: Correct — female-pattern hair loss has fewer options, and finasteride is not indicated in women.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Pyoderma gangrenosum. Despite its name, it is a neutrophilic dermatosis that is not infectious; dysregulated innate immune activation with neutrophil recruitment causes the tissue destruction.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 57

src.question: What is pyoderma gangrenosum, despite its name?
src.key: A neutrophilic dermatosis that is not infectious
src.explanation: Correct — dysregulated innate immune activation with neutrophil recruitment causes the tissue destruction.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Scaling. It is accumulation of loose or adherent cornified fragments of the epidermis, typically gray or white; lichenification is thickening and hardening of the skin.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 18

src.question: How is scaling described?
src.key: Accumulation of loose or adherent cornified fragments of the epidermis, typically gray or white

also.key: Lichenification and scaling, respectively
also.explanation: Lichenification is thickening and hardening of the skin, and scaling is accumulation of loose or adherent cornified fragments of the epidermis, typically gray or white.

items.section_title: 9.5 · Objective 1 — Malignant melanoma
items.html: Stage IV melanoma. It is defined by any T, any N, with M1, meaning distant metastasis is present whatever the primary or nodal status; M1 alone determines it.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 54

src.question: What defines stage IV melanoma in the staging overview?
src.key: Any T, any N, with M1 — that is, distant metastasis present whatever the primary or nodal status
src.explanation: Correct — M1 alone determines it.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Bulla. A fluid-filled lesion greater than one centimeter is called a bulla; a vesicle is the same lesion up to one centimeter.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 14

src.question: A fluid-filled lesion greater than one centimeter is called what?
src.key: A bulla
src.explanation: Correct — a vesicle is the same lesion up to one centimeter.

items.section_title: 8.5 · Objective b — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Light or laser treatment of freckles. Patients should expect that lesions can relapse, so treatment is not necessarily permanent.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 7

src.question: A 26-year-old woman is booked for intense pulsed light treatment of her freckles. What must she be told to expect?
src.key: The lesions can relapse, so this is not necessarily permanent
src.explanation: Correct — lesions can relapse after light or laser treatment.

items.section_title: 8.1 · Objective a — Ephelides, lentigines and solar lentigo
items.html: Solar lentigines. The lesions themselves are benign, but they mark cumulative sun damage that is also associated with actinic keratosis, squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma and melanoma.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 13

src.question: A 70-year-old woman with numerous solar lentigines asks what her lesions mean for her health. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: The lesions themselves are benign, but they mark sun damage that is also associated with actinic keratosis and skin cancers
src.explanation: Correct — the association includes squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma and melanoma.

also.key: Actinic keratosis, squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma and melanoma
also.explanation: Correct — the lesion itself is benign but marks cumulative sun damage.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Cellulitis without diagnostic workup. It can be managed this way when involvement is limited, pain is minimal, there are no systemic signs and no risk factor for serious illness; serious infections warrant blood cultures, punch biopsy, blood count and creatine phosphokinase.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 109

src.question: When can cellulitis be managed without any diagnostic workup?
src.key: Limited area of involvement, minimal pain, no systemic signs and no risk factor for serious illness
src.explanation: Serious infections warrant blood cultures, punch biopsy, blood count and creatine phosphokinase.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Pityriasis rosea course. It is self-limited and typically fades over 4 to 6 weeks, though darker skin may show post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation for several months; reassurance is the mainstay, with antihistamines or topical steroids used cautiously for itch.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 171

src.question: A 21-year-old man with pityriasis rosea asks what to expect. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: It is self-limited and typically fades over 4 to 6 weeks, though darker skin may show post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation for several months
src.explanation: Correct — reassurance is the mainstay, with antihistamines or topical steroids used cautiously for itch.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Pyoderma gangrenosum in inflammatory bowel disease. Infliximab at 5 mg/kg intravenously is the biologic of choice and is approved for pyoderma gangrenosum in inflammatory bowel disease.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 60

src.question: A 39-year-old woman with Crohn's disease has biopsy-supported pyoderma gangrenosum that continues to enlarge on high-dose prednisone. Which is the most appropriate next treatment?
src.key: Infliximab at 5 mg/kg intravenously
src.explanation: Correct — it is approved for pyoderma gangrenosum in inflammatory bowel disease and is the biologic of choice.

items.section_title: 6.2 · Objective b — The dermatophytes, by body site
items.html: Safety steps before systemic antifungals for tinea capitis. Review drug interactions and hepatic disease, and obtain baseline liver tests when indicated by the agent, its labeling, and patient risk; baseline testing is indication-driven, not automatic.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 15

src.question: You are about to prescribe a systemic antifungal for an 8-year-old with confirmed tinea capitis. Which safety step comes before the first dose?
src.key: Review drug interactions and hepatic disease, and obtain baseline liver tests when indicated by the agent, its labeling, and patient risk
src.explanation: Correct — baseline testing is indication-driven, not automatic.

items.section_title: 5.4 · Objective a — Spider bites
items.html: Tarantula hair in the eye. It needs urgent ophthalmology referral, since embedded hairs can cause corneal granuloma; topical corticosteroid addresses only the cutaneous reaction.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 66

src.question: A 25-year-old woman handling her pet tarantula developed a red painful eye an hour later and now has blurred vision. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Urgent ophthalmology referral, since embedded hairs can cause corneal granuloma
src.explanation: Correct — topical corticosteroid addresses only the cutaneous reaction.

items.section_title: 5.6 · Objectives b & c — Primary versus secondary lesions, and care across the age range
items.html: Household measures after head lice. Put clothing and bedding from the past week in the dryer or bag it for two weeks, wash combs and vacuum; fumigation is specifically not recommended.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 30

src.question: A 6-year-old girl has been treated for head lice and her mother asks what to do about the house. Which is the most appropriate advice?
src.key: Put clothing and bedding from the past week in the dryer or bag it for two weeks, wash combs and vacuum
src.explanation: Correct — fumigation is specifically not recommended.

items.section_title: 5.3 · Objective a — Cutaneous larva migrans and cercarial dermatitis
items.html: Cercarial dermatitis treatment. Treat symptomatically with antihistamines, oatmeal baths, antipruritic lotions, aspirin for pain and topical or oral glucocorticoids; proper washing and hygiene are also advised.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 91

src.question: A 16-year-old girl with cercarial dermatitis has pain and swelling with the itch, worst about two days after exposure. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
src.key: Antihistamines, oatmeal baths, antipruritic lotions, aspirin for pain and topical or oral glucocorticoids
src.explanation: Correct — the pain and swelling peak at 48 to 72 hours before settling.

also.key: Symptomatically, with antihistamines, oatmeal baths, antipruritic lotions, aspirin for pain and topical or oral glucocorticoids
also.explanation: Correct — proper washing and hygiene are also advised.

items.section_title: 8.1 · Objective a — Ephelides, lentigines and solar lentigo
items.html: Lentigines. They are well-circumscribed round to oval uniformly black or brown macules under 5 mm, on skin, conjunctiva and mucocutaneous surfaces, occurring on both sun-exposed and sun-protected areas.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 10

src.question: Describe the clinical appearance of lentigines and where they occur.
src.key: Well-circumscribed round to oval uniformly black or brown macules under 5 mm, on skin, conjunctiva and mucocutaneous surfaces
src.explanation: Correct — they occur on both sun-exposed and sun-protected areas.

items.section_title: 2.3 · Objective c — Vesiculobullous disease
items.html: Prodromal bullous pemphigoid. Weeks of intense itching with pruritic urticarial or edematous lesions and no blisters may be the prodromal phase, which may precede bullae by weeks to months.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 123

src.question: An 82-year-old woman has had several weeks of intense itching with urticarial plaques but no blisters. She is otherwise well. Which is the most likely explanation?
src.key: The prodromal phase of bullous pemphigoid, which may precede bullae by weeks to months
src.explanation: Correct — the prodrome presents as pruritic urticarial or edematous lesions before the blistering phase.

items.section_title: 6.3 · Objective b — Nails, distant reactions, and steroid-altered tinea
items.html: Confirming thickened discolored toenails. Use potassium hydroxide microscopy, periodic acid-Schiff stain of clippings, culture, or amplification testing; sample subungual debris after trimming the onycholytic nail, from the most proximal accessible diseased nail bed.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 51

src.question: A 64-year-old has thickened discolored toenails and you decide to confirm the diagnosis before prescribing. Which tests apply, and how should the sample be taken?
src.key: Potassium hydroxide microscopy, periodic acid–Schiff stain of clippings, culture, or amplification testing; sample the most proximal accessible diseased nail bed
src.explanation: Correct — sample subungual debris after trimming the onycholytic nail. Sampling proximally is the part most often missed.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Ocular rosacea. Ocular rosacea with keratitis, visual symptoms or corneal involvement needs urgent ophthalmology referral for slit-lamp examination, since untreated disease risks corneal scarring.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 70

src.question: Which rosacea complication requires urgent ophthalmology referral?
src.key: Ocular rosacea with keratitis, visual symptoms or corneal involvement
src.explanation: Correct — untreated ocular disease risks corneal scarring.

also.key: Urgent ophthalmology referral for slit-lamp examination
also.explanation: Correct — ocular rosacea with visual symptoms risks corneal scarring if untreated.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Rapidly expanding ulcer before treating as pyoderma gangrenosum. Malignancy and infection must be excluded because the diagnosis is one of exclusion and the immunosuppression used would worsen an infection.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 59

src.question: Why must malignancy and infection be excluded in a rapidly expanding ulcer before treating it as pyoderma gangrenosum?
src.key: Because the diagnosis is one of exclusion and the immunosuppression used would worsen an infection
src.explanation: Correct — the question to answer is why this ulcer is suddenly expanding.

items.section_title: 2.6 · Common dermatologic pharmacology
items.html: Psoriasis comorbidities. Patients are at increased risk of cardiovascular events, type 2 diabetes mellitus, metabolic syndrome and lymphoma; psoriasis is a systemic inflammatory disease, not only a skin condition.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 155

src.question: Which comorbidities are patients with psoriasis at increased risk of?
src.key: Cardiovascular events, type 2 diabetes mellitus, metabolic syndrome and lymphoma
src.explanation: Correct — psoriasis is a systemic inflammatory disease, not only a skin condition.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Stasis dermatitis priorities. The two primary clinical priorities are distinguishing it from cellulitis, and determining whether compression therapy can be used safely.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 112

src.question: What are the two primary clinical priorities in stasis dermatitis?
src.key: Distinguishing it from cellulitis, and determining whether compression therapy can be used safely
src.explanation: Correct — both are named as the priorities.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Granuloma annulare variants. The generalized or disseminated variant carries the strongest systemic associations: diabetes, thyroid disease, dyslipidemia and lymphoma. It is more common in adults over forty.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 50

src.question: Which variant of granuloma annulare carries the strongest systemic associations?
src.key: Generalized or disseminated, associated with diabetes, thyroid disease, dyslipidemia and lymphoma
src.explanation: and it is more common in adults over forty.

items.section_title: 6.4 · Objective b — The yeasts: candidal intertrigo and pityriasis versicolor
items.html: Vitiligo versus pityriasis versicolor. Vitiligo is completely white (depigmented) and autoimmune, whereas pityriasis versicolor is hypopigmented rather than depigmented, and it scales.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 79

src.question: How does vitiligo differ from pityriasis versicolor?
src.key: Vitiligo is completely white — depigmented — and is an autoimmune disorder
src.explanation: Correct — pityriasis versicolor is hypopigmented rather than depigmented, and it scales.

items.section_title: 6.2 · Objective b — The dermatophytes, by body site
items.html: Allylamine antifungals. They destroy the fungal cell membrane, which prevents growth and ultimately kills the fungus. Names end in -fine, such as terbinafine and naftifine.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 5

src.question: How does the allylamine class of antifungals work, and how do you recognize one by name?
src.key: It destroys the fungal cell membrane; the names end in -fine
src.explanation: Correct — terbinafine and naftifine. Destroying the membrane prevents growth and ultimately kills the fungus.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Hot tub folliculitis management. Reassure, since most cases clear in two to ten days, and use dilute acetic acid compresses: 3 tablespoons of 5% vinegar in a pint of water, for 20 minutes, two to four times daily.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 52

src.question: A 31-year-old man has hot tub folliculitis over the trunk. He is systemically well and the rash began four days ago. Which is the most appropriate management?
src.key: Reassurance with dilute acetic acid compresses, since most clear in two to ten days
src.explanation: Correct — 3 tablespoons of 5% vinegar in a pint of water, 20 minutes, two to four times daily.

items.section_title: 4.1 · Objective a — Acne vulgaris
items.html: Acne pointing to polycystic ovarian syndrome. In a woman with persistent acne, hirsutism together with irregular or absent menses points toward polycystic ovarian syndrome, indicating androgen hypersecretion.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 17

src.question: Which finding in a woman with persistent acne points toward polycystic ovarian syndrome?
src.key: Hirsutism together with irregular or absent menses
src.explanation: That combination indicates androgen hypersecretion.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Endoscopic thoracic sympathectomy risk. The principal risk is compensatory sweating elsewhere, occurring in over 30%. The procedure is permanent, so the trade-off must be discussed thoroughly beforehand.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 75

src.question: What is the principal risk a patient must understand before endoscopic thoracic sympathectomy?
src.key: Compensatory sweating elsewhere, occurring in over 30%
src.explanation: Correct — the procedure is permanent, so the trade-off has to be discussed thoroughly beforehand.

items.section_title: 8.5 · Objective b — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Freckles management. Manage with sun protection, patient education and topical depigmenting agents; cryotherapy is not used because of the size of the lesions. Laser or intense pulsed light is preferred, but the lesions can relapse.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 7

src.question: A 24-year-old with red hair and widespread freckling across her nose and cheeks asks what can be done about them. Which management is appropriate, and which must be avoided?
src.key: Sun protection, patient education and topical depigmenting agents; cryotherapy is NOT used
src.explanation: Correct — cryotherapy is difficult because of the size of the lesions, so intense pulsed light or lasers are preferred.

also.key: Laser and intense pulsed light are preferred over cryotherapy, but the lesions can relapse
also.explanation: Correct — sun protection and education remain the foundation of management.

items.section_title: 4.3 · Objective a — Impetigo, erysipelas, cellulitis and abscess
items.html: Cultures in impetigo. Obtain cultures when the patient is at high risk for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (for example a health-care worker or teacher) or when post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis is present.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 93

src.question: When should cultures be obtained in impetigo?
src.key: When the patient is at high risk for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, or when post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis is present
src.explanation: Correct — impetigo is cultured when the patient is at high risk for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, such as a health-care worker or teacher, or has post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.

items.section_title: 6.7 · Objective b — Molluscum contagiosum and warts
items.html: Treating cutaneous warts. No therapy eradicates human papillomavirus with certainty, and recurrence can occur. Choose treatment by location, symptoms, age, pregnancy status, immune status, and risk of scarring or dyspigmentation, avoiding excessive freezing or destruction.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 149

src.question: A 25-year-old woman with several common warts on the hands asks whether treatment will get rid of the virus for good. What treatment principle applies to all cutaneous warts?
src.key: No therapy eradicates the virus; recurrence happens
src.explanation: No therapy eradicates human papillomavirus with certainty and recurrence can occur. Treatment is chosen according to location, symptoms, age, pregnancy status, immune status, and the risk of scarring or dyspigmentation, avoiding excessive freezing or destruction.

items.section_title: 1.6 · Objective g — Discuss the implications for treatment
items.html: Treating despite diagnostic uncertainty. The value of treatment versus no treatment is a linear function of the probability of disease, together with the likelihood of success and the ability to tolerate treatment, weighed as risk against benefit.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 27

src.question: A 67-year-old woman has a probable but unconfirmed diagnosis, and a treatment with meaningful adverse effects is being considered. What factors govern the decision to treat when the diagnosis carries some uncertainty?
src.key: Probability, success, tolerance, risk-benefit
src.explanation: The value of treatment versus no treatment is a linear function of the probability of disease, together with the likelihood of success and the ability to tolerate treatment, weighed as risk against benefit.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Demodex-associated papulopustular rosacea. Ivermectin 1 percent cream is described as superior to metronidazole, reflecting the contribution of Demodex folliculorum mite overgrowth to the pathogenesis.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 69

src.question: A 48-year-old woman with papulopustular rosacea has Demodex-associated disease that has not responded to topical metronidazole. What topical agent is described as superior for this situation?
src.key: Ivermectin 1 percent cream
src.explanation: Ivermectin 1 percent cream is described as superior to metronidazole for Demodex-associated papulopustular rosacea, reflecting the contribution of Demodex folliculorum mite overgrowth to the pathogenesis.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Irritant versus candidal diaper rash. Fold involvement separates them: irritant disease affects convex surfaces and generally spares the inguinal folds, while candidal disease gives beefy erythema in the folds with satellite papules and pustules.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 107

src.question: A 9-month-old boy is brought in for a diaper rash of one week. Examination shows beefy erythema involving the inguinal folds, with peripheral scale and several small papules and pustules on the thighs a short distance beyond the main area of redness. He completed a course of amoxicillin two weeks ago. What finding most strongly indicates the infectious complication rather than simple irritant disease?
src.key: Fold involvement with satellites
src.explanation: Whether the skin folds are involved is the finding that distinguishes irritant from candidal disease. Irritant diaper dermatitis affects the convex surfaces and generally spares the inguinal folds because they are less exposed to urine and feces; candidal disease produces beefy erythema in the folds with satellite papules and pustules.

items.section_title: 3.3 · Objective a — Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
items.html: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome. It spares the mucosa and is toxin-mediated, which separates it from Stevens-Johnson syndrome on the differential.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 82

src.question: A 3-year-old boy presents with widespread superficial skin peeling and a positive Nikolsky sign but entirely normal mucous membranes. What diagnosis does the preserved mucosa most suggest?
src.key: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
src.explanation: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome spares the mucosa and is toxin-mediated, which is exactly how it is separated from Stevens-Johnson syndrome on the differential.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Von Zumbusch pustular psoriasis. A rare, severe, abrupt and life-threatening form associated with other forms of psoriasis; it may follow systemic steroid withdrawal, begins with several days of fever, and is commonly mistaken for bacterial or viral infection.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 160

src.question: A 44-year-old woman with a history of plaque psoriasis was given a two-week course of oral prednisone by an urgent care clinician for back pain. Four days after finishing it she develops fever lasting several days followed by the sudden appearance of widespread sheets of small pustules on erythematous skin. She appears unwell. What has most likely occurred?
src.key: Pustular psoriasis precipitated by systemic steroid withdrawal
src.explanation: Pustular psoriasis of von Zumbusch type is a rare, severe form associated with other forms of psoriasis and may follow systemic steroid withdrawal. It is abrupt and life-threatening, begins with several days of fever, and is commonly mistaken for bacterial or viral infection.

also.key: Recognize this as pustular psoriasis of the Von Zumbusch type and treat it as a life-threatening emergency
also.explanation: Correct — it is abrupt and life-threatening, may follow systemic steroid withdrawal, and is commonly mistaken for bacterial or viral infection.

items.section_title: 6.2 · Objective b — The dermatophytes, by body site
items.html: Tinea capitis and school. School exclusion is generally unnecessary once effective treatment has started. Avoid sharing personal hair items and clean clippers, combs, brushes, bedding and hats; household contacts may use a sporicidal shampoo.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 17

src.question: A 7-year-old girl is being treated for tinea capitis and her school has asked whether she must stay at home. What advice about school attendance and household measures is correct?
src.key: No exclusion once treated; do not share hair items
