src.explanation: School exclusion is generally unnecessary once effective treatment has started. Patients should avoid sharing personal hair items and should clean clippers, combs, brushes, bedding, and hats, and household contacts may use a sporicidal shampoo.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Urticaria mechanism. Mast cell degranulation releases histamine, prostaglandins and leukotrienes, causing transient dermal edema. Immunoglobulin E mediated immunologic triggers include shellfish, nuts, eggs, penicillin and insect stings.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 36

src.question: A 27-year-old man develops widespread wheals within 20 minutes of eating shellfish. What mechanism underlies this reaction, and what class of trigger does it represent?
src.key: Immunoglobulin E mediated, an immunologic trigger
src.explanation: Urticaria results from mast cell degranulation releasing histamine, prostaglandins, and leukotrienes, producing transient dermal edema. Immunologic immunoglobulin E mediated triggers include foods such as shellfish, nuts, and eggs, drugs including penicillin, and insect stings.

items.section_title: 6.2 · Objective b — The dermatophytes, by body site
items.html: Allylamine class. Terbinafine is an allylamine, a class that destroys fungal cell membranes; members end in -fine (terbinafine, naftifine). Imidazoles instead block synthesis of ergosterol, a vital component of the fungal cell membrane.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 5

src.question: A 24-year-old man has tinea corporis, and the clinician wants an antifungal that works by destroying the fungal cell membrane rather than by blocking ergosterol synthesis. Which agent belongs to that class, and how is the class recognized by name?
src.key: Terbinafine, an allylamine, recognizable by the ending -fine
src.explanation: The allylamine class works by destroying the cell membranes of fungi, preventing growth and ultimately killing them, and its members end in -fine: terbinafine and naftifine. Imidazoles instead block synthesis of ergosterol, a vital component of the fungal cell membrane.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Velvety hyperpigmented plaques of the neck and axillae. Primary management is treating the underlying cause through weight loss and glycemic control, discontinuing any offending drug. Metformin reduces insulin resistance and may improve the skin findings.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 25

src.question: A 34-year-old woman with obesity, type 2 diabetes, and polycystic ovary syndrome has velvety hyperpigmented plaques of the neck and axillae. What is the primary management?
src.key: Weight loss and glycemic control
src.explanation: Primary management is treating the underlying cause through weight loss and glycemic control, discontinuing any offending drug. Metformin reduces insulin resistance and may improve the skin findings.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Ulceration versus erosion. Ulceration is full-thickness skin loss extending to the dermis or deeper, whereas erosion is partial loss of only the epidermis. Depth is the entire distinction.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 17

src.question: A 71-year-old woman has a sacral wound showing full-thickness loss of skin extending into the dermis, and a second area on the heel showing partial loss involving only the epidermis. What are these two findings called?
src.key: Ulceration and erosion, respectively
src.explanation: Ulceration is full-thickness loss of the skin extending to the dermis or deeper, whereas erosion is partial loss of the skin of only the epidermis. Depth is the entire distinction.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Impetigo herpetiformis. The psoriasis of pregnancy, typically in the third trimester, with erythematous patches whose margins are studded with subcorneal pustules. Onset brings fever, chills, malaise, diarrhea, nausea and arthralgia.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 161

src.question: A 30-year-old woman in her third trimester develops erythematous patches whose margins are studded with small pustules, accompanied by fever, chills, malaise, diarrhea, nausea, and joint pains. What is the most likely diagnosis?
src.key: Impetigo herpetiformis
src.explanation: Impetigo herpetiformis is the psoriasis of pregnancy, occurring typically in the third trimester with erythematous patches whose margins are studded with subcorneal pustules. Onset is accompanied by fever, chills, malaise, diarrhea, nausea, and arthralgia.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Recurrent folliculitis. Recurrent or recalcitrant folliculitis raises the Staphylococcus aureus carrier state, treated with mupirocin ointment to the nares. Nasal swabs of the patient and family members evaluate carriage.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 46

src.question: A 31-year-old man has folliculitis that has recurred repeatedly despite topical treatment, and cultures grow Staphylococcus aureus each time. What additional measure addresses the likely reservoir?
src.key: Mupirocin to the nares for the carrier state
src.explanation: Recurrent or recalcitrant folliculitis raises the Staphylococcus aureus carrier state, and mupirocin ointment is used for it. Nasal swabs of the patient and family members are taken to evaluate carriage.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Common acquired melanocytic nevi. They are usually under 6 mm, homogeneous in surface and color, round to oval with sharp demarcation. A very dark brown or black lesion on a light-skinned individual is suspicious and warrants evaluation.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 36

src.question: A 32-year-old fair-skinned woman has numerous moles under 6 mm with homogeneous surface and color. One lesion is very dark brown to black. What is the significance of that lesion?
src.key: It is suspicious and warrants evaluation
src.explanation: Common acquired melanocytic naevi are usually less than 6 mm with homogeneous surface and color, round to oval with sharp demarcation. A very dark brown or black lesion on a light-skinned individual is specifically flagged as suspicious.

items.section_title: 9.1 · Objective 1 — Describe before you name
items.html: Describe before naming. Evaluate any premalignant or malignant lesion by first characterizing it: primary lesion type, color, surface texture, border definition, size, distribution, palpability, ulceration and bleeding, before assigning a diagnosis.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 4

src.question: A 63-year-old man presents with a lesion on the temple that he is unable to describe, and the clinician has not yet formed an impression. What is the recommended first step when evaluating any premalignant or malignant cutaneous lesion?
src.key: Characterize the lesion before naming it
src.explanation: The foundational approach is to describe before naming: characterize each lesion systematically by primary lesion type, color, surface texture, border definition, size, distribution, palpability, ulceration, and bleeding before assigning a diagnosis.

items.section_title: 6.4 · Objective b — The yeasts: candidal intertrigo and pityriasis versicolor
items.html: Candidal intertrigo. It produces well-demarcated erythematous patches in warm moist folds, with satellite papules and pustules beyond the main area; pruritus with burning pain is typical.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 71

src.question: A 63-year-old woman with obesity has a burning rash under both breasts. Examination shows well-demarcated beefy erythematous patches in the folds with peripheral scale and several small papules and pustules on adjacent skin just beyond the main area of redness. What is the most likely diagnosis?
src.key: Cutaneous candidiasis
src.explanation: Candidal intertrigo produces well-demarcated erythematous patches in warm moist folds with satellite papules and pustules beyond the main area, and pruritus with burning pain is typical.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: Infantile hemangioma growth. Rapid proliferation is followed by slower involution, with rapid growth in the neonatal period and most growth in the first 4 to 6 months. The earliest sign is blanching, then fine telangiectasias, then a red macule.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 66

src.question: A 3-week-old infant, born prematurely, has a bright red papule on the scalp that was a faint blanched area with fine telangiectasias at birth and has grown noticeably in the past fortnight. What growth pattern should the parents be told to expect?
src.key: Rapid growth, then slow involution
src.explanation: Infantile hemangiomas have a unique growth pattern of rapid proliferation followed by slower involution, with rapid growth during the neonatal period and most growth in the first 4 to 6 months. The earliest sign is blanching of the involved skin followed by fine telangiectasias and then a red macule.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Tinea corporis versus nummular eczema. Both are red or pink itchy circular patches. Tinea corporis is a fungal infection that is annular and clears centrally; nummular eczema is non-infectious and coin-shaped without central clearing.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 27

src.question: A 45-year-old man has red, itchy, circular patches on the forearm, and the clinician is distinguishing tinea corporis from nummular eczema. What is the distinguishing feature?
src.key: Tinea corporis clears centrally; eczema does not
src.explanation: Both present as red or pink itchy circular patches. Tinea corporis is a fungal infection with an annular appearance, whereas nummular eczema is non-infectious and coin-shaped without central clearing.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Objective d — Discuss clinical principles and decision-making
items.html: VINDICATE mnemonic. A category-based differential framework: vascular, infectious, neoplastic, degenerative, iatrogenic, congenital, autoimmune, trauma, and endocrine or metabolic.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 16

src.question: A student uses the VINDICATE mnemonic to build a differential for a 72-year-old man brought to the emergency department with confusion. What do the letters stand for?
src.key: Vascular, infectious, neoplastic, degenerative, iatrogenic, congenital, autoimmune, trauma, endocrine
src.explanation: VINDICATE is a category-based framework: vascular, infectious, neoplastic, degenerative, iatrogenic, congenital, autoimmune, trauma, and endocrine or metabolic. Applied to confusion it yields stroke, meningitis, brain tumor, Alzheimer disease, and so on.

items.section_title: 4.3 · Objective a — Impetigo, erysipelas, cellulitis and abscess
items.html: Erysipelas work-up. In a classic presentation it is a clinical diagnosis. Leukocytosis and raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein are common, but blood and tissue cultures are not cost effective (extremely low yield) and imaging is not indicated.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 103

src.question: A 59-year-old woman has a classic presentation of erysipelas with a sharply demarcated raised plaque of the shin and a fever of 39 degrees Celsius. What laboratory and imaging approach is appropriate?
src.key: Clinical; cultures and imaging add little
src.explanation: Erysipelas is a clinical diagnosis in a classic presentation. Leukocytosis and raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein are common, but blood and tissue cultures are not cost effective because of extremely low organism yield, and imaging studies are of low yield and not indicated.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Objective d — Discuss clinical principles and decision-making
items.html: Common things occur commonly. Bet on uncommon manifestations of common conditions rather than common manifestations of uncommon conditions: when you hear hoof beats, think horses, not zebras. An unusual presentation of a common condition is more probable than a textbook presentation of a rare one.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 25

src.question: A student proposes a rare diagnosis to explain a very typical presentation in a 30-year-old woman. What does the principle 'place your bets on uncommon manifestations of common conditions rather than common manifestations of uncommon conditions' mean in practice?
src.key: An atypical presentation of a common disease is likelier
src.explanation: Common things occur commonly — when you hear hoof beats think of horses, not zebras. An unusual presentation of a common condition is more probable than a textbook presentation of something rare.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Psoriasis heredity. About 8 percent of children are affected when one parent has psoriasis and 41 percent when both do, reflecting a genetic predisposition in which PSORS1 is the major susceptibility locus.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 155

src.question: A 29-year-old woman and her 31-year-old husband both have plaque psoriasis and ask about the likelihood their future children will be affected. What is the most accurate counseling?
src.key: About 41 percent of their children
src.explanation: The figures given are 8 percent when one parent has psoriasis and 41 percent when both do, reflecting a genetic predisposition in which PSORS1 is the major susceptibility locus.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Purpura. Non-blanching blood deposits of 4 mm or more are purpura, a medical emergency until proven otherwise; with fever in a child it demands immediate evaluation.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 15

src.question: A 6-year-old boy is brought in with fever and a rash. Examination shows non-blanching deposits of blood in the skin, several measuring 6 mm across. What is the most appropriate interpretation of this finding?
src.key: Purpura, an emergency until proven otherwise
src.explanation: Blood deposits of 4 mm or more are purpura, which is a medical emergency until proven otherwise; with fever in a child it demands immediate evaluation.

items.section_title: 4.1 · Objective a — Acne vulgaris
items.html: Acne mechanica. Pressure on the skin occludes the pilosebaceous follicle; shoulder pads, orthopedic casts and helmets are the named examples.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 9

src.question: A 16-year-old football player develops acne confined to the shoulders and upper back under his pads. What predisposing factor does this represent?
src.key: Acne mechanica from pressure on the follicle
src.explanation: Acne mechanica results from pressure on the skin — shoulder pads, orthopedic casts, and helmets are the named examples — occluding the pilosebaceous follicle.

also.key: Acne mechanica, where pressure occludes the pilosebaceous follicles
also.explanation: Correct — shoulder pads, orthopedic casts and helmets are the named examples.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: Nevus araneus. A central arteriole with radiating capillaries, caused by dilation of pre-existing vessels with no vascular proliferation. Estrogen excess may be the cause; ask about pregnancies, hormone use, alcohol and medications high-risk for liver damage.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 89

src.question: A 27-year-old pregnant woman has several lesions on the upper trunk consisting of a central arteriole with radiating capillaries. What is the mechanism, and what should be asked in the history?
src.key: Dilated existing vessels; ask about estrogen and alcohol
src.explanation: Nevus araneus involves no vascular proliferation and is due to dilation of pre-existing vessels. Estrogen excess states may be the cause, and lesions resolve after delivery or cessation of hormonal contraception. History should cover pregnancies, hormone use, alcohol, and high-risk medications for liver damage.

items.section_title: 3.3 · Objective a — Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
items.html: Ocular rosacea. Keratitis, visual symptoms or corneal involvement warrants urgent ophthalmology referral; visual symptoms and photophobia raise exactly those concerns.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 70

src.question: A 51-year-old woman with known rosacea reports a gritty foreign-body sensation, blurred vision, and photophobia. What is the most appropriate action?
src.key: Urgent ophthalmology referral
src.explanation: Ocular rosacea with keratitis, visual symptoms, or corneal involvement warrants urgent ophthalmology referral. Visual symptoms and photophobia raise exactly those concerns.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective c — Alopecia
items.html: Female-pattern hair loss. It produces diffuse thinning of the central and parietal scalp without significant change to the frontal hairline, with increased frequency of balding among first-degree male relatives.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 146

src.question: A 46-year-old woman reports gradual hair thinning over several years. Examination shows diffuse thinning across the central and parietal scalp with preservation of the frontal hairline. There are no bald patches, no scaling, no scarring, and no exclamation point hairs. Several of her male relatives began balding in their twenties. What is the most likely diagnosis?
src.key: Female-pattern hair loss
src.explanation: Female-pattern hair loss produces diffuse thinning of the central and parietal scalp without significant change to the frontal hairline. There is an increased frequency of balding among first-degree male relatives, which the family history here supplies.

items.section_title: 8.1 · Objective a — Ephelides, lentigines and solar lentigo
items.html: Lentigo maligna. Melanoma in situ that is asymmetric with irregular border and color and darker areas; dermoscopy is essential. A solar lentigo that has diverged from its uniform neighbors requires that evaluation.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 111

src.question: A 62-year-old woman has several uniformly tan-brown macules on the dorsal hands and face that have appeared gradually over years. One lesion is larger, asymmetric, and has irregular borders with darker areas within it. What should be done about that lesion?
src.key: Evaluate it with dermoscopy for lentigo maligna
src.explanation: Lentigo maligna, which is melanoma in situ, is asymmetric with irregular border and color and darker areas, and dermoscopy is described as essential. A solar lentigo that has diverged from its uniform neighbors requires that evaluation.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Mycosis fungoides. It may resemble psoriasis, eczema or tinea; the discriminators are chronicity, treatment resistance, and large or oddly distributed lesions. Early patches or scaly plaques are usually on the trunk, frequently greater than 5 cm.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 74

src.question: A 61-year-old man has had erythematous scaly patches and plaques on the trunk for four years, several larger than 5 cm, that have been treated as psoriasis and eczema without lasting response. Pruritus is prominent. What features discriminate this from the inflammatory conditions it resembles?
src.key: Chronicity, treatment resistance, odd sites
src.explanation: Mycosis fungoides may resemble psoriasis, eczema, or tinea, and the discriminators are chronicity, treatment resistance, and large or oddly distributed lesions. Early morphology is localized or generalized erythematous patches or scaly plaques, usually on the trunk, frequently greater than 5 cm.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Cellulitis work-up. Cellulitis is usually a clinical diagnosis; no work-up is needed with a limited area of involvement, minimal pain, no systemic signs, and no risk factor for serious illness such as extremes of age or immunocompromise.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 109

src.question: A 45-year-old man has a small area of cellulitis of the forearm with minimal pain, no systemic signs, and no comorbidity. In which patient with cellulitis is no diagnostic workup required?
src.key: Limited area, no systemic signs
src.explanation: Cellulitis is usually a clinical diagnosis, and no workup is needed when there is a limited area of involvement, minimal pain, no systemic signs, and no risk factor for serious illness such as extremes of age or immunocompromise.

items.section_title: 3.3 · Objective a — Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
items.html: Stevens-Johnson syndrome versus toxic epidermal necrolysis. They lie on one spectrum separated by body surface area involved: Stevens-Johnson syndrome has less than 10 percent detachment, toxic epidermal necrolysis more than 30 percent.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 88

src.question: A 55-year-old man is admitted with widespread painful erythema progressing to flaccid bullae and confluent epidermal detachment of about 40 percent of the body surface area, with a positive Nikolsky sign and severe mucosal erosions. What distinguishes this from Stevens-Johnson syndrome?
src.key: Detachment over 30 percent
src.explanation: The two conditions sit on one spectrum and are separated by the percentage of body surface area involved: Stevens-Johnson syndrome has less than 10 percent detachment, and toxic epidermal necrolysis has more than 30 percent, with mortality up to 30 to 35 percent.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Potassium hydroxide wet preparation. It detects fungal elements in skin, hair or nail samples and is the appropriate bedside confirmation before treating a suspected dermatophyte infection.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 28

src.question: A 34-year-old man presents with an itchy, scaling annular plaque on the trunk. The clinician wishes to confirm the presence of fungal elements at the bedside before starting treatment. What is the most appropriate test?
src.key: Potassium hydroxide wet preparation
src.explanation: A potassium hydroxide wet preparation detects fungal elements in skin, hair, or nail samples, and it is the appropriate bedside confirmation before treating a suspected dermatophyte infection.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Pseudomonas folliculitis. It is usually self-limiting, and most cases resolve without specific treatment in 2 to 10 days. A wet dressing of 5 percent acetic acid for 20 minutes, 2 to 4 times daily, may relieve symptoms.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 52

src.question: A 31-year-old woman develops an itchy pustular eruption two days after using a hotel hot tub. Examination shows follicular papules and pustules over the trunk, buttocks, and proximal limbs, sparing the face, neck, palms, and soles. She is afebrile. What is the most appropriate management?
src.key: Reassurance; most resolve in 2 to 10 days
src.explanation: Pseudomonas folliculitis is usually self-limiting and most cases resolve without specific treatment, clearing in 2 to 10 days. A wet dressing of 5 percent acetic acid may be applied for 20 minutes 2 to 4 times daily for symptom relief.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Poorly demarcated. A poorly demarcated lesion has an irregular or blotchy appearance without well-defined borders, in contrast to a well-demarcated lesion, which has clearly defined borders.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 20

src.question: A 38-year-old man has a blotchy eruption on the trunk whose edges cannot be traced, and the clinician documents it as poorly demarcated. What does this term convey?
src.key: Irregular, blotchy, poorly defined borders
src.explanation: A poorly demarcated lesion has an irregular or blotchy appearance without well-defined borders, in contrast to a well-demarcated lesion, which has clearly defined borders.

items.section_title: 6.5 · Objective b — Varicella and herpes zoster
items.html: Antiviral timing. For a dermatomal vesicular eruption, start antivirals as soon as possible, ideally within 72 hours of rash onset. Treatment is still given after 72 hours when new lesions are forming or there is ophthalmic involvement.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 106

src.question: A 67-year-old woman presents on day four of a dermatomal vesicular eruption with new lesions still appearing. Within what window should antiviral therapy ideally be started, and when should it still be given beyond that window?
src.key: Within 72 hours, and later if lesions still form
src.explanation: Antivirals should be started as soon as possible, ideally within 72 hours of rash onset, and treatment is still given after 72 hours when new lesions are forming or there is ophthalmic involvement.

items.section_title: 5.2 · Objective a — Bedbugs, fleas, stings and caterpillars
items.html: Hymenoptera sting anaphylaxis. Treat with subcutaneous or intramuscular epinephrine, emergency department transfer and supportive measures.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: A 28-year-old man is stung by a wasp and within minutes develops widespread urticaria, wheezing, and hypotension. What is the immediate treatment?
src.key: Intramuscular or subcutaneous epinephrine
src.explanation: For an anaphylactic reaction to a hymenoptera sting the treatment is subcutaneous or intramuscular epinephrine with emergency department transfer and supportive measures.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Erythrasma sites. Most common on the inner thighs, crural region, scrotum, and between the fourth and fifth toes; less common in the axilla, under the breasts and intergluteal folds. It is usually asymptomatic and may be pruritic.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 81

src.question: A 55-year-old man with diabetes has an asymptomatic brownish patch in a skin fold noted on routine examination. Where is erythrasma most commonly found, and what is the typical symptom profile?
src.key: Inner thighs, groin, and fourth toe web; often silent
src.explanation: The most common sites are the inner thighs, crural region, scrotum, and between the fourth and fifth toes, with the axilla, under the breasts, and intergluteal folds less common. It is usually asymptomatic and may be pruritic.

also.key: Inner thighs, crural region, scrotum, and between the fourth and fifth toes
also.explanation: Less common sites are the axilla, under the breasts and intergluteal folds.

items.section_title: 9.4 · Objective 1 — Basal cell carcinoma
items.html: Mohs surgery for basal cell carcinoma. Indicated for high-risk anatomic sites, recurrent tumors, aggressive histology, or where tissue sparing is needed. The goal is complete eradication with minimal cosmetic and functional deformity.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 38

src.question: A 70-year-old woman has a basal cell carcinoma on the nasal ala that has recurred after a previous excision. When should Mohs micrographic surgery be considered for basal cell carcinoma?
src.key: High-risk sites, recurrence, or tissue sparing
src.explanation: Mohs surgery is indicated for high-risk anatomic sites, recurrent tumors, aggressive histology, or where tissue-sparing is needed. The overall goal is complete eradication with minimal cosmetic and functional deformity.

items.section_title: 7.2 · Objective a — Abnormal wound healing: keloid and hypertrophic scar
items.html: Keloid management. Prevention is the most important treatment. High-risk patients should avoid cosmetic procedures such as ear piercing; post-surgical education includes avoiding stretching of an immature scar and avoiding hot baths.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 15

src.question: A 19-year-old woman whose sister developed a large keloid after ear piercing asks how to avoid the same problem. What is described as the most important element in the management of keloids?
src.key: Prevention, including avoiding ear piercing
src.explanation: Prevention is described as the most important treatment. High-risk patients should be advised to avoid cosmetic procedures such as ear piercing, and post-surgical education includes avoiding stretching of an immature scar and avoiding hot baths.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Stasis dermatitis red flag. Acute unilateral swelling or pain should raise concern for deep venous thrombosis, particularly when it is a new unilateral change on chronic bilateral changes.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 115

src.question: A 72-year-old man is referred with a red, warm, tender left lower leg. He has bilateral chronic ankle swelling and brown discoloration of both gaiter regions, but the left leg has become acutely more swollen and painful over two days. He is afebrile. What consideration should most urgently shape the evaluation?
src.key: Acute unilateral swelling suggests thrombosis
src.explanation: The differential for stasis dermatitis explicitly flags that acute unilateral swelling or pain should raise concern for deep venous thrombosis. Chronic bilateral changes with a new unilateral acute change is precisely that pattern.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Atopic dermatitis diagnosis. Diagnosis is usually clinical, supported by family history, personal history of atopy and recurrent rash. Immunoglobulin E may be elevated but is not routinely tested, and routine laboratory testing is not required.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 56

src.question: A 4-year-old girl has a typical history and examination for atopic dermatitis. Her parents ask whether blood tests are needed to confirm the diagnosis. What is the most accurate response?
src.key: It is clinical; no routine laboratory testing
src.explanation: The diagnosis is usually clinical, supported by family history, personal history of atopy, and a recurrent history of rash. Immunoglobulin E may be elevated but is not routinely tested, and routine laboratory testing is not required.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Irritant reaction timing. Mild irritants such as soaps may cause subacute symptoms progressing over weeks; alkalis and acids may present minutes after exposure or delayed up to 24 hours or more. Concentrated agents can cause chemical burns and necrosis.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 81

src.question: A 43-year-old factory worker splashes a concentrated alkali solution on the forearm, while a colleague of the same age has had weeks of soreness from repeated soap exposure. How does the timing of an irritant reaction to a strong alkali differ from that of a reaction to a mild irritant such as soap?
src.key: Alkalis act in minutes; soaps over weeks
src.explanation: Symptoms present differently depending on the exposure: mild irritants such as soaps may present with subacute symptoms that progress over weeks, while alkalis and acids may present minutes after exposure or delayed up to 24 hours or more. Concentrated agents can lead to chemical burns and necrosis.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Erysipelas organism and drug. Group A streptococcus (Streptococcus pyogenes) is the most common organism, involving the upper dermis and superficial lymphatics. Penicillin V is the drug, with clindamycin if penicillin allergic; tinea pedis is a risk factor.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 104

src.question: A 62-year-old woman presents with sudden onset of fever to 39.1 degrees Celsius, chills, and myalgias, followed within a day by a painful red area on her left shin. Examination shows a brightly erythematous plaque raised above the surrounding skin with a sharply defined border, and red streaks extending proximally. She has tinea pedis. What is the most likely organism and the drug of choice?
src.key: Streptococcus pyogenes, treated with penicillin V
src.explanation: Group A streptococcus is the most common organism in erysipelas, which involves the upper dermis and superficial cutaneous lymphatics. Penicillin V is the pharmacotherapy, with clindamycin if the patient is penicillin allergic. Tinea pedis is a listed risk factor.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Tender pretibial nodules. A deep incisional biopsy, needed because the pathology lies in subcutaneous fat, shows septal panniculitis without vasculitis and Miescher's granulomas.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: A 34-year-old woman with tender pretibial nodules undergoes a deep incisional biopsy. What finding confirms the diagnosis?
src.key: Septal panniculitis without vasculitis, with Miescher's granulomas
src.explanation: Biopsy shows septal panniculitis without vasculitis and Miescher's granulomas. A deep incisional biopsy is needed because the pathology lies in the subcutaneous fat.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Perioral dermatitis versus acne vulgaris. Open or closed comedones point to acne vulgaris; perioral dermatitis produces grouped monomorphic papules, papulovesicles or papulopustules without comedones.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 100

src.question: A 26-year-old woman has grouped papules and papulopustules around the mouth, and the clinician is distinguishing perioral dermatitis from its principal differential diagnoses. What finding would most specifically point to acne vulgaris instead?
src.key: Open or closed comedones
src.explanation: Acne vulgaris is more likely when open or closed comedones are present. Perioral dermatitis produces grouped monomorphic papules, papulovesicles, or papulopustules without comedones.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Objective a — Tick-borne illness
items.html: Rocky Mountain spotted fever laboratory findings. Thrombocytopenia with a normal white count is characteristic, and indirect immunofluorescence assay is the gold standard test. Cerebrospinal fluid may show leukocytosis, moderately elevated protein and normal glucose.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 85

src.question: A 34-year-old man with suspected Rocky Mountain spotted fever has blood drawn before treatment is started. What laboratory abnormalities are characteristic, and what is the gold standard diagnostic test?
src.key: Thrombocytopenia with a normal white count
src.explanation: Those are the characteristic laboratory findings, and the indirect immunofluorescence assay is the gold standard. Cerebrospinal fluid may show leukocytosis, moderately elevated protein, and normal glucose.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Epidermolysis bullosa and cancer. Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa causes severe scarring and carries the greatest long-term squamous cell carcinoma risk, so its multidisciplinary team includes hematology and oncology for surveillance. Scarring subtypes carry the malignancy risk.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 30

src.question: A 2-week-old neonate develops blisters at sites of handling and diapering, and genetic testing is planned. Which subtype carries the greatest long-term risk of squamous cell carcinoma and requires the most intensive multidisciplinary surveillance?
src.key: Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa
src.explanation: Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa causes severe scarring, and the multidisciplinary team includes hematology and oncology specifically for squamous cell carcinoma surveillance. Scarring subtypes carry the malignancy risk.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Pityriasis rosea management. It is self-limited, so reassurance is the mainstay, with oral antihistamines or topical steroids used cautiously for pruritus. Ultraviolet B phototherapy or sunlight helps if begun in the first week; severe cases may be treated with acyclovir.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 171

src.question: A 24-year-old man is diagnosed with pityriasis rosea. The eruption began four days ago and is mildly itchy. He is otherwise well and not pregnant-exposed or immunocompromised. What is the most appropriate management?
src.key: Reassurance, with an antihistamine for itch
src.explanation: Pityriasis rosea is self-limited and the mainstay is reassurance. Oral antihistamines or topical steroids can be used cautiously for pruritus, and phototherapy or natural sunlight may help if begun in the first week of the eruption.

also.key: It is self-limited, so reassurance is the mainstay, with antihistamines or topical steroids used cautiously for pruritus
also.explanation: Ultraviolet B phototherapy or sunlight helps if begun in the first week; severe cases may be treated with acyclovir.

items.section_title: 3.2 · Objective a — Lesions that signal systemic disease
items.html: Löfgren syndrome. Erythema nodosum, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, fever and arthralgia form its recognized presentation, and it is referred to pulmonology or rheumatology.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 45

src.question: A 31-year-old woman with biopsy-confirmed erythema nodosum has bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy on chest radiograph together with fever and arthralgia. What is the most appropriate referral?
src.key: Pulmonology or rheumatology, for probable Löfgren syndrome
src.explanation: Löfgren syndrome is the association referred to pulmonology or rheumatology. The combination of erythema nodosum, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, fever, and arthralgia is its recognized presentation.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Topical therapy for impetigo. For a single or limited number of non-bullous lesions, mupirocin ointment is adequate for most cases and as effective as oral therapy with fewer side effects. Remove crusts before applying it.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 94

src.question: A 5-year-old boy has several lesions around the nose and mouth. Examination shows golden-yellow adherent crusts over shallow erosions, with palpable regional lymphadenopathy. He is afebrile and there are only four lesions. What is the most appropriate treatment?
src.key: Topical mupirocin, removing crusts first
src.explanation: Topical therapy is used for a single or limited number of non-bullous lesions, and mupirocin ointment is adequate for most cases of impetigo and as effective as oral therapy with fewer side effects. Crusts should be removed before applying it.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Objective a — Tick-borne illness
items.html: Erythema migrans. Stage 1, early localized infection: a lesion greater than 5 cm that expands with central clearing and often a darker punctate center (bull's-eye). Diagnose and treat on that basis; testing helps most in non-endemic regions with non-diagnostic symptoms.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 72

src.question: A 40-year-old man in Connecticut develops an expanding erythematous oval lesion 8 cm across with central clearing and a darker punctate center at the site of a recent tick bite. What stage is this?
src.key: Stage 1, early localized infection
src.explanation: Stage 1 early localized infection is characterized by erythema migrans, a lesion greater than 5 cm that expands with central clearing and often a darker punctate center, also called a bull's-eye. A patient with this lesion should be diagnosed and treated on that basis, and testing is most helpful in patients from non-endemic regions with non-diagnostic symptoms.

items.section_title: 9.2 · Objective 1 — Actinic keratosis
items.html: Actinic keratosis pathogenesis. Actinic keratoses are intraepidermal keratinocytic dysplasias induced by cumulative ultraviolet B exposure; ultraviolet-induced TP53 mutation is the critical molecular event. They represent a field cancerization process.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 112

src.question: A 71-year-old man with a lifetime of outdoor work has multiple rough, scaly erythematous papules on the scalp and dorsal hands, each 2 to 8 mm, that feel like sandpaper when palpated. What molecular event is the critical step in their development?
src.key: Ultraviolet-induced TP53 mutation
src.explanation: Actinic keratoses are intraepidermal keratinocytic dysplasias induced by cumulative ultraviolet B exposure, and ultraviolet-induced mutations in TP53 are the critical molecular event. They represent a field cancerisation process.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Resistant folliculitis testing. A potassium hydroxide wet mount of a plucked hair rules out fungal (dermatophyte) folliculitis. Culture and Gram stain from an unroofed pustule are also performed.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: A 27-year-old woman has folliculitis of the thighs that has failed to respond to antibacterial treatment, and a hair is plucked from an affected follicle. What test should be performed on it?
src.key: A potassium hydroxide wet mount
src.explanation: In resistant cases a potassium hydroxide wet mount using a plucked hair is used to rule out fungal, specifically dermatophyte, folliculitis. Culture and Gram stain from an unroofed pustule are also performed.

items.section_title: 6.8 · Objective c — Care strategies by age
items.html: Tinea pedis prevention. Drying between the toes after bathing is essential, alongside antifungal foot powder for shoes, open-toed sandals when possible, sandals in community showers, and frequent sock changes.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 45

src.question: A 38-year-old man with recurrent tinea pedis is being counseled on preventing further episodes. What patient education point is described as essential?
src.key: Drying between the toes after bathing
src.explanation: Drying between the toes after bathing is marked as essential, alongside antifungal foot powder for shoes, wearing open-toed sandals when possible, using sandals in community showers, and changing socks frequently.

items.section_title: 2.3 · Objective c — Vesiculobullous disease
items.html: Bullous pemphigoid diagnosis. Biopsy the lesion for histopathology and perilesional tissue for direct immunofluorescence. Serum indirect immunofluorescence or enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay can identify anti-basement membrane zone antibodies.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 124

src.question: A 63-year-old woman has widespread tense bullae and a pruritic prodrome. The clinician plans a biopsy. What specimen and technique will best establish the diagnosis?
src.key: Lesion histology, perilesional immunofluorescence
src.explanation: Bullous pemphigoid is diagnosed by biopsying the lesion for histopathology and perilesional tissue for direct immunofluorescence examination. Serum indirect immunofluorescence or enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay can identify anti-basement membrane zone antibodies.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Localized granuloma annulare. The localized variant (about 75 percent of cases) is asymptomatic, with flesh-colored to erythematous papules in an annular ring on the dorsal hands, feet and ankles. It is a benign, self-limiting granulomatous dermatosis.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 50

src.question: A 28-year-old woman has a single asymptomatic annular ring of flesh-colored papules on the dorsum of the foot. What course should be expected?
src.key: Benign and self-limiting
src.explanation: The localized variant accounts for about 75 percent of cases, presenting as flesh-colored to erythematous papules in an annular ring on the dorsal hands, feet, and ankles, and is asymptomatic. Granuloma annulare is a benign, self-limiting granulomatous dermatosis.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Lichen planus histology. Biopsy shows a band-like lymphocytic infiltrate in the dermis, plus hyperkeratosis without parakeratosis, basal layer vacuolisation, Civatte bodies in the lower epidermis and saw-tooth shaped rete ridges.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 177

src.question: A 50-year-old man has an intensely pruritic eruption of violaceous flat-topped papules on both wrists, and a biopsy is taken from one lesion. What histopathological finding is most characteristic?
src.key: A band-like lymphocytic infiltrate
src.explanation: Biopsy in lichen planus shows band-like infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis. Additional characteristic findings include hyperkeratosis without parakeratosis, vacuolisation of the basal layer, Civatte bodies in the lower epidermis, and saw-tooth shaped rete ridges.

items.section_title: 3.3 · Objective a — Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
items.html: Stevens-Johnson syndrome first step. Immediate withdrawal of the causative drug is the first step; earlier withdrawal is strongly associated with improved survival, and each day of delay worsens prognosis. Allopurinol is the most common trigger worldwide.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 83

src.question: A 58-year-old man taking allopurinol for three weeks develops fever, malaise, and painful swallowing, followed by erosions of the lips, mouth, and conjunctivae, and dusky skin lesions with detachment involving about 6 percent of his body surface area. What is the single most important immediate action?
src.key: Withdraw all suspect medications
src.explanation: Immediate causative drug withdrawal is the first step, and earlier withdrawal is strongly associated with improved survival — each day of delay worsens prognosis. Allopurinol is named as the most common trigger worldwide.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Objective a — Tick-borne illness
items.html: Rocky Mountain spotted fever triad. Fever above 39.5 degrees Celsius, headache and rash, present in only about 60 percent of patients. Fever presents in the first 3 days, with rash following 2 to 4 days after fever onset.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 82

src.question: A 12-year-old girl presents with fever and headache four days after a tick bite, and a rash has now appeared. What is the clinical triad of Rocky Mountain spotted fever, and how often is it present?
src.key: Fever, headache, and rash, in about 60 percent
src.explanation: The clinical triad is fever above 39.5 degrees Celsius, headache, and rash, present in only about 60 percent of patients. Fever presents in the first 3 days with rash following 2 to 4 days after fever onset.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Rosacea triggers. Sun exposure is the most universal trigger, alongside heat, alcohol, spicy foods and stress. Chronic ultraviolet exposure is also a listed risk factor.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 67

src.question: A 44-year-old fair-skinned woman newly diagnosed with rosacea asks which trigger is most important to control. What is the most accurate answer?
src.key: Sun exposure, described as the most universal trigger
src.explanation: Sun exposure is named as the most universal trigger of rosacea, alongside heat, alcohol, spicy foods, and stress. Chronic ultraviolet exposure is also a listed risk factor.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Emollient use in atopic dermatitis. Apply emollient to the skin after rinsing, avoid irritants, and keep skin care fragrance-free. Clinicians should also demonstrate medication quantity and correct application.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 58

src.question: The mother of a 3-year-old boy with atopic dermatitis asks how to apply the emollient she has been given. What instruction is correct?
src.key: Apply after rinsing; avoid fragrance
src.explanation: Prevention advice is that emollient should be applied to the skin after rinsing, the patient should avoid irritants, and skin care should be fragrance-free. Clinicians should also demonstrate medication quantity and correct application.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Toxicodendron (urushiol) dermatitis. Urushiol sap produces intensely pruritic vesicular lesions in linear distributions. Lesions erupt within 4 to 96 hours and may appear in multiple stages.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 87

src.question: A 19-year-old man presents two days after clearing brush at a summer job. He reports intense itching. Examination shows erythematous papules, vesicles, and a few small bullae arranged in linear streaks across the forearms and one calf, with excoriation between them. Some lesions appear newer than others. He is afebrile and the rash does not cross the midline of the trunk or follow a single band. What feature of the eruption best supports the diagnosis?
src.key: The linear arrangement of the lesions
src.explanation: Urushiol sap from Toxicodendron species produces intensely pruritic vesicular lesions in linear distributions, because the streaks mark where the plant grazed the skin in passing. Lesions erupt within 4 to 96 hours and may appear in multiple stages, as they do here.

items.section_title: 6.3 · Objective b — Nails, distant reactions, and steroid-altered tinea
items.html: Id reaction criteria. A dermatophyte infection is present elsewhere, none is found at the id site, and the eruption resolves. The primary site is potassium hydroxide positive, the id site negative, and onset is 1 to 2 weeks after the primary infection.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 62

src.question: A 30-year-old man develops an extremely pruritic papulovesicular eruption on the fingers ten days after being diagnosed with tinea pedis. A potassium hydroxide preparation from the finger lesions is negative, while one from the toe webs is positive. What three criteria establish this diagnosis?
src.key: Dermatophyte elsewhere, none at the site, resolves
src.explanation: Those are the three criteria for establishing an id reaction. The primary site is potassium hydroxide positive and the distant id site is potassium hydroxide negative, and the eruption occurs 1 to 2 weeks after the primary infection.

items.section_title: 7.3 · Objective a — Cutaneous horn and skin tags
items.html: Cutaneous horn. It arises from the surface of another lesion, benign or malignant (actinic keratosis, warts, squamous cell carcinoma). There is often no clinical feature to distinguish them, so the lesion at the base must be diagnosed.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 27

src.question: A 68-year-old man has a hard, conical keratotic projection on the dorsum of his hand. What is the key principle in evaluating this lesion?
src.key: Diagnose the lesion at the base
src.explanation: A cutaneous horn arises from the surface of another lesion, which may be benign or malignant — actinic keratosis, warts, and squamous cell carcinoma among them. There is often no clinical feature to distinguish them, so the underlying lesion must be diagnosed.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Wood's lamp. A handheld diagnostic device emitting long-wave ultraviolet light to highlight subtle changes in skin, scalp and hair; it evaluates pigment changes in selected fungal or bacterial infections.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 27

src.question: A 9-year-old boy has scaly patches of hair loss, and the clinician suspects a fungal or bacterial infection producing pigment change and reaches for a handheld device emitting long-wave ultraviolet light. What is this device and what does it evaluate?
src.key: A Wood's lamp, evaluating pigment change
src.explanation: A Wood's lamp is a handheld diagnostic device emitting long-wave ultraviolet light to highlight subtle changes in the skin, scalp, and hair, and it evaluates pigment changes in selected fungal or bacterial infections.

items.section_title: 6.1 · Objective a — Reading a potassium hydroxide preparation
items.html: Contact dermatitis pattern. It is often distinguishable from other dermatologic conditions by its clearly demarcated, unnatural patterns, tracing the shape of whatever touched the skin rather than a biological distribution.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 79

src.question: A 41-year-old woman has a sharply bounded eruption on the forearm whose outline does not correspond to any anatomical distribution. What general feature most often allows contact dermatitis to be distinguished from other dermatologic conditions on inspection alone?
src.key: Its clearly demarcated, unnatural patterns
src.explanation: Contact dermatitis in general is often distinguishable from other dermatologic conditions because of its clearly demarcated, unnatural patterns — the eruption traces the shape of whatever touched the skin rather than following a biological distribution.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Sunscreen use. Broad-spectrum sun protection factor 30 or above is advised for daily use and 50 or above for prolonged outdoor exposure, applied 15 minutes before sun exposure and reapplied every 2 hours.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 123

src.question: A 29-year-old fair-skinned woman asks how to use sunscreen correctly before a beach holiday. What advice matches the guidance given?
src.key: Factor 30 daily, reapplied every 2 hours
src.explanation: Broad-spectrum sun protection factor 30 or above is advised for daily use and 50 or above for prolonged outdoor exposure, applied 15 minutes before sun exposure and reapplied every 2 hours.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Bullous impetigo differential. It includes thermal burn, allergic contact dermatitis, and herpes simplex or zoster; non-bullous impetigo has a different differential list.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 92

src.question: Which conditions are named in the differential for bullous impetigo?
src.key: Thermal burn, allergic contact dermatitis, and herpes simplex or zoster
src.explanation: Correct — non-bullous impetigo has a different differential list.

items.section_title: 4.3 · Objective a — Impetigo, erysipelas, cellulitis and abscess
items.html: Cellulitis examination. All four cardinal signs of inflammation are present, most often on one lower leg, with borders neither raised nor demarcated. Bilateral disease almost never occurs.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 107

src.question: What are the examination findings of cellulitis?
src.key: All four cardinal signs of inflammation, most often on one lower leg, with borders neither raised nor demarcated
src.explanation: Bilateral disease is described as almost never occurring.

items.section_title: 4.1 · Objective a — Acne vulgaris
items.html: Acne vulgaris hallmark. The comedone, either open (blackhead) or closed (whitehead), defines acne, although acne is polymorphic.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 11

src.question: What is the hallmark lesion of acne vulgaris on physical examination?
src.key: The comedone, either open (blackhead) or closed (whitehead)
src.explanation: Acne is polymorphic, but the comedone is what defines it.

items.section_title: 4.4 · Objective a — Paronychia and necrotizing fasciitis
items.html: Necrotizing fasciitis microbiology. It is polymicrobial, with aerobic, anaerobic or mixed flora, and group A streptococci (Streptococcus pyogenes) are common.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 124

src.question: What is the microbiology of necrotizing fasciitis?
src.key: Polymicrobial from mixed flora, or group A Streptococcus
src.explanation: Correct — necrotizing fasciitis is polymicrobial, with aerobic, anaerobic or mixed flora, and group A streptococci (Streptococcus pyogenes) are common.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Acne vulgaris epidemiology. It is the most common skin disease in the United States, affecting about 80% of Americans in their lifetime, and usually begins with the onset of puberty.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 5

src.question: Where does acne vulgaris rank among skin diseases in the United States?
src.key: It is the most common skin disease, affecting about 80% of Americans in their lifetime
src.explanation: It usually begins with the onset of puberty.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Folliculitis sites. Small papules or pustules pierced by a central hair, commonly on the scalp, thighs, trunk, axilla and inguinal area.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 41

src.question: Which sites does folliculitis commonly affect?
src.key: Scalp, thighs, trunk, axilla, groin
src.explanation: Correct — folliculitis forms small papules or pustules pierced by a central hair, commonly on the scalp, thighs, trunk, axilla and inguinal area.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Impetigo portal of entry. The primary portal is minor superficial breaks in the skin such as cuts and bug bites, though no predisposing lesion is identified in most patients.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 86

src.question: What is the primary portal of entry for impetigo?
src.key: Minor superficial breaks in the skin such as cuts and bug bites
src.explanation: No predisposing lesion is identified in most patients.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Hot tub folliculitis timing and distribution. Onset is eight hours to five days after exposure, on the trunk, extremities and buttocks, usually sparing the face, neck, soles and palms.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 49

src.question: What is the typical timing and distribution of hot tub folliculitis?
src.key: Onset eight hours to five days after exposure, on the trunk, extremities and buttocks
src.explanation: It usually spares the face, neck, soles and palms.

items.section_title: 4.3 · Objective a — Impetigo, erysipelas, cellulitis and abscess
items.html: Non-bullous impetigo. A macule evolves into a vesicle or pustule that ruptures, leaving a honey-colored adherent crust, typically on the face and extremities, with regional lymphadenopathy common.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 87

src.question: Describe the classic appearance of non-bullous impetigo.
src.key: A macule evolves into a vesicle or pustule that ruptures, leaving a honey-colored adherent crust
src.explanation: typically on the face and extremities, with regional lymphadenopathy common.

items.section_title: 4.3 · Objective a — Impetigo, erysipelas, cellulitis and abscess
items.html: Cellulitis portals of entry. Named portals are tinea pedis, open lesion, trauma, surgical wound, insect bite, fissure and radiation therapy. These are distinct from the risk factors, which include diabetes and lymphedema.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 106

src.question: Which portals of entry are named for cellulitis?
src.key: Tinea pedis, open lesion, trauma, surgical wound, insect bite, fissure and radiation therapy
src.explanation: Those are distinct from the risk factors, which include diabetes and lymphedema.

items.section_title: 4.3 · Objective a — Impetigo, erysipelas, cellulitis and abscess
items.html: Erysipelas laboratory findings. Leukocytosis with raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein are common but not diagnostic; the diagnosis remains clinical in a classic presentation.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 103

src.question: Which laboratory abnormalities are common in erysipelas, and what do they contribute?
src.key: Leukocytosis with raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein — common but not diagnostic
src.explanation: The diagnosis remains clinical in a classic presentation.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Impetigo isolation. A child may return once treatment has been underway for twenty-four to forty-eight hours. Towels, clothing, bath water, washcloths and razors must not be shared.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 96

src.question: What isolation advice is given for a child with impetigo?
src.key: Isolate until treatment has been underway for twenty-four to forty-eight hours
src.explanation: and do not share towels, clothing, bath water, washcloths or razors.

also.key: He may return once treatment has been underway for twenty-four to forty-eight hours
also.explanation: and towels, clothing, bath water, washcloths and razors must not be shared.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Pseudofolliculitis barbae. This foreign-body reaction to hair in shaved areas is most common in Black males with tightly curled hair and keratin gene variations, and in anyone who shaves and has curlier hair.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 54

src.question: In whom does pseudofolliculitis barbae most commonly occur?
src.key: Black males, or anyone who shaves and has curlier hair
src.explanation: Correct — this foreign-body reaction to hair in shaved areas is common in Black males with tightly curled hair and keratin gene variations, and in anyone curly-haired who shaves.

items.section_title: 4.4 · Objective a — Paronychia and necrotizing fasciitis
items.html: Contact dermatitis versus cellulitis. Contact dermatitis is itchy with vesicles and no fever, whereas cellulitis is tender and warm rather than itchy.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 108

src.question: Which feature distinguishes contact dermatitis from cellulitis?
src.key: Itching and vesicles with an absence of fever
src.explanation: Correct — cellulitis is tender and warm rather than itchy.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Carbuncle versus furuncle. A carbuncle is extremely painful and more often produces systemic symptoms: malaise, chills and fever.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 63

src.question: How does a carbuncle differ from a furuncle at presentation?
src.key: It is extremely painful and more often produces malaise, chills and fever
src.explanation: Systemic symptoms are more common with a carbuncle.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Folliculitis not clearing on topical treatment. This is now a resistant case: unroof a pustule for Gram stain and culture. Culture, potassium hydroxide mount, nasal swab and biopsy are all available.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: A 36-year-old woman has folliculitis of the thighs that has not cleared after two weeks of topical clindamycin. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Unroof a pustule for Gram stain and culture, since this is now a resistant case
src.explanation: Correct — culture, potassium hydroxide mount, nasal swab and biopsy are all available.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Hidradenitis suppurativa diagnosis. No test is required: it is a clinical diagnosis resting on lesions, distribution and recurrence. Biopsy is not usually required, though it shows follicular occlusion and apocrine gland destruction.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 74

src.question: A 33-year-old woman has axillary nodules and sinuses. The diagnosis of hidradenitis suppurativa is being considered. Which test is required to confirm it?
src.key: None — it is a clinical diagnosis resting on lesions, distribution and recurrence
src.explanation: Biopsy is not usually required, though it shows follicular occlusion and apocrine gland destruction.

items.section_title: 4.4 · Objective a — Paronychia and necrotizing fasciitis
items.html: Nail fold vesicles. A Tzanck smear rules out herpetic whitlow. Potassium hydroxide rules out candida and Gram stain identifies bacteria.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 118

src.question: A 30-year-old woman has a painful swollen fingertip with grouped small vesicles at the lateral nail fold. Which test would settle the diagnosis?
src.key: Tzanck smear, to rule out herpetic whitlow
src.explanation: Potassium hydroxide rules out candida and Gram stain identifies bacteria.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Excluding fungal folliculitis. A potassium hydroxide wet mount using a plucked hair is the specific test named for dermatophyte folliculitis.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: A 28-year-old man with folliculitis has failed topical mupirocin. Scraping and culture are being arranged. Which additional test excludes fungal folliculitis?
src.key: A potassium hydroxide wet mount using a plucked hair
src.explanation: Correct — that is the specific test named for dermatophyte folliculitis.

items.section_title: 4.3 · Objective a — Impetigo, erysipelas, cellulitis and abscess
items.html: Tinea pedis and erysipelas. Tinea pedis is a named risk factor for erysipelas, serving as the portal of entry and predicting recurrence, so treat it.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 99

src.question: A 58-year-old man with longstanding athlete's foot develops erysipelas of the same leg. Which is the most appropriate additional management step?
src.key: Treat the tinea pedis, since it is the portal of entry and predicts recurrence
src.explanation: Correct — it is named among the risk factors for erysipelas.

items.section_title: 4.3 · Objective a — Impetigo, erysipelas, cellulitis and abscess
items.html: Cellulitis treatment failure. Fever persisting beyond forty-eight hours of antibiotics is the stated trigger to change the antimicrobial therapy, guided by the culture results.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 112

src.question: A 59-year-old woman with cellulitis of the leg still has a fever of 38.6 degrees Celsius after fifty-four hours of oral antibiotics. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Change the antimicrobial therapy, guided by the culture results
src.explanation: Correct — fever beyond forty-eight hours is the stated trigger for a change.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Hidradenitis suppurativa steroids. Intralesional triamcinolone acetonide decreases the size of draining sinuses. Oral prednisone reduces inflammation and prevents future lesions.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 77

src.question: A 35-year-old woman with hidradenitis suppurativa has draining sinuses that persist despite topical clindamycin and a mild steroid cream. Which is the most appropriate next treatment?
src.key: Intralesional triamcinolone acetonide to decrease the size of the draining sinuses
src.explanation: Oral prednisone reduces inflammation and prevents future lesions.

items.section_title: 4.3 · Objective a — Impetigo, erysipelas, cellulitis and abscess
items.html: Abscess versus furuncle. An abscess arises from traumatic inoculation of bacteria into the skin, whereas a furuncle arises from an infected hair follicle.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 113

src.question: A 33-year-old man who injects drugs has a tender fluctuant swelling of the forearm that developed at an injection site. Which best describes how this lesion arose?
src.key: Traumatic inoculation of bacteria into the skin, which is how an abscess differs from a furuncle
src.explanation: Correct — a furuncle arises from an infected hair follicle instead.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Endocarditis prophylaxis. Endocarditis prophylaxis before the procedure is named for at-risk patients in both furuncle and carbuncle management.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 67

src.question: A 57-year-old woman with a prosthetic heart valve has a carbuncle requiring drainage. Which additional measure is specifically indicated?
src.key: Endocarditis prophylaxis before the procedure
src.explanation: Correct — it is named for at-risk patients in both furuncle and carbuncle management.

items.section_title: 4.3 · Objective a — Impetigo, erysipelas, cellulitis and abscess
items.html: Erysipelas risk factor. Impaired lymphatic drainage, such as after axillary node clearance, is the first risk factor named for erysipelas and explains recurrence.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 99

src.question: A 70-year-old woman who had a mastectomy with axillary node clearance has recurrent erysipelas of that arm. Which factor most explains the recurrence?
src.key: Impaired lymphatic drainage from the node clearance
src.explanation: Correct — it is the first risk factor named for erysipelas.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Topical tretinoin in pseudofolliculitis barbae. It relieves the hyperkeratosis, removing the epidermis the emerging hair embeds in. Mild corticosteroids reduce inflammation and topical antibiotics reduce colonization.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 58

src.question: A 33-year-old man with pseudofolliculitis barbae is prescribed topical tretinoin. Which is the most appropriate explanation of what it does?
src.key: It relieves the hyperkeratosis, removing the epidermis the emerging hair embeds in
src.explanation: Mild corticosteroids reduce inflammation and topical antibiotics reduce colonization.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Extensive hidradenitis suppurativa. When medical therapy has failed, wide excision of the affected areas gives the best chance of permanent cure. Large fluctuant cysts are meanwhile incised and drained.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 79

src.question: A 40-year-old woman has extensive hidradenitis suppurativa in both axillae that has failed medical therapy for years. She asks whether anything can cure it. Which is the most appropriate response?
src.key: Wide excision of the affected areas gives the best chance of permanent cure
src.explanation: Large fluctuant cysts are meanwhile incised and drained.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Impetigo in high-risk occupations. Teachers and health-care workers are at high risk for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, so their impetigo is cultured rather than diagnosed on appearance alone.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 93

src.question: A 30-year-old primary school teacher has impetigo across one forearm. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Obtain a culture, because her occupation places her at high risk for resistant organisms
src.explanation: Correct — teachers and health-care workers are at high risk for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, so their impetigo is cultured rather than diagnosed on appearance alone.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Diagnosis of classic erysipelas. No routine testing is needed, since blood and tissue cultures have extremely low yield. Leukocytosis and raised inflammatory markers are common but not diagnostic.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 103

src.question: A 72-year-old woman with erysipelas of the leg has a clinically classic presentation. Which is the most appropriate diagnostic approach?
src.key: No routine testing, since blood and tissue cultures have extremely low yield
src.explanation: Leukocytosis and raised inflammatory markers are common but not diagnostic.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Recurrent folliculitis. Swab the nose for Staphylococcus aureus carriage and treat with mupirocin if positive; nasal mupirocin twice daily for five days addresses the carrier state.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 46

src.question: A 41-year-old woman has had folliculitis recur four times in a year despite topical treatment each time. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Swab the nose for Staphylococcus aureus carriage and treat with mupirocin if positive
src.explanation: Correct — nasal mupirocin twice daily for five days addresses the carrier state.

items.section_title: 6.4 · Objective b — The yeasts: candidal intertrigo and pityriasis versicolor
items.html: Pityriasis versicolor distribution and appearance. Lesions favor the trunk, neck and proximal arms as finely scaling macules and patches that are hypopigmented, hyperpigmented or pink and velvety, from 4 to 5 millimeters up to large confluent areas.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 78

src.question: Where do the lesions of pityriasis versicolor favor, and what do they look like?
src.key: Trunk, neck and proximal arms; finely scaling macules and patches
src.explanation: Correct — hypopigmented, hyperpigmented or pink, velvety, from 4 to 5 millimeters up to large confluent areas.

items.section_title: 6.5 · Objective b — Varicella and herpes zoster
items.html: Varicella complication risk. Adults, pregnancy, newborn age and immunocompromise carry an increased risk of complications.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 84

src.question: Which groups have increased risk of complications from varicella?
src.key: Adults, pregnancy, newborn age, and immunocompromise
src.explanation: Correct — those four groups carry the increased risk.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Tinea cruris. Commonly called jock itch, it is more common in men and often coexists with tinea pedis, which is why the coexisting foot infection must be treated too.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 31

src.question: Who gets tinea cruris, what is it commonly called, and what does it often coexist with?
src.key: More common in men; jock itch; often coexists with tinea pedis
src.explanation: Correct — which is why the coexisting foot infection must be treated too.

items.section_title: 6.4 · Objective b — The yeasts: candidal intertrigo and pityriasis versicolor
items.html: Risk factors for intertrigo and cutaneous candidiasis. Obesity, diabetes, incontinence, occlusion, immobility, antibiotics and immunosuppression. Common sites are inframammary, axillary, abdominal, inguinal, perineal and interdigital folds.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 68

src.question: Which risk factors are named for intertrigo and cutaneous candidiasis?
src.key: Obesity, diabetes, incontinence, occlusion, immobility, antibiotics
src.explanation: Correct — and immunosuppression. Common sites are inframammary, axillary, abdominal, inguinal, perineal and interdigital folds.

items.section_title: 6.4 · Objective b — The yeasts: candidal intertrigo and pityriasis versicolor
items.html: First step in candidal intertrigo. Correct the environment first: gently dry the folds, reduce friction and occlusion, use moisture-wicking fabric or absorbent material, and address incontinence or hyperhidrosis.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 72

src.question: What is the first move in treating candidal intertrigo?
src.key: Correct the environment first
src.explanation: Correct — gently dry the folds, reduce friction and occlusion, use moisture-wicking fabric or absorbent material, and address incontinence or hyperhidrosis. The environment is what created the problem.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Topical antifungal in tinea corporis. Localized disease is treated with topical terbinafine, butenafine or an azole applied to the lesion and 1 to 2 centimeters beyond its border, which covers the advancing edge.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 28

src.question: How far beyond the lesion border should topical antifungal be applied in tinea corporis?
src.key: One to two centimeters beyond the border
src.explanation: Correct — with topical terbinafine, butenafine or an azole for localized disease.

also.key: Topical terbinafine, butenafine, or an azole, applied to the lesion and 1 to 2 centimeters beyond its border
also.explanation: Correct — treating beyond the border covers the advancing edge.

items.section_title: 6.2 · Objective b — The dermatophytes, by body site
items.html: Vesiculobullous tinea pedis. It presents as a moist, acute, pruritic and painful vesicular or bullous eruption on underlying erythema, and is caused by Trichophyton species like the other two forms.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 41

src.question: How does vesiculobullous tinea pedis present?
src.key: A moist, acute, pruritic and painful vesicular or bullous eruption
src.explanation: Correct — on underlying erythema, and caused by Trichophyton species like the other two forms.

items.section_title: 6.2 · Objective b — The dermatophytes, by body site
items.html: Tinea pedis patient education. Drying between the toes after bathing is essential. Also advise antifungal foot powder for shoes, open-toed sandals when possible, sandals in community showers, and changing socks frequently.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 45

src.question: Which piece of tinea pedis patient education is essential?
src.key: Dry between the toes after bathing
src.explanation: Correct — alongside antifungal foot powder for shoes, open-toed sandals when possible, sandals in community showers, and changing socks frequently.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
