items.html: Herpes simplex virus. It is a double-stranded DNA virus of the Herpesviridae family that produces latent but lifelong infection; latency for life is its defining feature.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 116

src.question: What kind of virus is herpes simplex, and what defines its behavior in the host?
src.key: A double-stranded DNA virus of the Herpesviridae family that produces latent but lifelong infection
src.explanation: Correct — latency for life is the defining feature.

items.section_title: 6.4 · Objective b — The yeasts: candidal intertrigo and pityriasis versicolor
items.html: Sites to inspect for candidal skin disease. The inframammary, axillary, abdominal, inguinal, perineal and interdigital folds are the six named common sites.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 68

src.question: A 70-year-old with obesity, diabetes and incontinence is examined for candidal skin disease. Which sites are the common ones to inspect?
src.key: Inframammary, axillary, abdominal, inguinal, and interdigital folds
src.explanation: Correct — the perineal folds are on the list too, making six named sites.

items.section_title: 6.2 · Objective b — The dermatophytes, by body site
items.html: Tinea capitis and shared items. Fungal particles remain viable for months, so hair-care items must not be shared and should be cleaned.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 10

src.question: The parents of a child with tinea capitis ask how long fungal particles survive on the hairbrush she shares with her sister. Which is the most appropriate response?
src.key: Fungal particles remain viable for months, so hair-care items must not be shared and should be cleaned

src.key: Oral antifungal therapy with griseofulvin or terbinafine, plus shaving or hair removal and warm compresses to remove crusts

src.question: Which self-care measure is essential for a patient with tinea pedis?
src.key: Drying between the toes after bathing

items.section_title: 6.5 · Objective b — Varicella and herpes zoster
items.html: Varicella and prompt consultation. Pregnancy, neonatal exposure, immunocompromise or severe complications are the four situations that warrant prompt consultation.

items.section_title: 6.1 · Objective a — Reading a potassium hydroxide preparation

items.section_title: 6.5 · Objective b — Varicella and herpes zoster

src.question: A patient has an atypical, widespread vesicular eruption and is immunocompromised. Which test is preferred, and from what sample?

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice

src.question: Which living circumstances predispose to body louse infestation?

src.question: What characterizes stage 2, early disseminated Lyme disease?

items.section_title: 5.5 · Objective a — Tick-borne illness

src.question: When is serological testing for Lyme disease most useful?

items.section_title: 5.4 · Objective a — Spider bites

src.question: Which patients are at increased risk of complications from a black widow bite, and how is envenomation treated?

items.section_title: 5.4 · Objective a — Spider bites

src.key: Shed hairs embed in skin or eyes causing pruritus, granulomas or conjunctivitis; treat with topical steroid and refer eyes to ophthalmology

src.question: What draws bedbugs out to feed, and where do they hide during the day?

items.section_title: 5.2 · Objective a — Bedbugs, fleas, stings and caterpillars

src.question: How should a honeybee sting be removed and why?

src.question: By which mechanisms do caterpillars produce skin disease?

src.question: How is a bedbug infestation diagnosed and managed?

src.question: On what basis is cutaneous larva migrans diagnosed?

items.section_title: 5.2 · Objective a — Bedbugs, fleas, stings and caterpillars

src.explanation: Correct — it results from keratin 5 and 14 mutations and is autosomal dominant.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Chronic urticaria escalation. If symptoms persist on a standard dose of a non-sedating antihistamine, increase up to four times the standard dose and consider adding an H2 blocker; omalizumab and ciclosporin follow if that fails.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 39

src.question: A patient with chronic urticaria is still symptomatic on a standard dose of a non-sedating antihistamine. What comes next?
src.key: Increase to up to four times the standard dose, and consider adding an H2 blocker
src.explanation: Correct — omalizumab and ciclosporin follow if that fails.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Photodermatitis versus seborrheic dermatitis. Photodermatitis spares the nasolabial folds, which seborrheic dermatitis involves, because shadowed areas are protected from light.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 101

src.question: Which feature separates photodermatitis from seborrheic dermatitis on the face?
src.key: Photodermatitis spares the nasolabial folds, which seborrheic dermatitis involves
src.explanation: Correct — shadowed areas are protected from light.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Fitzpatrick types IV to VI. These patients are not immune to ultraviolet damage or skin cancer, and melanoma is frequently diagnosed at advanced stages; delayed diagnosis is common because of a lower index of suspicion.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 122

src.question: What is true of patients with Fitzpatrick types IV to VI?
src.key: They are not immune to ultraviolet damage or skin cancer, and melanoma is frequently diagnosed at advanced stages
src.explanation: Correct — delayed diagnosis is common because of a lower index of suspicion.

items.section_title: 6.6 · Objective b — Herpes simplex and herpetic whitlow
items.html: Genetics of dermatitis herpetiformis. HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8 are strongly associated, the same haplotypes that underlie celiac disease.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 16

src.question: Which human leukocyte antigen haplotypes are strongly associated with dermatitis herpetiformis?
src.key: HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8
src.explanation: Correct — the same haplotypes that underlie celiac disease.

items.section_title: 3.3 · Objective a — Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
items.html: Level of care in Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Patients should be under intensive care or a burn unit, with dermatology involved. Nasogastric feeding is often needed because mucosal involvement prevents eating.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 83

src.question: Which services should a patient with Stevens-Johnson syndrome be under?
src.key: Intensive care or a burn unit, with dermatology involved
src.explanation: Correct — nasogastric feeding is often needed because mucosal involvement prevents eating.

items.section_title: 6.6 · Objective b — Herpes simplex and herpetic whitlow
items.html: Recurrent herpes-associated erythema multiforme. Chronic suppressive antiviral therapy, such as aciclovir 400 mg twice daily, is appropriate, because preventing the herpes recurrence prevents the eruption.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 12

src.question: A patient has had four episodes of herpes-associated erythema multiforme this year. Which chronic measure is appropriate?
src.key: Suppressive antiviral therapy, such as aciclovir 400 mg twice daily
src.explanation: Correct — preventing the herpes recurrence prevents the eruption.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Key diagnostic feature of urticaria. Individual lesions last less than twenty-four hours; lesions persisting beyond that suggest urticarial vasculitis.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 37

src.question: What single feature most reliably separates urticaria from its differentials?
src.key: Individual lesions last less than twenty-four hours
src.explanation: Correct — this is called the key diagnostic feature, and lesions persisting beyond it suggest urticarial vasculitis.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Erythema multiforme minor. It shows three-zone target lesions (dusky center, pale swollen ring, outer red halo) on acral surfaces after herpes simplex, with skin involvement only and no mucosal involvement.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 9

src.question: A 28-year-old man has a two-day history of a rash on his hands and forearms. Examination shows symmetric lesions on the palms and dorsal hands, each with a dusky center, a pale swollen ring and an outer red halo. He had a cold sore ten days ago. There is no mucosal involvement. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
src.key: Erythema multiforme minor
src.explanation: Three-zone target lesions on acral surfaces after herpes simplex, with skin involvement only.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Botulinum toxin for axillary hyperhidrosis. It is effective for three to six months, so retreatment will be needed; setting that expectation is named in the patient education.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 76

src.question: A 27-year-old man is considering botulinum toxin for axillary hyperhidrosis. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: It is effective for three to six months, so retreatment will be needed
src.explanation: Correct — setting that expectation is specifically named in the patient education.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Sunscreen in photoaging. Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen of SPF 30 or higher, applied as the last skincare step, is the single most evidence-supported intervention; use about one teaspoon for face and neck.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 119

src.question: A 47-year-old man with early photoaging asks what single measure will most reduce further damage. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen of SPF 30 or higher, applied as the last skincare step
src.explanation: Correct — it is the single most evidence-supported intervention, at about one teaspoon for face and neck.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Rosacea counseling. It is a chronic condition that therapy controls rather than eliminates, so long-term management and daily sun protection are expected, alongside a trigger diary and gentle non-irritating skincare.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 70

src.question: A 41-year-old woman newly diagnosed with rosacea asks whether treatment will cure it. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: It is a chronic condition that therapy controls rather than eliminates, so long-term management and daily sun protection are expected
src.explanation: alongside a trigger diary and gentle non-irritating skincare.

items.section_title: 8.1 · Objective a — Ephelides, lentigines and solar lentigo
items.html: Biopsy of a pigmented facial macule. Atypical or uncertain morphology on dermoscopy is the stated indication for biopsy; an asymmetric macule with an irregular border and two darker areas is biopsied to exclude lentigo maligna.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 111

src.question: A 64-year-old woman has one facial pigmented macule that is asymmetric with an irregular border and two darker areas within it, unlike her other lesions. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Biopsy the lesion to exclude lentigo maligna
src.explanation: Correct — atypical or uncertain morphology on dermoscopy is the stated indication for biopsy.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Severe blistering sunburn. Severe blistering above 20% of the body surface with systemic symptoms warrants hospitalization, with intravenous fluids and wound care given the systemic toxicity.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 96

src.question: A 19-year-old man has extensive blistering sunburn over his back and chest with fever, nausea and tachycardia after a day on the water. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Admit for intravenous fluids and wound care given the systemic toxicity
src.explanation: Correct — severe blistering above 20% of the body surface with systemic symptoms warrants hospitalization.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Severe Herlitz junctional epidermolysis bullosa. Early palliative care integration is appropriate, alongside genetics counseling and family support resources; goals-of-care discussion, pain optimization and psychosocial support are all indicated.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 32

src.question: The parents of a child with severe Herlitz junctional epidermolysis bullosa ask what support is available. Which is the most appropriate response?
src.key: Early palliative care integration is appropriate, alongside genetics counseling and family support resources
src.explanation: Correct — goals-of-care discussion, pain optimization and psychosocial support are all indicated in this subtype.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Post-phytophotodermatitis pigmentation. It fades over months, and daily sunscreen prevents it darkening further. Reassurance is first line, with hydroquinone or azelaic acid if it persists.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 101

src.question: A 33-year-old woman with resolved phytophotodermatitis is distressed by persistent brown streaks on her arms. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: The pigmentation fades over months, and daily sunscreen prevents it darkening further
src.explanation: Correct — reassurance is first line, with hydroquinone or azelaic acid if it persists.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Primary axillary hyperhidrosis not helped by aluminum chloride. Use glycopyrronium 2.4% cloth applied once daily, which is approved for axillary disease, or an oral anticholinergic as second line.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 75

src.question: A 22-year-old woman with primary axillary hyperhidrosis has not improved with nightly aluminum chloride. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Glycopyrronium 2.4% cloth applied once daily, or an oral anticholinergic
src.explanation: Correct — topical glycopyrronium is approved for axillary disease, with oral anticholinergics as second line.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Trigger testing for target lesions with oral erosions after cough and fever. Order Mycoplasma pneumoniae immunoglobulin M serology or polymerase chain reaction; elevated Mycoplasma immunoglobulin M is characteristic in children and atypical presentations.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 11

src.question: A 9-year-old boy develops target lesions and oral erosions two weeks after a persistent cough and fever. Which test should be ordered to identify the trigger?
src.key: Mycoplasma pneumoniae immunoglobulin M serology or polymerase chain reaction
src.explanation: Correct — elevated Mycoplasma immunoglobulin M is characteristic in children and atypical presentations.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Biopsy in erythema multiforme. Negative direct immunofluorescence with interface dermatitis on histology supports the diagnosis; negativity distinguishes it from pemphigoid and pemphigus.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 11

src.question: A 24-year-old man has target lesions on the palms, and the clinical picture is not clear-cut. A punch biopsy is taken with direct immunofluorescence. Which result would support erythema multiforme?
src.key: Negative direct immunofluorescence with interface dermatitis on histology
src.explanation: Correct — negativity is what distinguishes it from pemphigoid and pemphigus.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Course of chronic urticaria. About half resolves spontaneously within a year, and over half of cases have no identifiable trigger, so the search for a cause often finds none.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 36

src.question: A 29-year-old woman has had chronic spontaneous urticaria for eight months and asks whether it will ever settle. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: About half of chronic urticaria resolves spontaneously within a year, and over half of cases have no identifiable trigger
src.explanation: Correct — this reframes the search for a cause that often does not exist.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Angioedema without wheals. It should raise hereditary angioedema, and initial testing is complement C4 with C1-esterase inhibitor level and function.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 38

src.question: A 33-year-old man has recurrent episodes of lip and periorbital swelling without any wheals. Which is the most appropriate initial testing?
src.key: Complement C4 with C1-esterase inhibitor level and function
src.explanation: Correct — angioedema without wheals should raise hereditary angioedema.

items.section_title: 3.3 · Objective a — Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
items.html: First action in Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Discontinue the suspected drug and every other non-essential medication; earlier withdrawal is strongly associated with improved survival, and each day of delay worsens it.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 83

src.question: A 52-year-old man is admitted with Stevens-Johnson syndrome six days after starting trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Which is the single most important initial action?
src.key: Discontinue the suspected drug and every other non-essential medication
src.explanation: Correct — earlier withdrawal is strongly associated with improved survival, and each day of delay worsens it.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Episodic sweating with headache, palpitations and hypertension. This points to pheochromocytoma, and initial testing is twenty-four hour urine metanephrines and catecholamines.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 74

src.question: A 54-year-old man reports new generalized sweating including at night, with episodes of headache and palpitations, and his blood pressure is 178/104. Which is the most appropriate initial testing?
src.key: Twenty-four hour urine metanephrines and catecholamines
src.explanation: Correct — episodic sweating with headache, palpitations and hypertension points to phaeochromocytoma.

items.section_title: 6.6 · Objective b — Herpes simplex and herpetic whitlow
items.html: Recurrent erythema multiforme after oral herpes. Recurrent disease is strongly associated with recurrent herpes simplex, and long-term suppression is suppressive acyclovir 400 mg twice daily or valacyclovir 500 mg daily.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 12

src.question: A 31-year-old woman has her fourth episode of target lesions on the hands in eighteen months. Each episode has followed an oral herpes outbreak. Which is the most appropriate long-term management?
src.key: Suppressive acyclovir 400 mg twice daily or valacyclovir 500 mg daily
src.explanation: Correct — recurrent disease is strongly associated with recurrent herpes simplex, and suppression is the answer.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Pyoderma gangrenosum and debridement. The ulcer worsens with trauma, a phenomenon called pathergy, so debridement makes it larger; this is the single most consequential management point in the condition.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 60

src.question: A patient with pyoderma gangrenosum asks why the wound clinic will not debride the ulcer as they would for other wounds. Which is the most appropriate explanation?
src.key: The ulcer worsens with trauma, a phenomenon called pathergy, so debridement makes it larger
src.explanation: Correct — this is the single most consequential management point in the condition.

items.section_title: 9.2 · Objective 1 — Actinic keratosis
items.html: Transplant recipients. Immunosuppression raises the risk of actinic keratosis and skin cancer about sixty-fold, so they need aggressive photoprotection and biannual skin surveillance.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 112

src.question: A 55-year-old kidney transplant recipient asks why she is being seen so often for skin checks. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: Immunosuppression raises the risk of actinic keratosis and skin cancer about sixty-fold
src.explanation: Correct — transplant recipients need aggressive photoprotection and biannual skin surveillance.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Initial workup of erythema nodosum without bowel or respiratory symptoms or drug exposure. Order antistreptolysin O titer, throat culture, chest radiograph and inflammatory markers, with tuberculin or interferon gamma testing and a pregnancy test where relevant.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: A 25-year-old man with erythema nodosum has no bowel or respiratory symptoms and no recent drug exposure. Which initial investigations should be ordered?
src.key: Antistreptolysin O titre, throat culture, chest radiograph and inflammatory markers
src.explanation: with tuberculin or interferon gamma testing and a pregnancy test where relevant.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Velvety, darkened, thickened skin at the neck and axillae. It is a visible marker of insulin resistance and warrants metabolic assessment: fasting glucose, hemoglobin A1c, fasting insulin and a lipid panel.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 24

src.question: A 15-year-old with a body mass index in the 97th percentile has velvety, darkened, thickened skin at the back of the neck and in both axillae. Which is the most appropriate initial testing?
src.key: Fasting glucose, hemoglobin A1c, fasting insulin and a lipid panel
src.explanation: Correct — the finding is a visible marker of insulin resistance and warrants metabolic assessment.

items.section_title: 3.3 · Objective a — Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
items.html: Pathognomonic test for Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Punch biopsy showing full-thickness epidermal necrosis with junctional separation is the pathognomonic finding.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 82

src.question: A 41-year-old woman with painful skin and oral erosions has suspected Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Which diagnostic test is considered pathognomonic?
src.key: Punch biopsy showing full-thickness epidermal necrosis with junctional separation
src.explanation: Correct — that histology is the pathognomonic finding named for this condition.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Drug therapy in toxic epidermal necrolysis. Cyclosporine at 3 to 5 mg/kg daily, started early, has the strongest current evidence of the available options; early initiation is preferred.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 90

src.question: A 49-year-old man with toxic epidermal necrolysis has been admitted to the burn unit and the offending drug stopped. Which pharmacologic therapy has the strongest current evidence base?
src.key: Cyclosporine at 3 to 5 mg/kg daily, started early
src.explanation: Correct — early initiation is preferred and the evidence is the strongest of the available options.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa. Annual squamous cell carcinoma surveillance starts after the age of ten, because the severe scarring of dystrophic disease carries a substantial carcinoma risk.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 31

src.question: A 12-year-old with recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa attends for review. Which surveillance should now begin?
src.key: Annual squamous cell carcinoma surveillance, which starts after the age of ten
src.explanation: Correct — the severe scarring of dystrophic disease carries a substantial carcinoma risk.

items.section_title: 3.3 · Objective a — Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
items.html: SCORTEN of 5 in toxic epidermal necrolysis. A score of five or above carries a predicted mortality near 90%, and palliative care is referred for an early goals-of-care discussion.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 90

src.question: A 71-year-old woman with toxic epidermal necrolysis has a SCORTEN of 5 on admission. Beyond intensive care, which referral is specifically indicated at this score?
src.key: Palliative care, for an early goals-of-care discussion
src.explanation: Correct — a score of five or above carries a predicted mortality near 90% and palliative involvement is named.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Malignant acanthosis nigricans. Rapid onset, extensive velvety hyperpigmentation, mucosal change and tripe palms without obesity call for urgent evaluation for an underlying malignancy, particularly of the gastrointestinal tract.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 23

src.question: A 61-year-old man with no obesity develops widespread velvety hyperpigmentation over eight weeks, involving the axillae, the oral mucosa and the palms, which have a thickened rugose appearance. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Urgent evaluation for an underlying malignancy, particularly of the gastrointestinal tract
src.explanation: Correct — rapid onset, extensive involvement, mucosal change and tripe palms indicate malignant acanthosis nigricans.

items.section_title: 2.3 · Objective c — Vesiculobullous disease
items.html: Pemphigus mechanism. Autoantibodies to adhesion molecules cause loss of keratinocyte-to-keratinocyte adhesion, called acantholysis, producing intraepithelial blisters in a life-threatening blistering disorder of skin and mucous membranes.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 129

src.question: What is the mechanism of pemphigus?
src.key: Loss of keratinocyte-to-keratinocyte adhesion, called acantholysis, from autoantibodies to adhesion molecules, producing intraepithelial blisters
src.explanation: Correct — a life-threatening blistering disorder of skin and mucous membranes.

items.section_title: 2.3 · Objective c — Vesiculobullous disease
items.html: Light microscopy in bullous pemphigoid. Neutrophils are aligned in a straight narrow row at the dermal-epidermal junction. Biopsy a lesion for histopathology and perilesional tissue for direct immunofluorescence.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 124

src.question: What does light microscopy show in bullous pemphigoid?
src.key: Neutrophils aligned in a straight narrow row at the dermal-epidermal junction
src.explanation: Biopsy of a lesion goes for histopathology and perilesional tissue for direct immunofluorescence.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Dermatoscope. It is used for magnified examination of a lesion's surface and pigment pattern, and is the first-line tool for evaluating a pigmented lesion.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 24

src.question: What is a dermatoscope used for?
src.key: Magnified examination of a lesion's surface and pigment pattern
src.explanation: Correct — it is the first-line tool for evaluating a pigmented lesion.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Plaque versus patch. A plaque is elevated and plateau-like, while a patch is flat with no elevation; both exceed one centimeter, so elevation is the discriminator.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 10

src.question: What distinguishes a plaque from a patch?
src.key: A plaque is elevated and plateau-like; a patch is flat with no elevation
src.explanation: Correct — both exceed one centimeter, so elevation is the discriminator.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Atopic dermatitis epidemiology. About 20% of children worldwide are affected, and it is more common in males. It often begins in infancy or childhood; adult-onset disease occurs but is rare.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 52

src.question: What proportion of children worldwide are affected by atopic dermatitis, and in which sex is it more common?
src.key: About 20% of children, more common in males
src.explanation: It often begins in infancy or childhood; adult-onset disease occurs but is rare.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Allergic contact dermatitis cause. The most common cause is urushiol sap from Toxicodendron species, and approximately 50 to 75% of people in the United States react to it, which explains why not everyone who contacts poison ivy, sumac or oak reacts.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 85

src.question: What is the most common cause of allergic contact dermatitis, and roughly what proportion of people in the United States react to it?
src.key: Urushiol sap from Toxicodendron species — approximately 50 to 75%
src.explanation: which explains why not everyone who contacts poison ivy, sumac or oak reacts.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Xerosis. It reflects impaired stratum-corneum hydration, promoted by aging, low humidity, hot water, detergents, atopy and systemic disease. It commonly affects older adults, especially in winter, causing tightness, pruritus, rough scale, fissuring or eczema.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 152

src.question: What underlies xerosis, and who is most affected?
src.key: Impaired stratum-corneum hydration promoted by aging, low humidity, hot water, detergents, atopy and systemic disease, commonly affecting older adults especially in winter
src.explanation: causing tightness, pruritus, rough scale, fissuring or eczema.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Guttate psoriasis. It presents as raindrop-shaped erythematous papules and plaques in children, typically 2 to 3 weeks after a streptococcal infection or upper respiratory infection. It often needs no treatment, though phototherapy and topical steroids may be used.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 160

src.question: How does guttate psoriasis present, and what precedes it?
src.key: Raindrop-shaped erythematous papules and plaques in children, typically 2 to 3 weeks after a streptococcal infection or upper respiratory infection
src.explanation: It often needs no treatment, though phototherapy and topical steroids may be used.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Lichen planus histology. A biopsy shows a band-like infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis, a classic descriptive phrase worth recognizing on sight.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 177

src.question: What does a biopsy show in lichen planus?
src.key: A band-like infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis
src.explanation: Correct — a classic descriptive phrase worth recognizing on sight.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Nummular eczema plaques. They are intensely pruritic, round coin-shaped, light pink, scaly, thin plaques 1 to 10 cm, uniform without central clearing, most commonly on the extremities though they can occur on the trunk.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 72

src.question: How are nummular eczema plaques described?
src.key: Intensely pruritic, round coin-shaped, light pink, scaly, thin plaques 1 to 10 cm, uniform without central clearing
src.explanation: most commonly on the extremities though they can occur on the trunk.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Wheal. A wheal is a firm edematous plaque produced by infiltration of fluid into the dermis. The fluid is in the tissue rather than in a cavity, which separates it from a vesicle.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 13

src.question: What defines a wheal?
src.key: A firm edematous plaque produced by infiltration of fluid into the dermis
src.explanation: Correct — the fluid is in the tissue rather than in a cavity, which is what separates it from a vesicle.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Describing a skin finding. Six features translate a dermatological finding into words: primary morphology, secondary morphology, demarcation, color, size and distribution. Including all six lets another provider picture the lesion without seeing it.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 9

src.question: Which six features are used to translate a dermatological finding into words?
src.key: Primary morphology, secondary morphology, demarcation, color, size and distribution
src.explanation: Getting all six into a description is what lets another provider picture the lesion without seeing it.

items.section_title: 2.6 · Common dermatologic pharmacology
items.html: Refractory bullous pemphigoid. When prednisone and doxycycline fail, immunosuppressives such as methotrexate and azathioprine are used, with biologics and intravenous immunoglobulin also used. Low-dose methotrexate is described as safe and effective in the elderly, with folic acid.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 125

src.question: A patient with bullous pemphigoid has not responded to prednisone and doxycycline. Which agents are used for refractory disease?
src.key: Immunosuppressives such as methotrexate and azathioprine, with biologics and intravenous immunoglobulin also used
src.explanation: Correct — low-dose methotrexate is described as safe and effective in the elderly, with folic acid.

items.section_title: 2.6 · Common dermatologic pharmacology
items.html: Compression for stasis dermatitis. Consider an ankle-brachial index or toe pressure before starting substantial compression. Arterial status has to be clarified first, because compression on an ischemic limb causes harm.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 116

src.question: Which test should be considered before starting substantial compression for stasis dermatitis?
src.key: An ankle-brachial index or toe pressure
src.explanation: Correct — arterial status has to be clarified first, because compression on an ischemic limb causes harm.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Lichenification. It is thickening and hardening of the skin, and it develops from chronic rubbing or scratching.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 18

src.question: What is lichenification?
src.key: Thickening and hardening of the skin
src.explanation: Correct — it develops from chronic rubbing or scratching.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Atopic dermatitis education. Apply emollient after rinsing, avoid irritants, use fragrance-free skincare, demonstrate quantity and application, and give a written flare and infection action plan. Corticosteroid concerns are addressed directly rather than avoided.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 58

src.question: Which education points are named for atopic dermatitis?
src.key: Apply emollient after rinsing, avoid irritants, use fragrance-free skincare, demonstrate quantity and application, and give a written flare and infection action plan
src.explanation: Correct — corticosteroid concerns are addressed directly rather than avoided.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Herald patch. It is a single 2 to 5 cm round or oval, sharply demarcated pink or salmon plaque on the chest, neck or back, occurring in 50 to 90% of cases. It precedes the general eruption by one to two weeks.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 169

src.question: What is the herald patch, and how often does it occur?
src.key: A single 2 to 5 cm round or oval, sharply demarcated pink or salmon plaque on the chest, neck or back, occurring in 50 to 90% of cases
src.explanation: Correct — it precedes the general eruption by one to two weeks.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Lichenoid drug reactions. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, sulfonamides, tetracyclines, hydrochlorothiazide, quinidine and some beta blockers can produce them. Ask about these, since the eruption can mimic idiopathic lichen planus.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 173

src.question: Which medications can produce lichenoid reactions?
src.key: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, sulfonamides, tetracyclines, hydrochlorothiazide, quinidine and some beta blockers
src.explanation: Correct — worth asking about, since the eruption can mimic idiopathic lichen planus.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Extensive allergic contact dermatitis. When the eruption is extensive rather than limited, high-dose oral corticosteroids replace the high-potency topical steroid used for limited disease. Soothing measures such as oatmeal baths and cool compresses are used throughout.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 89

src.question: How does treatment of allergic contact dermatitis change when the eruption is extensive rather than limited?
src.key: High-dose oral corticosteroids replace the high-potency topical steroid used for limited disease
src.explanation: Correct — soothing measures such as oatmeal baths and cool compresses are used throughout.

items.section_title: 2.6 · Common dermatologic pharmacology
items.html: Dyshidrotic eczema hand care. Use lukewarm water and soap-free cleansers, dry thoroughly, then apply emollient immediately and as often as possible. Also avoid detergents, solvents, hair lotions or dyes, and acidic foods.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 66

src.question: Which hand-care advice is given for dyshidrotic eczema?
src.key: Lukewarm water and soap-free cleansers, dry thoroughly, then emollient immediately and as often as possible
src.explanation: alongside avoiding detergents, solvents, hair lotions or dyes, and acidic foods.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Atopic dermatitis prognosis. The disease is chronic and relapsing, but many patients improve with age; it may improve, persist or recur.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 58

src.question: What is the prognosis of atopic dermatitis?
src.key: Chronic and relapsing, but many patients improve with age
src.explanation: Correct — it may improve, persist or recur.

items.section_title: 1.7 · Objective h — Recall counseling strategies to help patients adhere to treatment plans
items.html: Tzanck smear. It gives rapid evaluation of vesicular lesions for herpesvirus cytologic changes. Polymerase chain reaction is preferred for confirmation: the smear is fast, the polymerase chain reaction is definitive.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 32

src.question: What is a Tzanck smear used for, and what is preferred for confirmation?
src.key: Rapid evaluation of vesicular lesions for herpesvirus cytologic changes, with polymerase chain reaction preferred for confirmation
src.explanation: Correct — the smear is fast, the polymerase chain reaction is definitive.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Irritant contact dermatitis timing. Mild irritants such as soaps may progress over weeks, while alkalis and acids may present within minutes or be delayed up to 24 hours or more. The agent determines the tempo.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 81

src.question: How does the timing of irritant contact dermatitis vary with the irritant?
src.key: Mild irritants such as soaps may progress over weeks, while alkalis and acids may present within minutes or be delayed up to 24 hours or more
src.explanation: Correct — the agent determines the tempo.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Von Zumbusch pustular psoriasis. Onset is abrupt and life-threatening: several days of fever, then generalized 2 to 3 mm pustules over trunk and extremities, including nail beds, palms and soles, that may form lakes of pus. It may follow systemic steroid withdrawal.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 160

src.question: What characterizes pustular psoriasis of the Von Zumbusch type?
src.key: Abrupt, life-threatening onset with several days of fever then a generalized eruption of 2 to 3 mm pustules over trunk and extremities including nail beds, palms and soles, which may form lakes of pus
src.explanation: and it may follow systemic steroid withdrawal. It is commonly mistaken for bacterial or viral infection.

items.section_title: 2.6 · Common dermatologic pharmacology
items.html: Lichen simplex chronicus recurrence. Recurrence depends on whether the initiating itch is controlled; it is common if the itch is not controlled. Sleep, anxiety, neuropathic symptoms and the primary dermatosis all need addressing.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 183

src.question: What determines whether lichen simplex chronicus recurs?
src.key: Whether the initiating itch is controlled, since recurrence is common if it is not
src.explanation: Correct — sleep, anxiety, neuropathic symptoms and the primary dermatosis all need addressing.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective c — Alopecia
items.html: Alopecia areata dermoscopy. Yellow dots, black dots, broken hairs, tapered hairs and short regrowth support the diagnosis. The diagnosis is clinical and dermoscopy strengthens it.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 139

src.question: Which dermoscopic findings support alopecia areata?
src.key: Yellow dots, black dots, broken hairs, tapered hairs and short regrowth
src.explanation: Correct — the diagnosis is clinical and dermoscopy strengthens it.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective c — Alopecia
items.html: Alopecia areata extent. Alopecia totalis describes loss of all scalp hair, and alopecia universalis describes loss of all body hair.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 137

src.question: What terms describe complete scalp and complete body hair loss in alopecia areata?
src.key: Alopecia totalis for all scalp hair, alopecia universalis for all body hair

items.section_title: 2.3 · Objective c — Vesiculobullous disease
items.html: Confirming bullous pemphigoid. Biopsy of perilesional tissue for direct immunofluorescence confirms the diagnosis. Lesional tissue goes for histopathology, with serum studies or ELISA identifying anti-basement membrane zone antibodies.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 124

src.question: A 76-year-old woman has widespread tense bullae and a clinical suspicion of bullous pemphigoid. Which test confirms the diagnosis?
src.key: Biopsy of perilesional tissue for direct immunofluorescence
src.explanation: Correct — lesional tissue goes for histopathology and perilesional tissue for immunofluorescence, with serum studies or ELISA identifying anti-basement membrane zone antibodies.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Lichen planus biopsy. The confirming finding is a band-like infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis, with hyperkeratosis without parakeratosis, basal vacuolization, Civatte bodies and a saw-tooth rete ridge.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 177

src.question: A 50-year-old man has suspected lichen planus. Which biopsy finding confirms the diagnosis?
src.key: Band-like infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis
src.explanation: with hyperkeratosis without parakeratosis, basal vacuolisation, Civatte bodies and a saw-tooth rete ridge.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Counseling for atopic dermatitis steroid worries. Address the concern directly, review the side effects, demonstrate how much to apply, and provide a written flare and infection action plan.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 58

src.question: A mother of a child newly diagnosed with atopic dermatitis is anxious about using topical steroids at all. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: Address the concern directly, review the side effects, demonstrate how much to apply, and provide a written flare and infection action plan
src.explanation: Addressing steroid concerns directly and demonstrating quantity and application are named education points.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective c — Alopecia
items.html: Alopecia areata counseling. Psychological support is one of the most important considerations in managing this condition, and support groups may be offered.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 140

src.question: A 22-year-old woman with rapidly progressive alopecia areata is distressed and withdrawing socially. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: Psychological support is one of the most important considerations, and support groups may be offered
src.explanation: Correct — it is named among the most important factors in managing this condition.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Chronic hand dermatitis from detergent exposure. Avoid the exposure and repair the barrier with emollients, sleeping in cotton gloves after applying a heavy emollient such as petroleum jelly, with antihistamines such as hydroxyzine or diphenhydramine for itch.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 82

src.question: A 44-year-old janitor has chronic dry, fissured, glazed dermatitis of both hands from repeated detergent exposure. Which is the most appropriate management?
src.key: Avoid the exposure and repair the barrier with emollients, sleeping in cotton gloves after applying a heavy emollient such as petroleum jelly
src.explanation: with antihistamines such as hydroxyzine or diphenhydramine for itch.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Transillumination. This bedside technique shows whether a soft subcutaneous nodule is fluid-filled: a fluid-filled lesion glows when a light is placed against it.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 25

src.question: A 47-year-old woman has a soft subcutaneous nodule on the forearm and the clinician wants to know whether it is fluid-filled. Which bedside technique addresses that?
src.key: Transillumination
src.explanation: Correct — a fluid-filled lesion glows when a light is placed against it.

items.section_title: 2.3 · Objective c — Vesiculobullous disease
items.html: Acantholysis. On biopsy of flaccid skin bullae with painful oral erosions, it is the defining histological feature: loss of keratinocyte-to-keratinocyte adhesion. Immunofluorescence and serum ELISA are confirmatory.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 132

src.question: A 58-year-old woman has painful oral erosions and flaccid skin bullae. A biopsy has been taken. Which finding on that biopsy would establish the diagnosis?
src.key: Acantholysis
src.explanation: Correct — loss of keratinocyte-to-keratinocyte adhesion is the defining histological feature, with immunofluorescence and serum ELISA confirmatory.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Stasis dermatitis with acute leg swelling. Acute unilateral swelling or pain should raise concern for deep venous thrombosis, so order venous duplex ultrasonography to evaluate for it.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 115

src.question: A 66-year-old woman with known bilateral stasis dermatitis develops acute swelling and pain in the right calf over two days. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Order venous duplex ultrasonography to evaluate for deep venous thrombosis
src.explanation: Acute unilateral swelling or pain should raise concern for deep venous thrombosis in this setting.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Childhood atopic dermatitis treatment. A flexural distribution (antecubital and popliteal fossae) with family atopy history is classic. Initial treatment is topical hydrocortisone with regular emollient use: a low-potency steroid plus barrier repair is first line.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 57

src.question: A 7-year-old boy is brought in with a recurrent, intensely pruritic rash in the antecubital and popliteal fossae. Examination shows poorly demarcated erythematous plaques with excoriations and lichenification (thickening with exaggerated skin lines). His mother has asthma. There is no fever, drainage, crusting or tenderness. Which is the most appropriate initial treatment?
src.key: Topical hydrocortisone with regular emollient use
src.explanation: Low-potency steroid plus barrier repair is first line, and the flexural distribution with a family atopy history is classic childhood atopic dermatitis.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Lichen planus counseling. Genital and erosive oral disease carry an increased risk of squamous cell carcinoma, so ongoing surveillance is needed. This is why mucosal involvement must be identified and followed.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 176

src.question: A 54-year-old woman has erosive oral and vulvar lichen planus. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: Genital and erosive oral disease carry an increased risk of squamous cell carcinoma, so ongoing surveillance is needed
src.explanation: Correct — this is the reason mucosal involvement must be identified and followed.

items.section_title: 2.6 · Common dermatologic pharmacology
items.html: Extensive or persistent perioral dermatitis. When it persists despite stopping the topical corticosteroid and simplifying the routine, treat with oral tetracycline or doxycycline.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 102

src.question: A 29-year-old woman has extensive perioral dermatitis that has persisted despite stopping her topical corticosteroid and simplifying her routine. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
src.key: Oral tetracycline or doxycycline
src.explanation: Correct — more extensive or persistent disease may require an oral tetracycline.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Allergic contact dermatitis to adhesives. A rash that reproduces the shape of the object is the hallmark. A rectangular rash sparing a central area reflects a reaction to the adhesive in the dressing, with the spared center corresponding to the cotton pad.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 86

src.question: A 26-year-old developed an itchy rash confined to a rectangle on her forearm, sparing a small central area, three days after a minor injury. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: The reaction is to the adhesive in the dressing, and the spared center corresponds to the cotton pad
src.explanation: Correct — the shape reproducing the object is the hallmark of allergic contact dermatitis to adhesives.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Nickel allergy. Nickel is the most common metal allergen, and eruptions reproduce the shape of the item worn, such as under a necklace or beneath a jeans button.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 85

src.question: A 35-year-old woman develops an itchy eruption under a new necklace and beneath the button of her jeans. Which allergen is most likely?
src.key: Nickel
src.explanation: Correct — nickel is the most common metal allergen, and eruptions reproduce the shape of the item worn.

items.section_title: 2.6 · Common dermatologic pharmacology
items.html: Reducing flares of recurrent palmar vesicles. Avoid irritants such as detergents, solvents and hair dyes, wash with lukewarm water and soap-free cleanser, dry hands thoroughly, and apply emollients immediately afterwards.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 66

src.question: A 31-year-old woman with recurrent palmar vesicles asks how to reduce flares. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: Avoid irritants such as detergents, solvents and hair dyes, wash with lukewarm water and soap-free cleanser, dry hands thoroughly, and apply emollients immediately afterwards
src.explanation: Correct — trigger avoidance and barrier care are the named education points.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Greasy scaling of the scalp and face. Initial treatment is ketoconazole shampoo and topical ketoconazole cream. Topical antifungals are the mainstay because Malassezia overgrowth drives the condition; steroids may be added early to reduce inflammation.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 95

src.question: A 34-year-old man has recurrent scaling of the scalp, eyebrows, nasolabial folds and external ears. Examination shows greasy, yellow-white scale over mildly erythematous poorly demarcated patches. Which is the most appropriate initial treatment?
src.key: Ketoconazole shampoo and topical ketoconazole cream
src.explanation: Topical antifungals are the mainstay because Malassezia overgrowth drives the condition; steroids may be added early to reduce inflammation.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Lichenoid eruption after a new medication. Review the medication list, since several drugs produce lichenoid reactions: nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, sulfonamides, tetracyclines, hydrochlorothiazide, quinidine and some beta blockers.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 173

src.question: A 58-year-old man develops an itchy violaceous papular eruption on his wrists two months after starting a new antihypertensive. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Review the medication list, since several drugs produce lichenoid reactions
src.explanation: Correct — nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, sulfonamides, tetracyclines, hydrochlorothiazide, quinidine and some beta blockers are named.

items.section_title: 2.6 · Common dermatologic pharmacology
items.html: Perioral dermatitis after stopping corticosteroid. The eruption may temporarily worsen after corticosteroid withdrawal before it improves. Telling the patient in advance stops her restarting the steroid.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 102

src.question: A 31-year-old woman with perioral dermatitis has stopped her topical corticosteroid. Which is the most appropriate counseling point about what happens next?
src.key: The eruption may temporarily worsen after corticosteroid withdrawal before it improves
src.explanation: Correct — telling her in advance is what stops her restarting the steroid.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Recurrent greasy scaling of the scalp and nasolabial folds. The condition is chronic and relapsing, so repeated and long-term use of medication is often required.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 95

src.question: A 40-year-old man with recurrent greasy scaling of the scalp and nasolabial folds asks how long treatment will be needed. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: The condition is chronic and relapsing, so repeated and long-term use of medication is often required
src.explanation: Correct — that expectation is stated explicitly for this condition.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Culture in atopic dermatitis. Bacterial culture is indicated for purulent, pustular or significantly crusted lesions, such as weeping, thickly crusted plaques with pustules, to rule out infection.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 56

src.question: A 5-year-old with atopic dermatitis has an area of weeping, thickly crusted plaques with pustules over a previously flaring elbow. She is afebrile. Which is the most appropriate diagnostic test?
src.key: Bacterial culture of the crusted lesions
src.explanation: Correct — culture is indicated for purulent, pustular or significantly crusted lesions to rule out infection.

items.section_title: 2.3 · Objective c — Vesiculobullous disease
items.html: Pemphigus treatment. Pemphigus is life-threatening, so treatment is urgent: rituximab or high-dose oral prednisone. A steroid-sparing agent is usually added so steroids can be tapered.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 133

src.question: A 55-year-old man with widespread flaccid bullae and painful oral erosions has a biopsy showing acantholysis. Which is the most appropriate initial treatment?
src.key: Rituximab or high-dose oral prednisone, given urgently
src.explanation: Correct — pemphigus is life-threatening, so treatment is urgent, and a steroid-sparing agent is usually added so steroids can be tapered.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Oval scaly plaque followed by smaller oval lesions down the trunk. Diagnosis is clinical, based on the herald patch and the typical pattern. The herald patch and cleavage-line distribution are enough.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 171

src.question: A 23-year-old man has an oval scaly plaque on his chest that appeared ten days ago, and now smaller oval lesions are spreading down his trunk. Which is the most appropriate initial diagnostic approach?
src.key: Clinical diagnosis based on the herald patch and the typical pattern
src.explanation: Correct — the herald patch and cleavage-line distribution are enough.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Common acquired melanocytic naevi natural history. They develop slowly after birth, enlarge symmetrically, stabilize and regress, peaking in number in the thirties and then declining. Melanoma risk rises with the number of lesions.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 35

src.question: Describe the natural history of common acquired melanocytic naevi.
src.key: They develop slowly after birth, enlarge symmetrically, stabilize and regress, peaking in number in the thirties then declining
src.explanation: Correct — melanoma risk rises with the number of lesions.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Seborrheic keratosis features. Dermoscopy shows comedone-like openings, with a stuck-on appearance clinically. Solar lentigo shows finger-like projections and a moth-eaten border instead.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 111

src.question: Which dermoscopic feature identifies a seborrheic keratosis?
src.key: Comedone-like openings, with a stuck-on appearance clinically
src.explanation: Correct — solar lentigo shows finger-like projections and a moth-eaten border instead.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Common acquired melanocytic naevi risk factors. They include ultraviolet radiation exposure, male sex, and a genetic component, with more lesions in light skin tones that sunburn. The number of lesions peaks in the thirties.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 35

src.question: Which risk factors are named for common acquired melanocytic naevi?
src.key: Ultraviolet radiation exposure, male sex, and a genetic component, with more lesions in light skin tones that sunburn
src.explanation: Correct — the number of lesions peaks in the thirties.

items.section_title: 8.1 · Objective a — Ephelides, lentigines and solar lentigo
items.html: Solar lentigo risk factors. They are older age, sun damage, a history of ephelides, tanning, and birth control use. Solar lentigines are common: 90% of people have them by the age of fifty.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 13

src.question: Which risk factors are named for solar lentigo?
src.key: Older age, sun damage, a history of ephelides, tanning, and birth control use
src.explanation: Correct — 90% of people have them by the age of fifty.

also.key: Birth control use is among the named associations, alongside older age, sun damage, ephelides and tanning
also.explanation: Correct — 90% of people have solar lentigines by the age of fifty.

items.section_title: 8.3 · Objective a — Vitiligo
items.html: Segmental versus non-segmental vitiligo. Distinguishing them matters because the two differ in their diagnostic tools and in their treatment. Segmental disease is unilateral, does not cross the midline, and follows block-like patterns.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 23

src.question: Why is it important to distinguish segmental from non-segmental vitiligo?
src.key: The two differ in their diagnostic tools and in their treatment
src.explanation: Correct — segmental disease is unilateral, does not cross the midline, and follows block-like patterns.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Numerous solar lentigines. Advise daily broad-spectrum sunscreen of SPF 30 or higher, with an annual full-body skin examination. Dermoscopic surveillance is added for atypical lesions.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 111

src.question: Which surveillance is advised for a patient with numerous solar lentigines?
src.key: Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen of SPF 30 or higher, with an annual full-body skin examination
src.explanation: Correct — dermoscopic surveillance is added for atypical lesions.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Naevus spilus. It is thought to arise from a somatic mutation and appears at birth or in the first years of life. It is a variant of congenital naevus.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 32

src.question: What is naevus spilus thought to arise from, and when does it appear?
src.key: A somatic mutation, appearing at birth or in the first years of life
src.explanation: Correct — it is a variant of congenital naevus.

items.section_title: 8.5 · Objective b — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Ephelides. Topical depigmenting agents named are hydroquinone, retinoids, alpha-hydroxy acids and botanicals, though sun protection and counseling remain the priority.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 7

src.question: Which topical depigmenting agents are named for ephelides?
src.key: Hydroquinone, retinoids, alpha-hydroxy acids and botanicals
src.explanation: though sun protection and counseling remain the priority.

items.section_title: 8.2 · Objective a — Seborrheic keratosis and dermatosis papulosa nigrans
items.html: Biopsy in dermatosis papulosa nigrans. Biopsy is indicated when the diagnosis is uncertain; the diagnosis is otherwise clinical.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 19

src.question: When is biopsy indicated in dermatosis papulosa nigrans?
src.key: When the diagnosis is uncertain
src.explanation: Correct — it is otherwise a clinical diagnosis.

also.key: Biopsy that lesion, since biopsy is indicated where the diagnosis is uncertain
also.explanation: Correct — the diagnosis is otherwise clinical.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Congenital melanocytic naevi. Neurofibromatosis type I is a named associated risk factor. Congenital naevi also carry a high risk of developing into melanoma.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 28

src.question: Which condition is named as a risk factor associated with congenital melanocytic naevi?
src.key: Neurofibromatosis type I
src.explanation: Correct — congenital naevi also carry a high risk of developing into melanoma.

items.section_title: 8.2 · Objective a — Seborrheic keratosis and dermatosis papulosa nigrans
items.html: Dermatosis papulosa nigrans counseling. The lesions are benign and best left untreated, with removal available for cosmetic reasons. Options are excision, curettage or laser, avoiding cryotherapy.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 19

src.question: A 50-year-old man of dark-skinned Asian background has facial papules typical of dermatosis papulosa nigrans and asks whether they will worsen. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: They are benign and best left untreated, with removal available if he wants it for cosmetic reasons
src.explanation: Correct — excision, curettage or laser are the options, avoiding cryotherapy.

items.section_title: 8.1 · Objective a — Ephelides, lentigines and solar lentigo
items.html: Asymptomatic, unchanged flat brown patches on the backs of the hands. No treatment is necessary; cosmetic removal by cryotherapy or quality-switched laser is offered only if the patient wishes. Treatment is elective, not indicated.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 12

src.question: A 63-year-old asks about the flat brown patches on the backs of her hands. They are asymptomatic and unchanged. What is the most appropriate management?
src.key: No treatment is necessary; cosmetic removal by cryotherapy or quality-switched laser only if she wishes
src.explanation: Correct — treatment is elective, not indicated.

items.section_title: 8.5 · Objective b — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Treating solar lentigines. Treatment is cosmetic; reducing skin cancer risk depends on sun protection and surveillance for other lesions. The lesions mark sun damage rather than causing the cancers associated with it.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 15

src.question: A 71-year-old man asks whether treating his solar lentigines will reduce his skin cancer risk. Which is the most appropriate response?
src.key: Treating them is cosmetic; reducing risk depends on sun protection and surveillance for other lesions
src.explanation: Correct — the lesions mark sun damage rather than causing the cancers associated with it.

items.section_title: 8.5 · Objective b — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Very large congenital naevus. Counseling and support groups for families and patients with large naevi are appropriate support, named alongside the surgical and observational decision.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 31

src.question: The parents of a child with a very large congenital naevus feel isolated and overwhelmed. Which support is appropriate?
src.key: Counseling and support groups for families and patients with large naevi
src.explanation: Correct — that is named alongside the surgical and observational decision.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Large congenital naevus with neurological symptoms. Seizures and vomiting with a large naevus over the head and neck indicate neurocutaneous melanosis, and the prognosis is poor once neurological symptoms appear. Symptoms usually appear within the first few years of life.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 29

src.question: An 11-month-old with a large congenital naevus over the head and neck develops seizures and vomiting. Which is the most appropriate interpretation?
src.key: Neurocutaneous melanosis has developed, and the prognosis is poor once neurological symptoms appear
src.explanation: Correct — symptoms usually appear within the first few years of life.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Large congenital naevus workup. Head, neck or posterior midline lesions raise neurocutaneous melanosis, so magnetic resonance imaging of the brain, with or without total spine, is required, matched to where the naevus sits.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 30

src.question: A newborn has a large pigmented patch across the posterior midline of the neck and upper back. What is required next?
src.key: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain, with or without total spine, matched to where the naevus sits
src.explanation: Correct — head, neck or posterior midline lesions raise neurocutaneous melanosis.

also.key: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain, with or without total spine, matched to the location of the naevus
also.explanation: Correct — the concern is neurocutaneous melanosis.

items.section_title: 8.2 · Objective a — Seborrheic keratosis and dermatosis papulosa nigrans
items.html: Cryotherapy in dermatosis papulosa nigrans. Cryotherapy is avoided in this condition because of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation. Excision, curettage or laser can be used where treatment is wanted.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 19

src.question: A 39-year-old Polynesian woman with facial papules asks why her doctor will not freeze them off as a friend had done elsewhere. Which is the most appropriate explanation?
src.key: Cryotherapy is avoided in this condition because of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation
src.explanation: Correct — excision, curettage or laser can be used where treatment is wanted.

items.section_title: 8.2 · Objective a — Seborrheic keratosis and dermatosis papulosa nigrans
items.html: Multiple dark warty growths in older adults. They are benign and common in older adults, and the diagnosis is clinical without any need for biopsy. Cryotherapy helps if a lesion becomes itchy or inflamed, though it may recur.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 17

src.question: A 79-year-old man's family are alarmed by dozens of dark warty growths that appeared on his back over two years. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: They are benign, common in older adults, and the diagnosis is clinical without any need for biopsy
src.explanation: Correct — cryotherapy helps if a lesion becomes itchy or inflamed, though it may recur.

items.section_title: 8.3 · Objective a — Vitiligo
items.html: Psychosocial impact of vitiligo. The psychological and social impact is real, and psychological intervention is part of management. Low self-esteem and poor body image are named explicitly.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 21

src.question: A 26-year-old man with vitiligo says he has stopped going out because of how his skin looks, and that his doctor called it purely cosmetic. Which is the most appropriate response?
src.key: The psychological and social impact is real, and psychological intervention is part of management
src.explanation: Correct — low self-esteem and poor body image are named explicitly.

items.section_title: 8.5 · Objective b — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Cryotherapy of seborrheic keratosis. Tell the patient beforehand that the lesion can come back after freezing, so she is not surprised or disappointed later.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 15

src.question: A 69-year-old woman is about to have an irritated seborrheic keratosis frozen. What should she be told beforehand?
src.key: That the lesion can come back after freezing, so she is not surprised or disappointed later
src.explanation: Correct — seborrheic keratoses can recur after cryotherapy, so warning her beforehand keeps her from being surprised or disappointed if one returns.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Numerous dysplastic naevi counseling. Between visits, use sun protection and report any lesion that changes or is newly developing. Management is observation, biopsy of changing lesions and excision where melanoma is a concern.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: A 52-year-old man with numerous dysplastic naevi asks what he should do between clinic visits. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: Use sun protection and report any lesion that changes or is newly developing
src.explanation: Correct — management is observation, biopsy of changing lesions and excision where melanoma is a concern.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Removing a melanocytic naevus. Removal for symptomatic or cosmetic reasons is reasonable, alongside sun protection counseling. The diagnosis is clinical and management is otherwise observation.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 37

src.question: A 38-year-old woman wants a mole on her back removed because her bra strap catches it. Which is the most appropriate response?
src.key: Removal for symptomatic or cosmetic reasons is reasonable, alongside sun protection counseling
src.explanation: Correct — the diagnosis is clinical and management is otherwise observation.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma versus psoriasis, eczema and tinea. Discriminators are chronicity, treatment resistance, large or oddly distributed patches, severe pruritus, follicular hair loss, tumors or erythroderma, nodes, and histology over time. No single one settles it, so longitudinal reassessment is stressed.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 74

src.question: Which discriminators separate cutaneous T-cell lymphoma from psoriasis, eczema and tinea?
src.key: Chronicity, treatment resistance, large or oddly distributed patches, severe pruritus, follicular hair loss, tumors or erythroderma, nodes, and histology over time
src.explanation: Correct — no single one settles it, which is why longitudinal reassessment is stressed.

items.section_title: 9.3 · Objective 1 — Squamous cell carcinoma
items.html: Squamous cell carcinoma pathology report. It should identify differentiation grade, depth or thickness, perineural or perivascular invasion, margin status, and aggressive subtype. Each feeds the decision about Mohs and about follow-up.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 23

src.question: Which five features should the pathology report identify in a squamous cell carcinoma?
src.key: Differentiation grade, depth or thickness, perineural or perivascular invasion, margin status, and aggressive subtype
src.explanation: Correct — all five, and each of them feeds the decision about Mohs and about follow-up.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Procedures in Kaposi sarcoma. Bronchoscopy is for suspected pulmonary disease, and endoscopy is driven by symptoms or management rather than done routinely in asymptomatic patients. A chest radiograph is used when pulmonary involvement is possible.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 65

src.question: Which directed procedures are reserved for symptomatic Kaposi sarcoma rather than performed routinely?
src.key: Bronchoscopy for suspected pulmonary disease, and endoscopy driven by symptoms or management rather than routinely in asymptomatic patients
src.explanation: Correct — a chest radiograph is used when pulmonary involvement is possible, but scoping is not routine.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Antiretroviral therapy in Kaposi sarcoma. Patients must be told the lesions may worsen early, as immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome. Warning them beforehand stops early worsening being read as treatment failure.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 67

src.question: What must a patient starting antiretroviral therapy for Kaposi sarcoma be told?
src.key: That the lesions may worsen early, as immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome
src.explanation: Correct — warning them beforehand stops early worsening being read as treatment failure.

items.section_title: 9.2 · Objective 1 — Actinic keratosis
items.html: Actinic keratosis biopsy. Morphology or behavior raising concern for squamous cell carcinoma, or persistence or recurrence after therapy, prompts biopsy. A shave or punch biopsy is used.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 13

src.question: What triggers a biopsy of an actinic keratosis, and which technique is used?
src.key: Morphology or behavior raising concern for squamous cell carcinoma, or persistence or recurrence after therapy; shave or punch biopsy
src.explanation: Correct — concern for squamous cell carcinoma, or persistence or recurrence after therapy, prompts a shave or punch biopsy.

items.section_title: 9.2 · Objective 1 — Actinic keratosis
items.html: Fate of an actinic keratosis. An individual lesion may persist, involute, recur, or progress, so individual lesion behavior is unpredictable.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 15

src.question: What are the four possible fates of an individual actinic keratosis?
src.key: It may persist, involute, recur, or progress
src.explanation: Correct — including involution, which is why individual lesion behavior is unpredictable.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Biopsy site in suspected cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Select an active, representative, untreated lesion, coordinating with dermatopathology. Treating a lesion first can obscure the histology being read.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 74

src.question: Which lesion should be selected for skin biopsy in suspected cutaneous T-cell lymphoma?
src.key: An active, representative, UNTREATED lesion, coordinating with dermatopathology
src.explanation: Correct — treating a lesion first can obscure the very histology you are trying to read.

items.section_title: 9.4 · Objective 1 — Basal cell carcinoma
items.html: Sampling basal cell carcinoma. A suspected lesion is sampled with a shave or punch biopsy to confirm the diagnosis. Pathology then determines the histologic subtype, which dictates treatment.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 36

src.question: How should a suspected basal cell carcinoma be sampled?
src.key: With a shave or punch biopsy, to confirm the diagnosis
src.explanation: Correct — and the pathology then determines the histologic subtype, which dictates treatment.

items.section_title: 9.8 · Objective 11 — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Single persistent nail abnormality. Avoid repeated empiric antifungal, antibiotic or wart treatment when the abnormality persists despite treatment. Repeating empiric therapy on a solitary persistent nail lesion is how diagnostic delay happens.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 95

src.question: A single nail abnormality has persisted despite treatment. What must be avoided?
src.key: Repeated empiric antifungal, antibiotic or wart treatment
src.explanation: Correct — repeating empiric therapy on a solitary persistent nail lesion is how diagnostic delay happens.

items.section_title: 9.4 · Objective 1 — Basal cell carcinoma
items.html: Basal cell carcinoma in immunosuppression. It is more common and more likely to recur after non-Hodgkin lymphoma, solid-organ transplant, or allogeneic stem cell transplant.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 33

src.question: In which three immunosuppressed groups is basal cell carcinoma more common and more likely to recur?
