src.key: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma, solid-organ transplant, and allogeneic stem cell transplant
src.explanation: Correct — basal cell carcinoma is more common and more likely to recur after non-Hodgkin lymphoma, solid-organ transplant or allogeneic stem cell transplant.

items.section_title: 9.3 · Objective 1 — Squamous cell carcinoma
items.html: Regional assessment in squamous cell carcinoma. Alongside biopsy, palpate the draining lymph-node basins, considering imaging or nodal evaluation for high-risk tumors. The nodes are examined at diagnosis, not only at follow-up.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 23

src.question: What regional assessment goes alongside biopsy of a squamous cell carcinoma?
src.key: Palpate the draining lymph-node basins, considering imaging or nodal evaluation for high-risk tumors
src.explanation: Correct — the nodes are examined at diagnosis, not only at follow-up.

items.section_title: 9.2 · Objective 1 — Actinic keratosis
items.html: Actinic keratosis field therapy. Warn patients to expect erythema and crusting, and stress adherence to the full treatment duration. Patients who are not warned stop the course early.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 15

src.question: Which local reactions should an actinic keratosis patient be warned to expect from field therapy?
src.key: Erythema and crusting, alongside adherence to the full treatment duration
src.explanation: Correct — patients who are not warned stop the course early.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Establishing cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Patients should be told the diagnosis may require repeated biopsies and the disease is usually chronic. Setting that expectation early matters, because the diagnosis is often slow to confirm.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 76

src.question: What should patients be told about establishing the cutaneous T-cell lymphoma diagnosis?
src.key: It may require repeated biopsies, and the disease is usually chronic
src.explanation: Correct — setting that expectation early matters, because the diagnosis is often slow to confirm.

items.section_title: 9.8 · Objective 11 — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Follow-up after squamous cell carcinoma. Examine skin and lymph nodes at least annually, with closer intervals if the patient is high-risk or immunosuppressed. The interval tightens rather than the examination changing.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 26

src.question: How often should a patient treated for squamous cell carcinoma be examined, and how does immunosuppression change it?
src.key: At least annual skin and lymph-node examination, with closer intervals if high-risk or immunosuppressed
src.explanation: Correct — the interval tightens rather than the examination changing.

items.section_title: 9.4 · Objective 1 — Basal cell carcinoma
items.html: Imaging in basal cell carcinoma. Routine imaging is not needed in typical localized disease; it is reserved for advanced, deeply invasive or metastatic disease. That specialist-directed workup is the exception rather than the rule.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 36

src.question: What is the role of imaging in typical localized basal cell carcinoma?
src.key: Routine imaging is not needed; it is reserved for advanced, deeply invasive or metastatic disease
src.explanation: Correct — and that specialist-directed workup is the exception rather than the rule.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Regression of Kaposi sarcoma. Iatrogenic disease may regress when immunosuppression is reduced, which is why the transplant team is consulted before any reduction.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 67

src.question: Which Kaposi sarcoma form may REGRESS, and what makes it do so?
src.key: Iatrogenic disease, which may regress when immunosuppression is reduced
src.explanation: Correct — which is why the transplant team is consulted before any reduction.

items.section_title: 9.8 · Objective 11 — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Photographing a concerning pigmented band. Do not let photographing it delay referral. Documentation is for tracking change, not for postponing the specialist.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 95

src.question: A concerning pigmented band should be photographed. What caution comes with that?
src.key: Do not let photographing it delay referral
src.explanation: Correct — documentation is for tracking change, not for postponing the specialist.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Kaposi sarcoma versus lookalikes. It is told apart from bacillary angiomatosis, hemangioma and other violaceous lesions by immune status, distribution, oral lesions, edema, visceral symptoms and biopsy, not color alone.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 65

src.question: Which features discriminate Kaposi sarcoma from its lookalikes?
src.key: Immune status, distribution, oral lesions, edema, visceral symptoms and biopsy — not color alone
src.explanation: Correct — Kaposi sarcoma is told apart from bacillary angiomatosis, hemangioma and other violaceous lesions by immune status, distribution, oral lesions, edema, visceral symptoms and biopsy.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Immune context in suspected Kaposi sarcoma. Test for human immunodeficiency virus if status is unknown; if known, assess CD4 count, viral load, antiretroviral history and adherence. Knowing the status is not enough; the degree of immune suppression matters.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 65

src.question: How is the immune context defined once Kaposi sarcoma is suspected?
src.key: Test for human immunodeficiency virus if status is unknown; if known, assess CD4 count, viral load, antiretroviral history and adherence
src.explanation: Correct — knowing the status is not enough, the degree of immune suppression matters.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Blood tests in advanced cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. They are complete blood count with differential, eosinophilia, circulating Sezary cells, T-cell gene-rearrangement testing and specialist flow cytometry. These belong to advanced disease rather than the initial skin diagnosis.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 74

src.question: Which blood tests apply in ADVANCED cutaneous T-cell lymphoma?
src.key: Complete blood count with differential, eosinophilia, circulating Sezary cells, T-cell gene-rearrangement testing and specialist flow cytometry
src.explanation: Correct — these belong to advanced disease rather than to the initial skin diagnosis.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Nondiagnostic biopsy in suspected cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. A single nondiagnostic biopsy does not exclude the disease; correlate clinically and reassess over time. Numerous biopsies may be needed.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 74

src.question: A biopsy for suspected cutaneous T-cell lymphoma comes back nondiagnostic, but the clinical picture still fits. What follows?
src.key: A single nondiagnostic biopsy does not exclude the disease; correlate clinically and reassess over time
src.explanation: Correct — and numerous biopsies may be needed, which is why patients are warned in advance.

items.section_title: 7.5 · Objective a — The nodules that must be told from a cancer
items.html: Squamous cell carcinoma prevention in transplant recipients. Nicotinamide five hundred milligrams twice daily reduces new squamous cell carcinoma by about thirty percent in high-risk patients.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 21

src.question: A kidney transplant recipient has had two squamous cell carcinomas removed this year. He asks whether anything can lower his chances of getting more. What do you tell him?
src.key: Nicotinamide five hundred milligrams twice daily reduces new squamous cell carcinoma by about thirty percent in high-risk patients
src.explanation: Correct — and it is specifically described as a strategy for transplant recipients.

items.section_title: 9.5 · Objective 1 — Malignant melanoma
items.html: Melanoma with nodal spread. Nodal spread, such as a positive sentinel node, is an explicit referral trigger to an expert center for coordinated dermatology and surgical oncology care. Nodal or other-site spread crosses the threshold regardless of thickness.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 52

src.question: A 52-year-old woman has a pigmented lesion excised, reported as melanoma with a positive sentinel node. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Refer to an expert center, since nodal spread is an explicit referral trigger and coordinated dermatology and surgical oncology care is warranted
src.explanation: Correct — nodal or other-site spread crosses the threshold regardless of thickness.

items.section_title: 9.3 · Objective 1 — Squamous cell carcinoma
items.html: Squamous cell carcinoma biopsy requirement. The sample must allow the pathologist to determine whether the disease is in situ or invasive, along with the histologic risk features. Sufficient depth makes that distinction possible.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 23

src.question: A 70-year-old transplant recipient has a firm nodule on his lower lip. You are arranging a biopsy. What must the sample allow the pathologist to determine?
src.key: Whether the disease is in situ or invasive, along with the histologic risk features
src.explanation: Correct — sufficient depth is what makes that distinction possible, and it changes everything downstream.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Enlarged nodes in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. They may be benign dermatopathic change or lymphoma involvement, and require directed biopsy or imaging to distinguish. Enlargement alone does not establish spread.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 70

src.question: A patient with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma develops enlarged inguinal nodes. What might these represent, and what is required?
src.key: They may be benign dermatopathic change or lymphoma involvement, and require directed biopsy or imaging to distinguish
src.explanation: Correct — enlargement alone does not establish spread.

items.section_title: 9.8 · Objective 11 — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Neurologic symptoms after squamous cell carcinoma. New numbness and tingling in the distribution of the scar are an urgent referral trigger, since they raise concern for perineural invasion.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 26

src.question: A patient treated for squamous cell carcinoma of the scalp returns with new numbness and tingling in the distribution of the scar. Which is the most appropriate response?
src.key: Refer urgently, because neurologic symptoms are an urgent referral trigger
src.explanation: Correct — they raise concern for perineural invasion.

items.section_title: 9.5 · Objective 1 — Malignant melanoma
items.html: Suspicious pigmented lesion. The initial diagnostic test is biopsy or excision to confirm the diagnosis. Tissue is required before staging decisions.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 49

src.question: A 45-year-old patient has a suspicious pigmented lesion that needs sampling. What is the initial diagnostic test?
src.key: Biopsy or excision to confirm the diagnosis
src.explanation: Correct — tissue is required before staging decisions.

items.section_title: 9.2 · Objective 1 — Actinic keratosis
items.html: Actinic keratosis recurring after therapy. Persistence or recurrence after therapy is a biopsy trigger, so take a shave or punch biopsy. Recurrence plus induration is exactly what should prompt sampling.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 13

src.question: A 74-year-old has had a scaly patch on his temple treated with cryotherapy twice over eight months, and it has come back again. It is now slightly firm to the touch. What is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Take a shave or punch biopsy, because persistence or recurrence after therapy is a biopsy trigger
src.explanation: Correct — recurrence after treatment, plus induration, is exactly what should prompt sampling.

items.section_title: 7.7 · Objectives a & b — Neurofibromatosis, and the remaining lesions
items.html: Xanthelasma. A collection of lipid-laden macrophages forming soft yellow cholesterol plaques, most commonly on the medial eyelids; it is asymptomatic.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 104

src.question: What is xanthelasma made of, and where does it sit?
src.key: A collection of lipid-laden macrophages forming soft yellow cholesterol plaques, most commonly on the medial eyelids
src.explanation: Correct — and it is asymptomatic.

items.section_title: 7.1 · Objective a — Corns, calluses, and the wart that mimics them
items.html: Corn and callus management. Use padding and avoid poorly fitting footwear, with over-the-counter keratolytic products: remove the pressure first, then thin the keratin.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 9

src.question: How are corns and calluses managed?
src.key: Padding and avoiding poorly fitting footwear, with over-the-counter keratolytic products
src.explanation: Correct — remove the pressure first, then thin the keratin.

items.section_title: 7.1 · Objective a — Corns, calluses, and the wart that mimics them
items.html: Clavus (corn). Mechanical trauma such as ill-fitting shoes causes hyperkeratosis with a cone-shaped central core of hard keratin pointing into the skin; the central core separates a corn from a callus.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 4

src.question: What produces a clavus, and what does the pressure create?
src.key: Mechanical trauma such as ill-fitting shoes, causing hyperkeratosis with a cone-shaped central core of hard keratin pointing into the skin
src.explanation: Correct — the central core is what separates a corn from a callus.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: Pyogenic granuloma education. It is benign and often resolves over months to years; treatment is available if wanted, for cosmetic reasons or to prevent bleeding. If it recurs, early follow-up is appropriate because small lesions are easier to treat than large ones.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 96

src.question: What should a patient with a pyogenic granuloma be told?
src.key: It is benign and often resolves over months to years; treatment is available if wanted
src.explanation: Correct — treatments exist for cosmetic reasons or to prevent bleeding. If it recurs, early follow-up is appropriate, because small lesions are easier to treat than large ones.

items.section_title: 7.4 · Objective a — Pressure injury and pilonidal disease
items.html: Pilonidal disease presentation. Acutely, sudden pain and swelling in or along the gluteal cleft; chronically, recurrent drainage and pain from one or more sinus tracts. A hair may occasionally be seen protruding from a sinus opening.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 40

src.question: How does an acute pilonidal abscess present, and how does chronic disease present?
src.key: Acutely, sudden pain and swelling in or along the gluteal cleft; chronically, recurrent drainage and pain from one or more sinus tracts
src.explanation: Correct — a hair may occasionally be seen protruding from a sinus opening.

items.section_title: 7.7 · Objectives a & b — Neurofibromatosis, and the remaining lesions
items.html: New lesion in a sun-exposed area. It is an opening to counsel on sunscreen, sun avoidance at peak hours and skin checks, as general skin-cancer education.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 112

src.question: What opportunity does a new lesion in a sun-exposed area create?
src.key: To counsel on sunscreen, peak-hour sun avoidance and skin checks
src.explanation: Correct — any new sun-exposed lesion is an opening for general skin-cancer education.

also.key: Sunscreen, sun avoidance at peak hours, and skin checks
also.explanation: Correct — any new sun-exposed lesion is an opening for general skin-cancer education.

items.section_title: 7.7 · Objectives a & b — Neurofibromatosis, and the remaining lesions
items.html: Lipoma. Soft, painless, rubbery subcutaneous nodules, usually under five centimeters, that can occur anywhere on the body; asymptomatic unless adjoining structures are invaded.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 105

src.question: What does a lipoma feel like, and when does it cause symptoms?
src.key: Soft painless subcutaneous nodules, rubbery, usually under five centimeters
src.explanation: Correct — asymptomatic unless adjoining structures are invaded, and it can occur anywhere on the body.

items.section_title: 7.3 · Objective a — Cutaneous horn and skin tags
items.html: Skin tags. Increased in females and obese patients, in areas of friction such as the neck, axilla and groin; very common, present in sixty percent of people by age seventy.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 29

src.question: In whom and where do skin tags occur, and how common are they?
src.key: Increased in females and obese patients, in areas of friction such as the neck, axilla and groin; present in sixty percent of people by age seventy
src.explanation: Correct — very common, and increasingly so with age.

items.section_title: 7.5 · Objective a — The nodules that must be told from a cancer
items.html: Keratoacanthoma risk factors. Age over forty, sun exposure, very fair skin that always burns and never tans, male sex, tattoos with red ink, skin trauma such as lasers, surgery or cryotherapy, and human papillomavirus infection.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 49

src.question: Which risk factors are listed for keratoacanthoma?
src.key: Age over forty, sun exposure, very fair skin that always burns and never tans, male sex, tattoos with red ink, skin trauma such as lasers, surgery or cryotherapy, and human papillomavirus infection
src.explanation: Correct — the red ink and the iatrogenic trauma are the unexpected ones.

items.section_title: 7.1 · Objective a — Corns, calluses, and the wart that mimics them
items.html: Painful corn with diabetes mellitus. A diabetic foot lesion goes to podiatry: refer the patient to podiatry.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 9

src.question: A 63-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus has a painful corn on his fifth toe. Which is the most appropriate management?
src.key: Refer him to podiatry
src.explanation: Correct — a diabetic foot lesion goes to podiatry.

items.section_title: 7.2 · Objective a — Abnormal wound healing: keloid and hypertrophic scar
items.html: Silicone sheets for keloid. They are worn twelve to twenty-four hours a day for up to a year, theorized to raise scar temperature and increase collagenase activity.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 16

src.question: A 35-year-old with a keloid asks about the silicone sheets a friend used. Which is the most appropriate description of how they are used?
src.key: Worn twelve to twenty-four hours a day for up to a year
src.explanation: Correct — theorized to raise scar temperature and increase collagenase activity.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Objective d — Discuss clinical principles and decision-making
items.html: Clinical guideline. A clinical guideline following an if-then rule, for example: if a patient is febrile and neutropenic, then use broad-spectrum antibiotics.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 23

src.question: "If a patient is febrile and neutropenic, then use broad-spectrum antibiotics" is given as an example of what?
src.key: A clinical guideline following an if-then rule
src.explanation: That is a guideline built on an if-then rule.

items.section_title: 1.2 · Objectives b & c — Define pretest and posttest probability
items.html: Posttest probability. Posttest probability is the likelihood after the result is known, the pretest likelihood revised by the test's sensitivity and specificity; with identical tests, different pretest probabilities give different posttest probabilities.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 9

src.question: Two clinicians order the same test with identical sensitivity and specificity, for two patients whose pretest probabilities differ substantially. What follows?
src.key: Their posttest probabilities will differ, because posttest probability builds on the pretest estimate
src.explanation: Posttest probability is the likelihood after the result is known, and it is the pretest likelihood revised by the test's sensitivity and specificity.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Objective d — Discuss clinical principles and decision-making
items.html: Three questions a clinician must answer. What disease is present, should testing be done, and should this patient be treated. Which clinician should take over the patient's care is not among them.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 13

src.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three questions a clinician must answer?
src.key: Which clinician should take over the patient's care?
src.explanation: The three questions are what disease, should testing be done, and should this patient be treated. Transfer of care is not among them.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Objective d — Discuss clinical principles and decision-making
items.html: Clinical decision making. Setting the sensitivity and specificity of the tests available is not part of it; these are fixed properties of a test, not decisions a clinician makes at the bedside.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 12

src.question: Clinical decision making covers all of the following EXCEPT which?
src.key: Setting the sensitivity and specificity of the tests available
src.explanation: Sensitivity and specificity are fixed properties of a test, not decisions a clinician makes at the bedside.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Objective d — Discuss clinical principles and decision-making
items.html: Clinical guideline caution. Guidelines are straightforward and easy to use but should be applied to patients with similar characteristics to those studied.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 23

src.question: Which caution applies to the use of clinical guidelines?
src.key: They should be applied to patients with similar characteristics to those studied
src.explanation: Guidelines are described as straightforward and easy to use but should be applied to patients with similar characteristics.

items.section_title: 1.5 · Objective e — Discuss the naturalistic approach
items.html: Naturalistic (event-driven) approach. It is characterized by treating signs and symptoms before a definitive diagnosis is reached.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 24

src.question: The naturalistic (event-driven) approach is characterized by which practice?
src.key: Treating signs and symptoms before a definitive diagnosis is reached
src.explanation: The naturalistic, event-driven approach treats signs and symptoms before a definitive diagnosis.

items.section_title: 1.1 · Objective a — Compare and contrast sensitivity and specificity
items.html: False-positives in human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) screening. A few are acceptable because they can be corrected by later confirmatory testing, whereas a missed case may unknowingly infect others.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 8

src.question: Why are a few false-positives acceptable when screening for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)?
src.key: Because they can be corrected by later confirmatory testing, whereas a missed case may unknowingly infect others
src.explanation: A correctable false-positive weighs less than failing to identify someone who might unknowingly infect others.

items.section_title: 8.3 · Objective a — Vitiligo
items.html: Vitiligo treatment. Phototherapy with narrow band ultraviolet B, ideally combined with topical therapy, is preferred over PUVA, which carries adverse effects including increased skin cancer risk.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 25

src.question: A 31-year-old man has vitiligo affecting roughly 20% of his body surface. Which is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
src.key: Phototherapy with narrow band ultraviolet B, ideally combined with topical therapy
src.explanation: Correct — narrow band ultraviolet B is preferred over PUVA, which raises skin cancer risk.

also.key: Narrow band ultraviolet B is preferred, because PUVA carries adverse effects including increased skin cancer risk
also.explanation: Correct — combining phototherapy with topical therapy is described as ideal.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Recurrent head lice. Use a multimodal approach combining physical methods with adjuvant chemical therapy, because of increasing resistance.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 30

src.question: Head lice have recurred after two pediculicide courses. Which approach is described?
src.key: A multimodal approach combining physical methods with adjuvant chemical therapy
src.explanation: Correct — increasing resistance is the stated reason.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Kaposi sarcoma in a transplant recipient. Reduce immunosuppressive medication doses where clinically feasible, coordinating with the transplant team before making any change.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 66

src.question: A 61-year-old kidney transplant recipient develops Kaposi sarcoma. Which is the most appropriate management step, and what caution applies?
src.key: Reduce immunosuppressive medication doses where clinically feasible, coordinating with the transplant team before making any change
src.explanation: Correct — the transplant team must be involved before doses change.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Early acute paronychia. With erythema and tenderness but no fluctuance, treat with warm water soaks for twenty minutes three times daily; incision and drainage is reserved for severe cases with purulent collection.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 119

src.question: A 35-year-old man has early acute paronychia with erythema and tenderness but no fluctuance. Which is the most appropriate initial treatment?
src.key: Warm water soaks for twenty minutes three times daily
src.explanation: Incision and drainage is reserved for severe cases with purulent collection.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Head lice and school. After treatment a child can return to school now; a no-nit policy is not recommended because of the school absence it causes, a position from the American Academy of Pediatrics.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 30

src.question: The parent of an 8-year-old treated for head lice asks when she can return to school. Which is the most appropriate response?
src.key: She can return now — a no-nit policy is not recommended because of the school absence it causes
src.explanation: Correct — that position comes from the American Academy of Pediatrics.

items.section_title: 8.2 · Objective a — Seborrheic keratosis and dermatosis papulosa nigrans
items.html: Symptomatic seborrheic keratosis. An itchy, inflamed lesion can be treated with cryotherapy, though the lesion may recur afterwards; asymptomatic lesions need no treatment at all.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 17

src.question: A 68-year-old man has one seborrheic keratosis on the back that has become itchy and inflamed where his belt rubs. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
src.key: Cryotherapy, though the lesion may recur afterwards
src.explanation: Correct — asymptomatic lesions need no treatment at all.

items.section_title: 9.5 · Objective 1 — Malignant melanoma
items.html: Small suspicious pigmented lesions. An asymmetric lesion with an irregular border that is darkening should be biopsied or excised, because smaller lesions can still be melanoma; the 6 mm figure is a prompt, not a rule-out.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 46

src.question: A 39-year-old has a 4 mm pigmented lesion that is asymmetric with an irregular border and has darkened over three months. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Biopsy or excise it, because smaller lesions can still be melanoma
src.explanation: Correct — the 6 mm figure is a prompt, not a rule-out.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Cellulitis. It involves the deeper dermis and subcutaneous tissue, from Group A streptococci or Staphylococcus aureus; it may be purulent or non-purulent, which changes the antibiotic choice.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 105

src.question: Which layers does cellulitis involve, and which organisms cause it?
src.key: The deeper dermis and subcutaneous tissue, from Group A streptococci or Staphylococcus aureus
src.explanation: It may be purulent or non-purulent, which changes the antibiotic choice.

items.section_title: 5.2 · Objective a — Bedbugs, fleas, stings and caterpillars
items.html: After sting-induced anaphylaxis. Carry an epinephrine auto-injector, and be referred for desensitization therapy where the skin test is positive; immunotherapy is specified for fire ant hypersensitivity.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: Which long-term measures are offered after a sting-induced anaphylactic reaction?
src.key: Carry an epinephrine auto-injector, and desensitization therapy where the skin test is positive
src.explanation: Correct — immunotherapy is specified for fire ant hypersensitivity.

also.key: Carry an epinephrine auto-injector and be referred for desensitization therapy
also.explanation: Correct — immunotherapy is specified for fire ant hypersensitivity as well.

items.section_title: 5.3 · Objective a — Cutaneous larva migrans and cercarial dermatitis
items.html: Cercarial dermatitis epidemiology. Particularly affects the Great Lakes region, and paddy workers and rice farmers of the Far East; all share exposure to cercaria-infested water.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 89

src.question: Which populations and regions are particularly affected by cercarial dermatitis?
src.key: The Great Lakes region, and paddy workers and rice farmers of the Far East
src.explanation: Correct — exposure to cercaria-infested water is what all of them share.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Body louse infestation. Typically found in homeless people, refugees, war victims and those in crowded conditions, persisting via unwashed clothing; transmission is through contaminated clothing and bedding.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 24

src.question: In whom is body louse infestation typically found, and how does it persist?
src.key: Homeless people, refugees, war victims and those in crowded conditions, persisting via unwashed clothing
src.explanation: Correct — transmission is through contaminated clothing and bedding.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Objective a — Tick-borne illness
items.html: Rocky Mountain spotted fever treatment. Doxycycline is used for adults, pregnant patients and children, with desensitization where it is contraindicated.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 86

src.question: How is Rocky Mountain spotted fever treated, including in pregnancy and young children?
src.key: Doxycycline for adults, pregnant patients and children, with desensitization where it is contraindicated
src.explanation: Correct — 100 mg twice daily for adults and 2.2 mg per kilogram twice daily for children, for 5 to 10 days.

items.section_title: 6.6 · Objective b — Herpes simplex and herpetic whitlow
items.html: Low-positive herpes simplex type 2 serology. Confirm it with a second method when one is available, because low-positive results may be false positives.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 123

src.question: What should be done with a low-positive herpes simplex type 2 serology result?
src.key: Confirm it with a second method when one is available
src.explanation: Correct — low-positive results may be false positives.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Oral agents for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infection. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, clindamycin and doxycycline recur as the core options, with linezolid added in particular settings; fluoroquinolones such as ciprofloxacin are not reliable against it.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 66

src.question: Which trait is shared by the oral agents used for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infection?
src.key: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, clindamycin and doxycycline recur as the core options
src.explanation: with linezolid added in particular settings; fluoroquinolones such as ciprofloxacin are not reliable against it.

items.section_title: 3.3 · Objective a — Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
items.html: SCORTEN in toxic epidermal necrolysis. Age, malignancy, heart rate, detachment, urea and bicarbonate each score; a SCORTEN of 6 indicates a predicted mortality of about 90%.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 89

src.question: A 58-year-old woman is admitted with toxic epidermal necrolysis. She has a known lymphoma, a heart rate of 132, detachment of 35% of her body surface, blood urea nitrogen of 34 mg/dL, bicarbonate of 17 mEq/L and glucose of 190 mg/dL. Which score should be calculated and what does it indicate?
src.key: A SCORTEN of 6, indicating a predicted mortality of about 90%
src.explanation: Correct — age, malignancy, heart rate, detachment, urea and bicarbonate each score, and glucose is below threshold.

items.section_title: 6.7 · Objective b — Molluscum contagiosum and warts
items.html: Plantar warts. They occur on weight-bearing surfaces, and clustered together they form a mosaic wart.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 145

src.question: Where do plantar warts occur, and what do they form when they cluster?
src.key: On weight-bearing surfaces, and clustered together they form a mosaic wart
src.explanation: Correct — mosaic warts are clustered plantar warts.

items.section_title: 8.3 · Objective a — Vitiligo
items.html: Vitiligo above five percent of body surface. Narrow-band ultraviolet B phototherapy is first line, ideally combined with topical therapy.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 25

src.question: A 35-year-old man has vitiligo affecting about fifteen percent of his body surface. He has used topical steroids without benefit. What is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Narrow-band ultraviolet B phototherapy, ideally combined with topical therapy
src.explanation: Correct — phototherapy is first line above five percent, and combination therapy is described as ideal.

items.section_title: 8.1 · Objective a — Ephelides, lentigines and solar lentigo
items.html: Forms of lentigines. Lentigo simplex, acral lentigo, agminated lentigo and generalized lentigo; they follow a bimodal age distribution.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 9

src.question: Which forms of lentigines are named?
src.key: Lentigo simplex, acral lentigo, agminated lentigo and generalized lentigo
src.explanation: Correct — they follow a bimodal age distribution.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Scabies recovery. Most patients feel relief in about three days, though rash and itch may last up to four weeks; triamcinolone can be used for the residual itch.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 19

src.question: How soon do most patients feel relief after scabies treatment, and how long may symptoms linger?
src.key: Relief in about three days, though rash and itch may last up to four weeks
src.explanation: Correct — triamcinolone can be used for the residual itch.

items.section_title: 8.5 · Objective b — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Removing seborrheic keratoses. Treatment is not necessary; removal is elective, for cosmetic or symptomatic reasons, using retinoids, cryotherapy or quality-switched laser.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 15

src.question: A 70-year-old man wants several waxy stuck-on lesions on his trunk removed because they catch on his clothing. Which options are available?
src.key: Retinoids, cryotherapy or quality-switched laser, since removal here is elective
src.explanation: Correct — treatment is not necessary; removal is for cosmetic or symptomatic reasons.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Objective a — Tick-borne illness
items.html: Suspected Rocky Mountain spotted fever. Start doxycycline now without waiting for serology, since treatment should begin by day 5 and the indirect immunofluorescence assay is rarely diagnostic before day 7.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 85

src.question: A 50-year-old woman with suspected Rocky Mountain spotted fever is on day 4 of illness. The indirect immunofluorescence assay has been sent. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Start doxycycline now, since treatment should begin by day 5 and the assay is rarely diagnostic before day 7
src.explanation: Correct — treatment must not wait for the serology to return.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Pubic lice. Screen for concurrent sexually transmitted infection, since pubic lice often coexist with one. Slate-gray to bluish macules are maculae caerulae, representing hemorrhage at feeding sites.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 24

src.question: A 26-year-old man has mild pubic itching, slate-gray to bluish irregular macules about 1 cm across on the lower abdomen, and papules around the umbilicus. Which additional step is most appropriate?
src.key: Screen for concurrent sexually transmitted infection, since pubic lice often coexist with one
src.explanation: Correct — the macules are maculae caerulae, representing hemorrhage at feeding sites.

items.section_title: 4.4 · Objective a — Paronychia and necrotizing fasciitis
items.html: Necrotizing fasciitis admission. Admit to a surgical intensive care unit, ideally a burn or trauma center; a team approach with consultations is required, not optional.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 131

src.question: Where should a patient with necrotizing fasciitis be admitted?
src.key: A surgical intensive care unit, ideally a burn or trauma center
src.explanation: Correct — a team approach with consultations is required.

also.key: A team approach with surgical intensive care, ideally at a burn or trauma center
also.explanation: Correct — consultations are described as necessary rather than optional.

items.section_title: 8.5 · Objective b — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Congenital melanocytic naevus management. It depends on melanoma risk together with cosmetic and functional considerations, removing as much as possible while preserving function; observation may be better where there is little skin for a graft site.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 31

src.question: What determines management of a congenital melanocytic naevus?
src.key: Melanoma risk together with cosmetic and functional considerations, removing as much as possible while preserving function
src.explanation: Correct — observation may be the better option where there is little skin for a graft site.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Head lice. Most affect children between three and twelve years, spread primarily by direct head-to-head contact; indirect spread through combs, brushes, bedding and headgear is less common.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 24

src.question: Which age group is most affected by head lice, and how is it usually transmitted?
src.key: Children between three and twelve years, primarily by direct head-to-head contact
src.explanation: Indirect spread through combs, brushes, bedding and headgear is less common.

items.section_title: 9.5 · Objective 1 — Malignant melanoma
items.html: Melanoma self-examination. Perform it monthly using the recognition mnemonic and ugly-duckling principles, including the scalp, back, palms, soles and nails, since acral and scalp sites are easy to miss.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 56

src.question: Which self-examination should melanoma patients perform, and which sites must be included?
src.key: Monthly self-examination using the recognition mnemonic and ugly-duckling principles, including the scalp, back, palms, soles and nails
src.explanation: Correct — the acral and scalp sites are easy to miss.

also.key: Monthly self-examination using the recognition mnemonic and ugly-duckling principles, including scalp, back, palms, soles and nails
also.explanation: Correct — the sun-protected and acral sites are the ones people skip.

items.section_title: 9.8 · Objective 11 — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Mohs micrographic surgery. Indicated for invasive squamous cell carcinoma on a high-risk site such as the temple, and for a lesion exceeding 1 cm on the face; either is a separate indication.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 24

src.question: A 70-year-old has a biopsy-proven invasive squamous cell carcinoma 1.4 cm across on the temple. Which is the most appropriate management?
src.key: Mohs micrographic surgery, since the temple is a high-risk site and the lesion exceeds 1 cm on the face
src.explanation: Correct — two separate Mohs indications are met.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Neurocutaneous melanosis. A related condition in patients with naevi on the head, neck or posterior midline, causing seizures, hydrocephalus, neurological deficits and vomiting; prognosis is poor once neurological symptoms appear, usually in the first few years of life.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 29

src.question: What is neurocutaneous melanosis and which patients are at risk?
src.key: A related condition in patients with naevi on the head, neck or posterior midline, causing seizures, hydrocephalus, neurological deficits and vomiting
src.explanation: Correct — the prognosis is poor once neurological symptoms appear, usually in the first few years of life.

items.section_title: 4.3 · Objective a — Impetigo, erysipelas, cellulitis and abscess
items.html: Non-purulent cellulitis on oral antibiotics. Fever that persists beyond 48 hours should prompt a change in antimicrobial therapy guided by culture results; with antibiotics fever usually resolves in 24 hours.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 112

src.question: A patient with non-purulent cellulitis is treated with oral antibiotics as an outpatient. Which finding should prompt a change in antimicrobial therapy?
src.key: Fever that persists beyond 48 hours
src.explanation: Correct — with antibiotic therapy the fever usually resolves in 24 hours, so fever lasting more than 48 hours calls for a change guided by culture results.

items.section_title: 6.6 · Objective b — Herpes simplex and herpetic whitlow
items.html: Herpetic whitlow. Do not incise; cover it and give antivirals. Incision and drainage does not treat herpes simplex virus and can delay healing; early oral acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir may shorten the episode.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 128

src.question: A 29-year-old dental hygienist develops a painful, swollen index finger with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base, preceded by burning and tingling. A colleague suggests incision and drainage. What is the correct management?
src.key: Do not incise; cover it and give antivirals
src.explanation: Incision and drainage does not treat herpes simplex virus and can delay healing. Lesions should be covered, hand hygiene used, contact with mucosa and broken skin avoided until healed, and early oral acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir may shorten the episode.

items.section_title: 2.6 · Common dermatologic pharmacology
items.html: Topical retinoid counseling. Start gradually and expect irritation; the important considerations are irritation, dryness and photosensitivity, and pregnancy precautions apply.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: A 22-year-old woman is prescribed topical tretinoin for acne. What counseling is most important before she starts?
src.key: Start gradually; expect irritation
src.explanation: The important clinical considerations for topical retinoids are irritation, dryness, and photosensitivity; therapy should begin gradually, and pregnancy precautions apply. Common agents include adapalene, tretinoin, tazarotene, and trifarotene.

items.section_title: 6.4 · Objective b — The yeasts: candidal intertrigo and pityriasis versicolor
items.html: Pityriasis versicolor pallor. Pigment recovery lags months behind clearance, because hypopigmentation reflects altered melanocyte function and reduced tanning; persistent pallor does not indicate treatment failure.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 77

src.question: A 21-year-old man treated for pityriasis versicolor returns two months later frustrated that the pale patches persist despite his completing the full course. What is the most accurate explanation?
src.key: Pigment recovery lags months behind clearance
src.explanation: Hypopigmentation reflects altered melanocyte function and reduced tanning, and recovery can lag months after yeast clearance. The persistence of pallor does not indicate treatment failure.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Spironolactone in hidradenitis suppurativa. It is an aldosterone antagonist that lowers androgens by inhibiting ovarian and adrenal androgen production; combination birth control pills are used similarly.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 78

src.question: A 30-year-old woman with moderate hidradenitis suppurativa of both axillae has not responded to topical therapy. What is the rationale for adding spironolactone?
src.key: An aldosterone antagonist that lowers androgens
src.explanation: Spironolactone is an aldosterone antagonist that inhibits ovarian and adrenal production of androgens. Combination birth control pills are used similarly, reducing luteinising hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone secretion.

items.section_title: 2.6 · Common dermatologic pharmacology
items.html: Before compression therapy. Perform an ankle-brachial index (or toe pressure) when peripheral arterial disease is suspected, such as with diminished pulses; compression is the cornerstone only once adequate arterial circulation is established.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 116

src.question: A 68-year-old woman presents with chronic bilateral lower-leg swelling, pruritus, and skin discoloration. Examination demonstrates poorly demarcated erythematous plaques, pitting edema, and brown hyperpigmentation around both medial ankles. Pedal pulses are diminished. What is the most appropriate next step before prescribing compression therapy?
src.key: Perform an ankle-brachial index
src.explanation: Compression is the cornerstone of management only once adequate arterial circulation has been established. An ankle-brachial index or toe pressure should be obtained when peripheral arterial disease is suspected — as the diminished pulses here suggest — before initiating substantial compression.

also.key: Perform an ankle-brachial index
also.explanation: Compression is the cornerstone of management, but only once adequate arterial circulation is established, and the diminished pulses demand that check first.

items.section_title: 6.5 · Objective b — Varicella and herpes zoster
items.html: Hutchinson sign. Herpes zoster lesions on the tip or side of the nose increase ocular risk, but its absence does not exclude eye involvement; systemic antiviral therapy should be started immediately.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 103

src.question: A 72-year-old man presents with vesicles in the right ophthalmic division distribution, including lesions on the tip of his nose. What does that finding signify?
src.key: Hutchinson sign, which increases ocular risk
src.explanation: Herpes zoster ophthalmicus involves the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve. Hutchinson sign — lesions on the tip or side of the nose — increases ocular risk, but its absence does not exclude eye involvement, and systemic antiviral therapy should be started immediately.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: Infantile hemangioma types. Superficial, mixed, and deep, classified by depth of vessel involvement; superficial is commonest, presenting as a bright red papule, plaque, or nodule, and the deep type is the least common.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 67

src.question: A 6-week-old infant has a bright red papule on the shoulder, and the clinician classifies the lesion by the depth of vessel involvement. What are the three types of infantile hemangioma, and which is the most common?
src.key: Superficial, mixed, and deep; superficial commonest
src.explanation: The superficial type is the most common, with dilated vessels in the dermis surrounded by proliferating endothelial cells, presenting as a bright red papule, plaque, or nodule and previously called a strawberry hemangioma. The deep type is the least common.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Shaving with pseudofolliculitis barbae. Avoid lift-and-cut razors and use a single blade (at most double) at a mild angle, because lift-and-cut systems cut the hair below the skin surface where it can re-enter the follicular wall.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 57

src.question: A 29-year-old Black man with pseudofolliculitis barbae cannot stop shaving because his employer requires a clean-shaven face. What advice about shaving technique is most appropriate?
src.key: Avoid lift-and-cut razors; use a single blade
src.explanation: Patients should avoid lift-and-cut razor systems and look for mild razor angles with single or at most double blades, because those systems cut the hair below the skin surface where it can re-enter the follicular wall.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Multimodal head lice treatment. It is warranted because resistance is rising; the World Health Organization recommends that pediculicidal testing be read 24 hours after application.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 30

src.question: A 9-year-old boy has head lice that persisted after a first pediculicide application. Why is a multimodal approach recommended, and what does the World Health Organization recommend regarding pediculicide assessment?
src.key: Resistance is rising; read the result at 24 hours
src.explanation: A multimodal approach is warranted because of increasing resistance, and the World Health Organization recommends that pediculicidal testing be read 24 hours after application. If treatment is not followed appropriately, patients tend to seek alternative care such as essential oils.

items.section_title: 5.2 · Objective a — Bedbugs, fleas, stings and caterpillars
items.html: Tungiasis management. Surgical excision or cryotherapy and topical agents, with tetanus prophylaxis and systemic antibiotics; prevention centers on avoiding walking barefoot in endemic areas.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 40

src.question: A 30-year-old man has confirmed tungiasis of both feet after a trip abroad. What management is appropriate?
src.key: Excision or cryotherapy, with tetanus cover
src.explanation: Management includes surgical excision or cryotherapy and topical agents, tetanus prophylaxis, and systemic antibiotics. Prevention centers on avoiding walking barefoot in endemic areas.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Infantile atopic dermatitis. Weeping inflammatory patches and crusted plaques on the cheeks, scalp, and extensor surfaces; rubbing commonly replaces scratching at this age. Roughly 80 percent of patients have a personal or family history of atopy.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 54

src.question: A 6-month-old girl is brought to the clinic by her father for a rash that has been present for three weeks. He reports she is difficult to settle at night and rubs her face against the bedsheet rather than scratching it. Her father has allergic rhinitis and her older brother has asthma. On examination there are weeping inflammatory patches and crusted plaques over both cheeks and the extensor surfaces of the forearms. The antecubital and popliteal fossae are clear. There is no fever, no purulent drainage, and no history of new detergents, soaps, or foods. What is the most likely diagnosis?
src.key: Atopic dermatitis, infantile pattern
src.explanation: In infants atopic dermatitis produces weeping inflammatory patches and crusted plaques on the cheeks, scalp, and extensor surfaces, and rubbing commonly replaces scratching at this age. The family history of allergic rhinitis and asthma completes the atopic triad, and roughly 80 percent of patients have a personal or family history of atopy.

items.section_title: 7.5 · Objective a — The nodules that must be told from a cancer
items.html: Dermatofibroma symptoms. Usually asymptomatic, sometimes with a history of insect bite; when symptomatic it may cause slight pruritus or pain, and it is described as the commonest painful skin tumor.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 45

src.question: A 37-year-old woman has a firm nodule on the lower leg and reports that it occasionally hurts when knocked. What is notable about the symptom profile of a dermatofibroma?
src.key: The commonest painful skin tumor
src.explanation: Dermatofibroma is usually asymptomatic, sometimes with a history of insect bite, and when symptomatic may cause slight pruritus or pain — it is described as the most common painful skin tumor.

items.section_title: 4.3 · Objective a — Impetigo, erysipelas, cellulitis and abscess
items.html: Culture in impetigo. Obtain a culture rather than relying on appearance alone if the patient is at high risk for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection, such as a healthcare worker or teacher, or if acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis is present.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 93

src.question: A 7-year-old boy and his mother, who teaches at his school, both present with honey-crusted perioral lesions. In which patient with impetigo should a culture be obtained rather than relying on clinical appearance alone?
src.key: A healthcare worker or teacher
src.explanation: Cultures are obtained if the patient is at high risk for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection, such as a healthcare worker or teacher, or if acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis is present.

items.section_title: 6.2 · Objective b — The dermatophytes, by body site
items.html: Tinea capitis treatment. It requires oral therapy, because topical agents alone do not penetrate the infected hair shaft; antifungal shampoo reduces viable spore shedding but does not replace oral treatment.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 15

src.question: A 7-year-old boy has scaly patches on the scalp with areas of hair loss and visible black dots where hairs have fractured. A potassium hydroxide preparation confirms fungal elements. His mother asks whether a medicated cream will be enough. What is the correct response?
src.key: Oral therapy; topicals miss the hair shaft
src.explanation: Tinea capitis requires oral therapy; topical agents alone do not penetrate the infected hair shaft. Antifungal shampoo reduces viable spore shedding but does not replace oral treatment.

also.key: Topical agents alone do not penetrate the infected hair shaft
also.explanation: Correct — antifungal shampoo reduces spore shedding but does not replace oral therapy.

items.section_title: 7.2 · Objective a — Abnormal wound healing: keloid and hypertrophic scar
items.html: Silicone gel sheets for scars. The theory is that occlusive dressings warm the scar, raising collagenase activity; they are worn 12 to 24 hours a day for up to a year.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 16

src.question: A 24-year-old woman is given silicone gel sheeting for a keloid on the chest and asks how it works and how long she must wear it. What is the theoretical basis for using it?
src.key: It warms the scar, raising collagenase activity
src.explanation: The theory is that occlusive dressings such as silicone gel sheets increase the temperature of the scar and thereby collagenase activity. They are worn 12 to 24 hours a day for up to a year.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Photoaging. Tretinoin is the only approved topical agent; expect initial irritation (retinoid dermatitis) over 6 to 12 months. It stimulates collagen synthesis, inhibits matrix metalloproteinase activity, and reduces fine lines and dyspigmentation.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 119

src.question: A 55-year-old woman asks about treatment for photoaging. What topical agent is approved for this indication, and what should she be told to expect?
src.key: Tretinoin, with initial irritation over 6 to 12 months
src.explanation: Tretinoin 0.025 to 0.1 percent is the only approved topical agent for photoaging. It stimulates collagen synthesis, inhibits matrix metalloproteinase activity, and reduces fine lines and dyspigmentation; therapy is started low and titrated, with initial retinoid dermatitis expected.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Objective d — Discuss clinical principles and decision-making
items.html: Clinical reasoning first steps. Gather initial patient information, then organize and interpret it, then synthesize it into a problem representation, before hypotheses are generated and tested.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 11

src.question: A student is seeing a 46-year-old woman with an undifferentiated complaint and is unsure how to begin working through it. What are the first three steps of the clinical reasoning process?
src.key: Gather, interpret, then represent the problem
src.explanation: The process begins with gathering initial patient information, then organizing and interpreting it, then synthesizing the information into a problem representation, before hypotheses are generated and tested.

items.section_title: 7.4 · Objective a — Pressure injury and pilonidal disease
items.html: Pilonidal disease risk factors. Obesity, sedentary life and dense cleft hair; the male to female ratio is 3 to 1.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 39

src.question: A 23-year-old man presents with a painful swelling in the natal cleft, and the clinician reviews what predisposed him to it. Which set of risk factors is associated with pilonidal disease?
src.key: Obesity, sedentary life, dense cleft hair
src.explanation: Those are the listed risk factors, and the male to female ratio is 3 to 1.

items.section_title: 5.3 · Objective a — Cutaneous larva migrans and cercarial dermatitis
items.html: Cercarial dermatitis. Also called swimmer's itch or clam digger's itch, it results from skin penetration by cercarial forms of parasitic flatworms; snails complete the cycle after eggs passed by host animals such as waterfowl and muskrats hatch and infect them.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 89

src.question: A 31-year-old camper develops a prickling sensation lasting about 30 minutes after wading in a freshwater lake, followed 10 to 12 hours later by severe itching and then erythematous papules. What is this condition, and what completes its life cycle?
src.key: Cercarial dermatitis; snails complete the cycle
src.explanation: Cercarial dermatitis, also called swimmer's itch or clam digger's itch, results from penetration of the skin by cercarial forms of parasitic flatworms. Host animals such as waterfowl and muskrats pass eggs in feces into water, the eggs hatch and infect snails within 12 hours, and cercariae are released about 5 weeks later.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: Cherry angioma. A benign capillary proliferation (capillary or venule proliferation), very common and increasing with age; treatment is unnecessary unless it bothers the patient, and new lesions will likely develop with no way to prevent them.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 87

src.question: A 54-year-old woman is found on routine examination to have several smooth, firm, deep red papules under 5 mm on the trunk that blanch with pressure. She has never noticed them. What education should be given?
src.key: Benign capillary proliferation
src.explanation: Cherry angiomas are acquired vascular lesions formed by capillary or venule proliferation, very common and increasing with age. Treatment is unnecessary unless they bother the patient, and patients should be aware that new lesions will likely develop and there is no way to prevent them.

items.section_title: 7.5 · Objective a — The nodules that must be told from a cancer
items.html: Epidermoid cyst. Enclosed epithelium filled with keratin within the dermis; it is often called a sebaceous cyst because it appears to contain sebum, which makes that term a misnomer.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 53

src.question: A 41-year-old man has a moveable nodule on the back with a central punctum, which he refers to as a sebaceous cyst. Why is that term a misnomer for an epidermoid cyst?
src.key: Enclosed epithelium filled with keratin
src.explanation: An epidermoid cyst is formed by cystic enclosure of epithelium within the dermis and becomes filled with keratin. It is often called a sebaceous cyst because it appears to contain sebum.

items.section_title: 6.5 · Objective b — Varicella and herpes zoster
items.html: Herpes simplex virus type and site. Either type causes either site: either virus type can cause oral or genital infection, lesion location does not reliably determine type, and typing requires a type-specific test.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 112

src.question: A 24-year-old man has painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the buttock that have broken down into shallow ulcers. He asks whether the location tells him which virus type he has. What is the correct response?
src.key: Either type causes either site
src.explanation: Either herpes simplex virus type can cause oral or genital infection, and lesion location does not reliably determine type. Infections can occur anywhere on the skin, and typing requires a type-specific test.

items.section_title: 4.3 · Objective a — Impetigo, erysipelas, cellulitis and abscess
items.html: Devitalized tissue in cellulitis. Tense, cyanotic, necrotic, bronzed, blanched tissue is devitalized and will not be perfused, so antibiotics cannot reach it; surgical debridement is required.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 111

src.question: A 66-year-old man with cellulitis of the leg has an area that is tense, cyanotic, and bronzed with blanching. What is the significance of this finding?
src.key: Devitalized tissue; antibiotics cannot reach it
src.explanation: Devitalized tissue that is tense, cyanotic, necrotic, bronzed, and blanched will not be perfused, so antibiotics will not get to the site. Surgical debridement is required.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: Telangiectasia. A dilated capillary under 1 mm that blanches; these are acquired vascular lesions of permanently dilated capillaries, single or grouped with a central punctum, primary or secondary.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 88

src.question: A 52-year-old woman has fine red lines on both cheeks that disappear when pressed with a glass slide. How is a telangiectasia defined, and what is its behavior on pressure?
src.key: A dilated capillary under 1 mm that blanches
src.explanation: Telangiectasias are acquired vascular lesions consisting of permanently dilated capillaries under 1 mm. They blanch, may be single or grouped with a central punctum, may be primary or secondary, and are associated with numerous diseases.

items.section_title: 7.7 · Objectives a & b — Neurofibromatosis, and the remaining lesions
items.html: New benign lesion in a sun-exposed area. Use the opportunity for counseling on sunscreen and self-examination, including avoiding direct sun during peak hours and performing periodic skin self-examinations.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 112

src.question: A 49-year-old man presents with a new benign lesion on a sun-exposed area of the forearm. What opportunity does this create?
src.key: Counseling on sunscreen and self-examination
src.explanation: When discussing any new lesion in sun-exposed areas, the clinician should take the opportunity to counsel on sunscreen use, avoiding direct sun during peak hours, and performing periodic skin self-examinations.

items.section_title: 6.7 · Objective b — Molluscum contagiosum and warts
items.html: Red or black dots in a wart. Tiny dots are thrombosed capillaries, made more prominent by trimming the surface, and distinguish a wart from a callus, which lacks them.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 142

src.question: A 12-year-old has several elevated, round papules under 1 cm with a rough grayish surface on the fingers. Trimming one reveals tiny red-black dots. What do those dots represent, and what does their presence help exclude?
src.key: Thrombosed capillaries, distinguishing it from a callus
src.explanation: Tiny red or black dots represent thrombosed dilated capillaries, and trimming the surface makes them more prominent. A callus lacks them, which is why paring the lesion is a useful bedside maneuver.

items.section_title: 6.5 · Objective b — Varicella and herpes zoster
items.html: Primary varicella-zoster infection. Its most characteristic feature is lesions in multiple stages of healing appearing simultaneously: macules progress to papules, vesicles, and crusts.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 84

src.question: A 6-year-old unvaccinated child has a generalized pruritic eruption concentrated on the trunk, scalp, and face. Macules, papules, vesicles, and crusts are all present at the same time. What feature is most characteristic?
src.key: Lesions in multiple stages of healing appearing simultaneously
src.explanation: Primary varicella-zoster virus infection causes a generalized pruritic eruption in multiple stages of healing — macules progress to papules, vesicles, and crusts, with several stages appearing simultaneously.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Carbuncle. A deeper infection made of interconnecting furuncles in several follicles, with several loculated abscesses, superficial pustules, necrotic plugs and sieve-like draining openings.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 63

src.question: Describe the physical findings of a carbuncle.
src.key: Several loculated abscesses, superficial pustules, necrotic plugs and sieve-like draining openings
src.explanation: Correct — a deeper infection made of interconnecting furuncles in several follicles.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Spontaneously draining abscess. Give warm soaks and broad-spectrum antibiotic cover that considers methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, then adjust to the culture result.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 115

src.question: An abscess drains spontaneously, and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is possible. How are antibiotics chosen?
src.key: Broad-spectrum cover, then adjusted to culture
src.explanation: Correct — a spontaneously draining abscess gets warm soaks and broad-spectrum antibiotics that consider methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, changed according to the culture result.

items.section_title: 4.1 · Objective a — Acne vulgaris
items.html: Acne scarring out of proportion. Suspect patient manipulation of the lesions through picking or squeezing; patients and families are educated about that risk.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 36

src.question: What should be suspected when acne scarring seems out of proportion to the severity of lesions?
src.key: Patient manipulation of the lesions through picking or squeezing
src.explanation: Patients and families are educated about that risk.

items.section_title: 4.3 · Objective a — Impetigo, erysipelas, cellulitis and abscess
items.html: Cellulitis course on antibiotics. It may look worse on day one, fever usually resolves within twenty-four hours, and inflammation clears over one to two weeks; fever beyond forty-eight hours prompts a change guided by culture.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 112

src.question: What is the expected course of cellulitis on antibiotic therapy?
src.key: It may look worse on day one, fever usually resolves within twenty-four hours, inflammation over one to two weeks
src.explanation: Fever beyond forty-eight hours prompts a change guided by culture.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Hot tub folliculitis. Caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a Gram-negative organism, from inadequately chlorinated water; named sources are whirlpools, hot tubs, water slides and physiotherapy pools.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 48

src.question: What causes hot tub folliculitis and why does it occur?
src.key: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a Gram-negative organism, from inadequately chlorinated water
src.explanation: Whirlpools, hot tubs, water slides and physiotherapy pools are the named sources.

items.section_title: 4.4 · Objective a — Paronychia and necrotizing fasciitis
items.html: Chronic paronychia. An inflammatory reaction of the proximal nail fold to irritants and allergens, with Candida albicans commonest; at risk are diabetics, laundry workers, cleaners, cooks, bartenders, dishwashers and swimmers.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 120

src.question: What causes chronic paronychia and who is at risk?
src.key: An inflammatory reaction of the proximal nail fold to irritants and allergens, with Candida albicans commonest
src.explanation: Correct — diabetics, laundry workers, cleaners, cooks, bartenders, dishwashers and swimmers.

items.section_title: 4.4 · Objective a — Paronychia and necrotizing fasciitis
items.html: Chronic paronychia treatment. Keep the hands dry and use a broad-spectrum topical antifungal, with oral fluconazole in severe cases, treating the underlying inflammation and infection together.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 123

src.question: How is chronic paronychia treated?
src.key: Keep the hands dry and use a broad-spectrum topical antifungal, with oral fluconazole in severe cases
src.explanation: Correct — treat the underlying inflammation and infection together.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Folliculitis. Defined by inflammatory cells within the wall and ostia of the hair follicle, forming a follicular pustule; causes include infection, physical injury and chemical irritation.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 38

src.question: What defines folliculitis?
src.key: Inflammatory cells within the wall and ostia of the hair follicle, forming a follicular pustule
src.explanation: The causes include infection, physical injury and chemical irritation.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Acute paronychia treatment. Warm soaks for twenty minutes three times daily in mild cases; incision and drainage in severe cases, with oral antibiotics and cultures to rule out resistant organisms where appropriate.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 119

src.question: How is acute paronychia treated?
src.key: Warm soaks for twenty minutes three times daily in mild cases; incision and drainage in severe cases
src.explanation: with oral antibiotics and cultures to rule out resistant organisms where appropriate.

items.section_title: 4.1 · Objective a — Acne vulgaris
items.html: Tretinoin with benzoyl peroxide. Separate the two by at least three hours, because applying them together irritates the skin.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 35

src.question: A 20-year-old man has been using topical tretinoin at night and benzoyl peroxide in the morning, but has begun applying them together and now has stinging and peeling. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: Separate the two by at least three hours, because applying them together irritates the skin
src.explanation: Correct — that interval is specified in the patient education.

items.section_title: 4.4 · Objective a — Paronychia and necrotizing fasciitis
items.html: Necrotizing fasciitis care. Requires aggressive surgical debridement, broad antibiotic cover of aerobic Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms and anaerobes, and surgical intensive care admission with a team approach.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 131

src.question: A 60-year-old man has confirmed necrotizing fasciitis. Which combination of care is required?
src.key: Aggressive surgical debridement, broad antibiotic cover and surgical intensive care admission
src.explanation: Correct — cover aerobic Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms and anaerobes, with a team approach.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Pseudofolliculitis barbae shaving advice. Use a single or double blade at a mild angle, avoid lift-and-cut systems, and keep razors clean; chemical depilatories and laser hair removal are alternatives.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 57

src.question: A 29-year-old man with pseudofolliculitis barbae must remain clean-shaven for work. Which is the most appropriate advice?
src.key: Use a single or double blade at a mild angle, avoid lift-and-cut systems, and keep razors clean
src.explanation: with chemical depilatories and laser hair removal as alternatives.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Secondary bacterial infection. A secondary bacterial infection can develop within skin already affected by acne, arising in skin damaged by an existing condition.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 56

src.question: A 15-year-old boy with untreated acne develops tender fluctuant nodules with purulent drainage over the same areas. Which best describes what has happened?
src.key: A secondary bacterial infection has developed within skin already affected by acne
src.explanation: Correct — secondary infection arises in skin damaged by an existing condition.

items.section_title: 4.1 · Objective a — Acne vulgaris
items.html: Acne with inadequate response. After six to eight weeks of inadequate response, add an oral tetracycline, keeping benzoyl peroxide to limit resistance.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 26

src.question: A 17-year-old girl has widespread inflammatory papules and pustules across the face, chest and back that have not improved after eight weeks of topical benzoyl peroxide with a retinoid. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Add an oral tetracycline, keeping benzoyl peroxide to limit resistance
src.explanation: Correct — inadequate response over six to eight weeks is the stated trigger.

items.section_title: 4.1 · Objective a — Acne vulgaris
items.html: Isotretinoin requirements. iPledge enrollment of the prescriber is required, with a one-month supply at a time; a pregnancy test is not needed for a man.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 30

src.question: A 18-year-old man with severe nodular acne has failed a topical retinoid with an oral antibiotic and benzoyl peroxide. Which test is required before the next treatment is started?
src.key: A pregnancy test is not needed for him, but iPledge enrollment of the prescriber is required
src.explanation: Correct — isotretinoin requires prescriber enrollment and a one-month supply at a time.

items.section_title: 4.1 · Objective a — Acne vulgaris
items.html: Acne response time. Improvement takes four to six weeks, and the back and chest may take three to four months; clinical improvement is judged by new lesion count at six to eight weeks.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 36

src.question: A 30-year-old woman with acne asks how soon she should expect to see a difference. Which is the most appropriate counseling point?
src.key: Improvement takes four to six weeks, and the back and chest may take three to four months
src.explanation: Clinical improvement is judged by new lesion count at six to eight weeks.
