items.section_title: 6.5 · Objective b — Varicella and herpes zoster
items.html: Herpes zoster pre-eruptive phase. Dysesthesia or pain within the affected dermatome, with lesions appearing by 48 to 72 hours. Malaise, myalgia, headache and photophobia may occur, and rarely fever.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 97

src.question: What characterizes the pre-eruptive phase of herpes zoster, and how long before the lesions?
src.key: Dysesthesia or pain within the affected dermatome, with lesions appearing by 48 to 72 hours
src.explanation: Correct — malaise, myalgia, headache and photophobia may occur, and rarely fever.

items.section_title: 6.2 · Objective b — The dermatophytes, by body site
items.html: Tinea corporis (ringworm). Progressive central clearing produces the annular outline. The lesion is a circular, sharply circumscribed, slightly erythematous, dry scaly patch or plaque.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 24

src.question: What produces the annular outline that gives tinea corporis the name ringworm?
src.key: Progressive central clearing
src.explanation: Correct — the lesion is a circular, sharply circumscribed, slightly erythematous, dry scaly patch or plaque.

items.section_title: 6.7 · Objective b — Molluscum contagiosum and warts
items.html: Molluscum contagiosum natural history. In immunocompetent patients most clear spontaneously, although resolution may take months to several years. Clearance is spontaneous but often slow.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 130

src.question: What is the natural history of molluscum contagiosum in an immunocompetent patient?
src.key: Most clear spontaneously, although resolution may take months to several years
src.explanation: Correct — spontaneous but often slow.

items.section_title: 6.7 · Objective b — Molluscum contagiosum and warts
items.html: Warts. Caused by human papillomavirus, which infects keratinocytes and remains confined to the epidermis, producing a benign proliferation.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 138

src.question: What causes warts, and which cells does the virus infect?
src.key: Human papillomavirus, which infects keratinocytes and remains confined to the epidermis
src.explanation: Correct — a benign proliferation confined to the epidermis.

items.section_title: 6.2 · Objective b — The dermatophytes, by body site
items.html: Recurrent tinea pedis with thickened discolored toenails. Consider oral therapy, treat the coexisting onychomycosis, and reinforce moisture control. An untreated nail reservoir drives recurrence.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: A patient has recurrent tinea pedis despite repeated topical courses, and also has thickened discolored toenails. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Consider oral therapy, treat the coexisting onychomycosis, and reinforce moisture control
src.explanation: Correct — an untreated nail reservoir drives recurrence.

items.section_title: 6.2 · Objective b — The dermatophytes, by body site
items.html: Tinea of the hand with foot scaling. A thickened, dry, scaly palm with interdigital foot scaling is two feet–one hand syndrome, in which the hand used to scratch the foot becomes affected. Patients often blame dry skin or manual labor.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 54

src.question: A 55-year-old laborer has a thickened, dry, scaly right palm. He assumed it was from hard work. His left foot has interdigital scaling. Which term describes this pattern?
src.key: Two feet–one hand syndrome, in which the hand used to scratch the foot becomes affected
src.explanation: Correct — and patients often blame dry skin or manual labor.

items.section_title: 6.4 · Objective b — The yeasts: candidal intertrigo and pityriasis versicolor
items.html: Extensive or recurrent pityriasis versicolor. Oral terbinafine is not appropriate because adequate drug levels are not achieved in sweat, although topical terbinafine can be effective. The route matters for this organism.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 82

src.question: A patient with extensive, recurrent pityriasis versicolor has failed topical therapy. Why is oral terbinafine NOT an appropriate choice?
src.key: Because adequate drug levels are not achieved in sweat, although topical terbinafine can be effective
src.explanation: Correct — the route matters for this organism.

items.section_title: 6.5 · Objective b — Varicella and herpes zoster
items.html: Zoster over the forehead, upper eyelid and nose tip with eye pain and photophobia. Start systemic antiviral therapy immediately and arrange same-day ophthalmology evaluation. Do not delay the antiviral while awaiting the eye review.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 103

src.question: A 68-year-old has a zoster eruption over the forehead and upper eyelid, with lesions on the tip of the nose. He reports eye pain and photophobia. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Start systemic antiviral therapy immediately and arrange same-day ophthalmology evaluation
src.explanation: Correct — do not delay the antiviral while awaiting the eye review.

items.section_title: 6.5 · Objective b — Varicella and herpes zoster
items.html: Severe disseminated zoster with visceral involvement. Manage with intravenous acyclovir with specialist or hospital management, as also for central nervous system or sight-threatening disease.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 106

src.question: A patient with zoster has severe disseminated disease with visceral involvement. Which is the most appropriate management?
src.key: Intravenous acyclovir with specialist or hospital management
src.explanation: Correct — also for central nervous system or sight-threatening disease.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Nits versus dandruff. Nits cannot be removed from the hair shaft. Live lice indicate active infestation while nits indicate past or present infestation; viable eggs are tan to brown and hatched remains are clear, white or light.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 28

src.question: How are nits distinguished from dandruff, and what does each finding indicate?
src.key: Nits cannot be removed from the hair shaft; live lice indicate active infestation while nits indicate past or present
src.explanation: Correct — viable eggs are tan to brown and hatched remains are clear, white or light.

items.section_title: 5.4 · Objective a — Spider bites
items.html: Hobo spider bite prognosis. Wounds heal within several weeks and headaches may last a week; treatment is supportive. Death from severe systemic effects, including aplastic anemia, is rare.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 65

src.question: What is the prognosis and treatment of a hobo spider bite?
src.key: Wounds heal within several weeks and headaches may last a week; treatment is supportive
src.explanation: Correct — death from severe systemic effects, including aplastic anemia, is rare.

also.key: The wound heals within several weeks and headaches may last a week; treatment is supportive
also.explanation: Correct — death from severe systemic effects, including aplastic anemia, is rare.

items.section_title: 5.4 · Objective a — Spider bites
items.html: Black widow bite, first thirty minutes. Localized erythema, piloerection and sweating around the bite, then crampy abdominal pain and muscle spasm. Headache, paresthesia, nausea, vomiting, hypertension and seizures may follow.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 57

src.question: How does a black widow spider bite present within the first thirty minutes?
src.key: Localized erythema, piloerection and sweating around the bite, then crampy abdominal pain and muscle spasm
src.explanation: Correct — headache, paresthesia, nausea, vomiting, hypertension and seizures may follow.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Objective a — Tick-borne illness
items.html: Rocky Mountain spotted fever rash. It starts on the ankles and wrists and spreads centripetally over six to eighteen hours, involving palms and soles but sparing the face. Blanching macules or papules may become petechial and purpuric.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 82

src.question: How does the Rocky Mountain spotted fever rash spread?
src.key: It starts on the ankles and wrists and spreads centripetally over six to eighteen hours, involving palms and soles but sparing the face
src.explanation: Correct — blanching macules or papules that may become petechial and purpuric.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Physical methods for head lice. Head shaving, or combing nits out after two minutes of hair moisturizer every few days; effective but slow and painful. They need adjuvant therapy alongside them.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 30

src.question: Which physical methods are described for head lice, and what is their limitation?
src.key: Head shaving, or combing nits out after two minutes of hair moisturizer every few days; effective but slow and painful
src.explanation: Correct — they need adjuvant therapy alongside them.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Multimodal approach to pediculosis. Recommended because of increasing resistance. Pediculicidal effect is read twenty-four hours after application, the World Health Organization recommendation.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 30

src.question: Why is a multimodal approach recommended for pediculosis?
src.key: Because of increasing resistance, with pediculicidal effect read twenty-four hours after application
src.explanation: Correct — that reading interval is the World Health Organization recommendation.

items.section_title: 5.2 · Objective a — Bedbugs, fleas, stings and caterpillars
items.html: Most poisonous caterpillar. The asp or puss caterpillar produces an intensely painful sting and train-track purpura. The gypsy moth caterpillar causes erucism and processionary caterpillars cause anaphylaxis.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 47

src.question: Which caterpillar is described as the most poisonous, and what does its sting produce?
src.key: The asp or puss caterpillar, producing an intensely painful sting and train-track purpura
src.explanation: The gypsy moth caterpillar causes erucism and processionary caterpillars cause anaphylaxis.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Objective a — Tick-borne illness
items.html: Intravenous antibiotics in Lyme disease. Used for some cutaneous manifestations, acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans and arthritis. Ceftriaxone, cefotaxime or penicillin G are the agents named.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 80

src.question: When is intravenous antibiotic therapy used in Lyme disease?
src.key: For some cutaneous manifestations, acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans and arthritis
src.explanation: Correct — ceftriaxone, cefotaxime or penicillin G are the agents named.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Objective a — Tick-borne illness
items.html: Stage 3 (late persistent) Lyme disease. The classic manifestation is monoarticular or oligoarticular arthritis affecting the knee or weight-bearing joints. Subacute encephalopathy and acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans also occur.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 75

src.question: What is the classic manifestation of stage 3, late persistent Lyme disease?
src.key: Monoarticular or oligoarticular arthritis affecting the knee or weight-bearing joints
src.explanation: Correct — subacute encephalopathy and acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans also occur.

items.section_title: 5.4 · Objective a — Spider bites
items.html: Brown recluse spider. Identified by a dark fiddle or violin marking on the cephalothorax; abundant in the American Midwest and Southeast. It is non-aggressive and shelters in closets, attics and stored bedding.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 59

src.question: How is the brown recluse spider identified and where is it abundant?
src.key: A dark fiddle or violin marking on the cephalothorax; abundant in the American Midwest and Southeast
src.explanation: Correct — it is non-aggressive and shelters in closets, attics and stored bedding.

items.section_title: 5.3 · Objective a — Cutaneous larva migrans and cercarial dermatitis
items.html: Cutaneous larva migrans lesion. An erythematous, raised, vesicular, linear or serpentine trail advancing 2 to 3 cm each day. It is intensely pruritic and painful, lasting two to eight weeks, with rare systemic symptoms.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 51

src.question: Describe the classic lesion of cutaneous larva migrans.
src.key: An erythematous, raised, vesicular, linear or serpentine trail advancing 2 to 3 cm each day
src.explanation: Correct — intensely pruritic and painful, lasting two to eight weeks, with rare systemic symptoms.

items.section_title: 5.4 · Objective a — Spider bites
items.html: Hobo spider bite presentation. A painless bite with induration and paresthesia within thirty minutes, a large red area, and vesicles within thirty-six hours. Eschar may follow; systemic symptoms include headache, nausea and memory impairment.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 64

src.question: How does a hobo spider bite present?
src.key: A painless bite with induration and paresthesia within thirty minutes, a large red area, and vesicles within thirty-six hours
src.explanation: Correct — eschar may follow, and systemic symptoms include headache, nausea and memory impairment.

items.section_title: 5.4 · Objective a — Spider bites
items.html: Brown recluse bite timeline. Systemic symptoms develop one to two days after the bite and necrosis at two to three days. Eschar forms between days five and seven, then deep ulcers.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 61

src.question: A 36-year-old man bitten by a brown recluse two days ago has a darkening area at the site plus nausea, headache and chills. Which is the most appropriate interpretation?
src.key: Systemic symptoms develop one to two days after the bite and necrosis at two to three days
src.explanation: Correct — eschar forms between days five and seven, then deep ulcers.

items.section_title: 5.2 · Objective a — Bedbugs, fleas, stings and caterpillars
items.html: Bedbugs. A professional exterminator is necessary; treatment of the bites themselves is symptomatic. Use topical antiseptic or antibiotic for secondary infection, and steroids or antihistamines for itch.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 35

src.question: A 45-year-old man has confirmed bedbug bites and asks what will get rid of them. Which is the most appropriate advice?
src.key: A professional exterminator is necessary; treatment of the bites themselves is symptomatic
src.explanation: Correct — topical antiseptic or antibiotic for secondary infection, steroids or antihistamines for itch.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Erythema nodosum infectious triggers. The most common is Group A Streptococcus, alongside Yersinia, tuberculosis, coccidioidomycosis, histoplasmosis and hepatitis B and C.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 42

src.question: What is the most common infectious trigger of erythema nodosum?
src.key: Group A Streptococcus
src.explanation: alongside Yersinia, tuberculosis, coccidioidomycosis, histoplasmosis and hepatitis B and C.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Dapsone for dermatitis herpetiformis. Check glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase status before the first dose, then monitor the blood count for hemolytic anemia and methemoglobinemia.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 19

src.question: What must be checked before starting dapsone for dermatitis herpetiformis?
src.key: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase status
src.explanation: and the blood count is then monitored for hemolytic anemia and methemoglobinemia.

also.key: Check glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase status before the first dose
also.explanation: then monitor the blood count for hemolytic anemia and methemoglobinemia.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Secondary versus primary hyperhidrosis. Generalized sweating, nocturnal sweating, or an asymmetric distribution should raise suspicion of secondary disease. Primary disease is bilateral, focal and absent during sleep.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 74

src.question: Which features should raise suspicion of secondary rather than primary hyperhidrosis?
src.key: Generalized sweating, nocturnal sweating, or an asymmetric distribution
src.explanation: Correct — primary disease is bilateral, focal and absent during sleep.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Generalized granuloma annulare in an adult over fifty. Screen for diabetes, thyroid disease and dyslipidemia, with age-appropriate malignancy screening. These associations include lymphoma.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 51

src.question: A 58-year-old man has hundreds of small papules over the trunk and limbs, present for a year and mildly itchy. Biopsy confirms granuloma annulare. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Screen for diabetes, thyroid disease and dyslipidemia, with age-appropriate malignancy screening
src.explanation: Correct — generalized disease in an adult over fifty carries these associations, including lymphoma.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Photoallergy diagnosis. Photopatch testing with duplicate sets, one of which is irradiated, is the gold standard; a reaction only on the irradiated set confirms it.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 99

src.question: A 44-year-old woman has an itchy, eczematous eruption on sun-exposed skin that extends onto covered areas, beginning after two weeks of a new sunscreen. Which test establishes the diagnosis?
src.key: Photopatch testing with duplicate sets, one of which is irradiated
src.explanation: Correct — it is the gold standard for photoallergy; a reaction only on the irradiated set confirms it.

items.section_title: 2.6 · Common dermatologic pharmacology
items.html: Papules and pustules around the mouth with topical corticosteroid use. Initial management is to discontinue the corticosteroid and simplify the skin-care routine. Topical corticosteroid exposure is the most important modifiable association, and continued use perpetuates the condition.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 102

src.question: A 27-year-old woman has burning and small red papules around her mouth. Examination shows grouped monomorphic papules and pustules over the nasolabial folds and chin, sparing a narrow rim next to the vermilion border. She has used hydrocortisone cream daily for several months. Which is the most appropriate initial management?
src.key: Discontinue the corticosteroid and simplify her skin-care routine
src.explanation: Topical corticosteroid exposure is the most important modifiable association, and continued use perpetuates the condition.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Guttate psoriasis. No specific treatment is required, though phototherapy or topical steroids may be used. It often needs no treatment.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 164

src.question: A 9-year-old with guttate psoriasis following a streptococcal throat infection is otherwise well. Which is the most appropriate management?
src.key: No specific treatment is required, though phototherapy or topical steroids may be used
src.explanation: Correct — guttate psoriasis often needs no treatment.

items.section_title: 8.1 · Objective a — Ephelides, lentigines and solar lentigo
items.html: Ephelides. Inherited autosomal dominant, most commonly in fair-skinned people with blonde or red hair and possibly Celtic ancestry. Males and females are equally affected.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 4

src.question: How are ephelides inherited, and in whom do they most commonly appear?
src.key: Autosomal dominant, most commonly in fair-skinned people with blonde or red hair and possibly Celtic ancestry
src.explanation: Correct — males and females are equally affected.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Pigmented spindle cell naevus (Reed naevus). A sharply circumscribed darkly pigmented papule usually under 7 mm, jet-black with shades of blue, gray or brown, on the extremities and mainly the thigh. Commonest in the thirties, females more than males; benign.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 41

src.question: Describe pigmented spindle cell naevus, also called Reed naevus.
src.key: A sharply circumscribed darkly pigmented papule usually under 7 mm, jet-black with shades of blue, gray or brown, on the extremities and mainly the thigh
src.explanation: Correct — commonest in the thirties, with females affected more than males, and it is benign.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Melanoma risk and common acquired melanocytic naevi. Risk increases as the number of naevi increases. Naevus numbers peak in the thirties and then decline.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 35

src.question: How does melanoma risk relate to common acquired melanocytic naevi?
src.key: Risk increases as the number of naevi increases
src.explanation: Correct — numbers peak in the thirties and then decline.

items.section_title: 8.2 · Objective a — Seborrheic keratosis and dermatosis papulosa nigrans
items.html: Seborrheic keratoses. Benign beige to brown to black papules and plaques 2 to 20 mm across, velvety or warty, looking stuck onto the skin, common in older adults. They are easily mistaken for neoplasms.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 17

src.question: Describe seborrheic keratoses and who gets them.
src.key: Benign beige to brown to black papules and plaques 2 to 20 mm across, velvety or warty, looking stuck onto the skin, common in older adults
src.explanation: Correct — they are easily mistaken for neoplasms.

items.section_title: 8.1 · Objective a — Ephelides, lentigines and solar lentigo
items.html: Solar lentigines over time. They can progress into lichenoid keratoses. They may also enlarge, darken, stay stable or regress.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 14

src.question: Into what can solar lentigines progress over time?
src.key: Lichenoid keratoses
src.explanation: Correct — they may also enlarge, darken, stay stable or regress.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Blue naevi location. Most commonly on the dorsal hands and feet, scalp, buttocks or sacral region. The lesions are blue, blue-gray or blue-black.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 39

src.question: Where do blue naevi most commonly occur?
src.key: The dorsal hands and feet, scalp, buttocks or sacral region
src.explanation: Correct — the lesions are blue, blue-gray or blue-black.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Spitz naevus. A solitary asymptomatic pink or red hairless firm dome-shaped lesion on face, neck, trunk or extremities, sparing palms, soles and mucous membranes. It has a growth phase, fast or slow, followed by a stable period.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 42

src.question: Describe a Spitz naevus and its distribution.
src.key: A solitary asymptomatic pink or red hairless firm dome-shaped lesion on face, neck, trunk or extremities, sparing palms, soles and mucous membranes
src.explanation: Correct — it has a growth phase, fast or slow, followed by a stable period.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Pigmented spindle cell naevus management. Confirmed by biopsy, with excision and negative margins as management. The lesion is benign despite its jet-black appearance.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 41

src.question: How is pigmented spindle cell naevus diagnosed and managed?
src.key: Confirmed by biopsy, with excision and negative margins as management
src.explanation: Correct — the lesion is benign despite its jet-black appearance.

items.section_title: 8.1 · Objective a — Ephelides, lentigines and solar lentigo
items.html: Solar lentigines. Well-defined with irregular borders, coalescing at sites of severe sunburn, from under 1 mm to several centimeters, light to dark brown. Over time they enlarge, darken, stay stable, regress, or progress into lichenoid keratoses.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 14

src.question: Describe the appearance and natural history of solar lentigines.
src.key: Well-defined with irregular borders, coalescing at sites of severe sunburn, from under 1 mm to several centimeters, light to dark brown
src.explanation: Correct — over time they enlarge, darken, stay stable, regress, or progress into lichenoid keratoses.

items.section_title: 8.3 · Objective a — Vitiligo
items.html: Non-pharmacologic vitiligo management. Psychological intervention, cosmetic therapies and non-traditional approaches; the psychological and social impact is emphasized.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 25

src.question: Which non-pharmacologic elements are named in the management of vitiligo?
src.key: Psychological intervention, cosmetic therapies and non-traditional approaches
src.explanation: Correct — the psychological and social impact is emphasized.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Common versus cellular blue naevi. Common blue naevi are deeply pigmented lesions under 1 cm arising in adolescence; cellular blue naevi are larger plaques or nodules over 1 cm arising before age forty. Both occur on dorsal hands and feet, scalp, buttocks or sacral region.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 39

src.question: How do common and cellular blue naevi differ?
src.key: Common blue naevi are deeply pigmented lesions under 1 cm arising in adolescence; cellular blue naevi are larger plaques or nodules over 1 cm arising before age forty
src.explanation: Correct — both occur on dorsal hands and feet, scalp, buttocks or sacral region.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Changing lesion in dysplastic naevi. Biopsy the lesion, since all changing or developing lesions are biopsied. Excision follows where there is concern for melanoma.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: A 45-year-old woman with dysplastic naevi has one lesion that her partner says has changed shape over three months. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Biopsy that lesion, since all changing or developing lesions are biopsied
src.explanation: Correct — excision follows where there is concern for melanoma.

items.section_title: 8.3 · Objective a — Vitiligo
items.html: Surgery for vitiligo. Tissue or cellular grafting is an option, since surgery is reserved for highly stable disease.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 25

src.question: A 48-year-old man with stable vitiligo that has not changed in four years asks about surgery. Which is the most appropriate response?
src.key: Tissue or cellular grafting is an option, since surgery is reserved for highly stable disease
src.explanation: Correct — his four stable years are exactly the criterion.

items.section_title: 8.5 · Objective b — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Very large congenital naevus. Point families to counseling and support groups; management balances melanoma risk, cosmetic outcome and preserved function. The goal is removing as much as possible while preserving function and improving appearance.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 31

src.question: The parents of a child with a very large congenital naevus ask what support exists. Where should they be pointed, and what shapes the plan?
src.key: Counseling and support groups, with management balancing melanoma risk, cosmetic outcome and preserved function
src.explanation: Correct — the goal is removing as much as possible while preserving function and improving appearance.

items.section_title: 8.2 · Objective a — Seborrheic keratosis and dermatosis papulosa nigrans
items.html: Seborrheic keratosis diagnosis and management. They are benign, diagnosed clinically, and management is supportive. They are common in older adults and easily mistaken for neoplasms.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 17

src.question: A 74-year-old woman has several beige to dark brown papules 5 to 15 mm on the trunk that feel warty and look pasted onto the skin. She is worried they are cancers. Which is the most appropriate response?
src.key: They are benign seborrheic keratoses, diagnosed clinically, and management is supportive
src.explanation: Correct — they are common in older adults and easily mistaken for neoplasms.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Dysplastic naevi. They are common on sun-exposed skin surfaces. They are at least 5 mm with irregular indistinct borders and variable pigmentation.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 43

src.question: A 36-year-old woman with several dysplastic naevi asks where they are most likely to appear. Which is the most appropriate response?
src.key: They are common on sun-exposed skin surfaces
src.explanation: Correct — they are at least 5 mm with irregular indistinct borders and variable pigmentation.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Cellular blue naevus diagnosis. Diagnosis is clinical for small lesions but by biopsy for larger ones. Observation follows, with biopsy or excision if changes are noted.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 40

src.question: A 36-year-old man has a 2 cm blue-gray nodule on the sacral region suspected to be a cellular blue naevus. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Biopsy, since diagnosis is clinical for small lesions but by biopsy for larger ones
src.explanation: Correct — observation follows, with biopsy or excision if changes are noted.

items.section_title: 9.4 · Objective 1 — Basal cell carcinoma
items.html: Topical therapy for basal cell carcinoma. Patients must understand that local inflammation is expected, and that clearance has to be confirmed afterwards. Inflammation is not a reason to stop, and clearing visibly is not the same as being clear.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 38

src.question: Which two things must a patient on topical therapy for basal cell carcinoma understand?
src.key: That local inflammation is expected, and that clearance has to be confirmed afterwards
src.explanation: Correct — the inflammation is not a reason to stop, and clearing visibly is not the same as being clear.

items.section_title: 9.8 · Objective 11 — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Nail unit squamous cell carcinoma. Incomplete excision, immunosuppression, delayed diagnosis and bone invasion increase recurrence and functional morbidity. It is often curable with complete surgery.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 95

src.question: What increases recurrence and functional morbidity in nail unit squamous cell carcinoma?
src.key: Incomplete excision, immunosuppression, delayed diagnosis and bone invasion
src.explanation: Correct — it is often curable with complete surgery, which is why incompleteness matters.

items.section_title: 9.8 · Objective 11 — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Early-stage cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Early aggressive treatment has not been proven to cure the disease or prevent progression, and may itself cause harm. A stage-directed, skin-first approach suits most early disease.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 75

src.question: A patient with early-stage cutaneous T-cell lymphoma asks whether aggressive chemotherapy now would cure it. Which is the most appropriate response?
src.key: Early aggressive treatment has not been proven to cure the disease or prevent progression, and may itself cause harm
src.explanation: Correct — overly aggressive therapy may cause complications and premature death, so a stage-directed, skin-first approach suits most early disease. Aggression is a harm here rather than a virtue.

items.section_title: 9.8 · Objective 11 — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Mohs micrographic surgery for squamous cell carcinoma. Refer when the site is high-risk, the tumor is over one centimeter on the face, or histology is aggressive such as perineural invasion; each independently qualifies.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 25

src.question: A 66-year-old woman has a biopsy-proven invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the ear, 1.2 cm across, with perineural invasion on pathology. What is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Refer for Mohs micrographic surgery, since the site, size and perineural invasion all meet the criteria
src.explanation: Correct — high-risk site, over one centimeter on the face, and aggressive histology each independently qualify.

items.section_title: 9.8 · Objective 11 — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Spread of actinically induced squamous cell carcinoma. An estimated 3 to 7%, raised substantially by high-risk sites or features, immunosuppression, multiple tumors, recurrence, or nodal involvement. The baseline is modest but modifiable.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 26

src.question: A patient asks how likely his actinically induced squamous cell carcinoma is to spread. What is the figure, and what raises it?
src.key: An estimated 3 to 7%, raised substantially by high-risk sites or features, immunosuppression, multiple tumors, recurrence, or nodal involvement
src.explanation: Correct — the baseline is modest but modifiable.

items.section_title: 7.2 · Objective a — Abnormal wound healing: keloid and hypertrophic scar
items.html: Keloid treated with laser. The best result comes from combining the laser with intralesional steroids; laser works by shrinking collagen or inducing microvascular thrombosis.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 19

src.question: A patient's keloid has been treated with laser. Which addition gives the best result?
src.key: Combining the laser with intralesional steroids
src.explanation: Correct — laser works by shrinking collagen or inducing microvascular thrombosis.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: Pyogenic granuloma. This acquired vascular lesion is a misnomer, being neither infectious nor granulomatous. It is a benign vascular tumor common in children, young adults, and pregnancy, arising in response to injury or hormonal factors, most often on the head, neck, and fingers.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 95

src.question: A 16-year-old girl is evaluated for a lesion on the finger pad that appeared rapidly after she injured the finger and bleeds easily when bumped. Examination shows a bright red, friable, pedunculated papule. What is the diagnosis, and what is notable about its name?
src.key: Pyogenic granuloma; the name is a misnomer
src.explanation: Pyogenic granuloma is an acquired vascular lesion that is misnamed, being neither infectious nor granulomatous. It is a benign vascular tumor common in children, young adults, and pregnancy, arising as a response to injury or hormonal factors, most often on the head, neck, and fingers.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Excisional biopsy. An excisional biopsy removes the whole lesion, taking all deep and wide margins, and always needs stitches to close the wound.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 26

src.question: A 57-year-old man has a suspicious pigmented growth on the back that the clinician wishes to sample in a way that removes the entire lesion with deep and wide margins. What biopsy technique is appropriate?
src.key: Excisional biopsy
src.explanation: An excisional biopsy removes the whole lesion taking all deep and wide margins, and always needs stitches to close the wound.

items.section_title: 5.4 · Objective a — Spider bites
items.html: Southern black widow spider. It is identified by a red hourglass on the underside of the abdomen, and its venom contains the neurotoxin alpha-latrotoxin. Latrodectus mactans is found in all but the most northern part of the country.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 56

src.question: How is the southern black widow spider identified, and what is in its venom?
src.key: A red hourglass on the underside of the abdomen; the venom contains the neurotoxin alpha-latrotoxin
src.explanation: Correct — Latrodectus mactans is found in all but the most northern part of the country.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Photopatch test. The suspected photohaptens are applied in duplicate and one set is irradiated with ultraviolet A. A reaction only on the irradiated patch indicates photoallergy; a reaction on both indicates contact allergy.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 99

src.question: How is a positive photopatch test interpreted?
src.key: A reaction only on the irradiated patch indicates photoallergy; a reaction on both indicates contact allergy
src.explanation: Correct — the suspected photohaptens are applied in duplicate and one set irradiated with ultraviolet A.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: Differential of pyogenic granuloma. Cherry angioma, malignant melanoma and squamous cell carcinoma; two of these are malignancies.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 95

src.question: What is the differential diagnosis for a pyogenic granuloma?
src.key: Cherry angioma, malignant melanoma and squamous cell carcinoma
src.explanation: Correct — two malignancies, which is why treatment is often taken up.

items.section_title: 7.5 · Objective a — The nodules that must be told from a cancer
items.html: Differential of dermatofibroma. Basal cell carcinoma, hypertrophic scar, cutaneous melanoma and keratoacanthoma; two of the four are malignancies.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 46

src.question: What is the differential diagnosis for a dermatofibroma?
src.key: Basal cell carcinoma, hypertrophic scar, cutaneous melanoma and keratoacanthoma
src.explanation: Correct — two of the four are malignancies, which is why it matters.

items.section_title: 7.2 · Objective a — Abnormal wound healing: keloid and hypertrophic scar
items.html: Hypertrophic scar versus keloid timing. Hypertrophic scars develop soon after surgery and usually improve with time; keloids may develop months after the trauma and rarely improve.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 24

src.question: How soon after the injury does each of these scars appear, and what happens with time?
src.key: Hypertrophic scars develop soon after surgery and usually improve with time; keloids may develop months after the trauma and rarely improve
src.explanation: Correct — timing and trajectory both separate them.

items.section_title: 7.7 · Objectives a & b — Neurofibromatosis, and the remaining lesions
items.html: Infantile hemangioma first-line treatment. Beta-blockers (propranolol by mouth or timolol topically) and corticosteroids (topical, intralesional or oral, to slow growth and shrink the lesion) are both named first line.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 73

src.question: What are the first-line treatments for an infantile hemangioma?
src.key: Beta-blockers and corticosteroids; both are named first line
src.explanation: Correct — propranolol by mouth or timolol topically, whose mechanism is not well understood, and corticosteroids given topically, intralesionally or orally to slow growth and shrink the lesion.

items.section_title: 7.1 · Objective a — Corns, calluses, and the wart that mimics them
items.html: Wart versus corn or callus. A wart interrupts the skin lines, has a blackened center, and is not confined to pressure areas; corns and calluses both let the skin lines run through.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 8

src.question: Which three features separate a wart from a corn or callus?
src.key: It interrupts the skin lines, has a blackened center, and is not confined to pressure areas
src.explanation: Correct — corns and calluses both let the skin lines run through.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: Flat blanchable pink-purple patch present since birth. No treatment is required; options are tinted waterproof makeup, or pulsed dye laser, which selectively destroys the superficial target vessels.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 81

src.question: A 2-year-old boy has a flat, blanchable, pink-purple patch on one cheek that has been present since birth and stops sharply at the midline. His parents ask what can be done about it. Which is the most appropriate answer?
src.key: No treatment is required; tinted waterproof makeup, or pulsed dye laser
src.explanation: Correct — the laser selectively destroys the superficial target vessels.

items.section_title: 1.5 · Objective e — Discuss the naturalistic approach
items.html: Naturalistic approach. It suits unstable patients and atypical presentations, along with ruling out the worst-case scenario and following responses to interventions.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 24

src.question: Which patient circumstances suit the naturalistic approach?
src.key: Unstable patients and atypical presentations
src.explanation: Both are listed, along with ruling out the worst-case scenario and following responses to interventions.

items.section_title: 1.2 · Objectives b & c — Define pretest and posttest probability
items.html: Pretest versus posttest probability. Pretest probability is estimated from signs, symptoms, history and frequency; posttest probability additionally reflects the test result.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 9

src.question: Which pairing correctly separates pretest from posttest probability?
src.key: Pretest is estimated from signs, symptoms, history and frequency; posttest additionally reflects the test result
src.explanation: That matches both definitions and their inputs.

items.section_title: 9.5 · Objective 1 — Malignant melanoma
items.html: Malignant melanoma appearance. The lesion is asymmetric, irregularly bordered and unevenly colored; a lesion on the sole demands more suspicion.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: Name the condition shown.
src.key: Malignant melanoma
src.explanation: Asymmetric, irregularly bordered and unevenly colored — and on the sole, which demands more suspicion.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Differential of scabies. Atopic dermatitis, body and pubic lice, other arthropod bites, dermatitis herpetiformis, fungal infection and psoriasis; all can produce an intensely itchy eruption.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 17

src.question: Which conditions are named in the differential for scabies?
src.key: Atopic dermatitis, body and pubic lice, other arthropod bites, dermatitis herpetiformis, fungal infection and psoriasis
src.explanation: Correct — all can produce an intensely itchy eruption.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Dysplastic nevus syndrome and melanoma. The higher the number of nevi, the higher the risk of melanoma; over one hundred nevi by adolescence defines the syndrome.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 43

src.question: What is the relationship between naevus number and melanoma in dysplastic naevus syndrome?
src.key: The higher the number of naevi, the higher the risk of melanoma
src.explanation: Correct — over one hundred by adolescence defines the syndrome.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Diagnosing a dysplastic melanocytic nevus. Biopsy establishes the diagnosis, because the lesion is diagnosed histologically.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: A 41-year-old man has a 7 mm naevus with an indistinct border and a pebbly surface, with tan and brown areas within it, on the upper back. Which test establishes the diagnosis?
src.key: Biopsy
src.explanation: Correct — dysplastic melanocytic naevus is diagnosed histologically.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Diagnosing psoriasis. It is generally a clinical diagnosis, though skin biopsy may be needed for definitive diagnosis, for example when the picture is not clear-cut and treatment has failed.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 162

src.question: A 41-year-old man has plaques on both elbows that have been present for two years. The clinical picture is not clear-cut and treatment has failed. Which test would settle the diagnosis?
src.key: Skin biopsy
src.explanation: Correct — psoriasis is generally a clinical diagnosis, though biopsy may be needed for definitive diagnosis.

items.section_title: 9.5 · Objective 1 — Malignant melanoma
items.html: Re-excision margin for melanoma in situ. The margin is 0.5 to 1 cm; margins widen with Breslow thickness from there.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 52

src.question: A 55-year-old man has a melanoma in situ confirmed on his forearm. Which re-excision margin applies?
src.key: 0.5 to 1 cm
src.explanation: Correct — margins widen with Breslow thickness from there.

items.section_title: 8.1 · Objective a — Ephelides, lentigines and solar lentigo
items.html: Ephelides. They are small light brown symmetric macules 3 to 5 mm across, with lentigines as the main differential; they are asymptomatic and the diagnosis is clinical.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 5

src.question: Describe the clinical appearance of ephelides and the main differential.
src.key: Small light brown symmetric macules 3 to 5 mm across, with lentigines as the main differential
src.explanation: Correct — they are asymptomatic and the diagnosis is clinical.

items.section_title: 9.5 · Objective 1 — Malignant melanoma
items.html: Melanoma levels of invasion (Clark level). I is confined to the epidermis; II into the papillary dermis; III filling the papillary dermis; IV into the reticular dermis; V into the subcutaneous tissue. It is an anatomic layer, unlike Breslow thickness, a measurement.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 50

src.question: How do the melanoma levels of invasion, I to V, map onto the layers of the skin (the system conventionally called the Clark level)?
src.key: I confined to the epidermis; II into the papillary dermis; III filling the papillary dermis; IV into the reticular dermis; V into the subcutaneous tissue
src.explanation: Correct — the level of invasion is an ANATOMIC layer, unlike Breslow thickness which is a measurement.

items.section_title: 3.3 · Objective a — Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
items.html: Toxic epidermal necrolysis mortality. Mortality is up to 30 to 35%, predicted by the SCORTEN score calculated within 24 hours and repeated on day three.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 89

src.question: What is the mortality of toxic epidermal necrolysis, and what predicts it at presentation?
src.key: Up to 30 to 35%, predicted by the SCORTEN score calculated within 24 hours
src.explanation: and SCORTEN is repeated on day three.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Management of nevus spilus. Observation with periodic clinical evaluation, plus sun protection counseling, because it rarely progresses to melanoma.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 34

src.question: How is naevus spilus managed?
src.key: Observation with periodic clinical evaluation, plus sun protection counseling
src.explanation: Correct — it rarely progresses to melanoma.

also.key: Observation with periodic clinical evaluation, plus sun protection counseling
also.explanation: Correct — the lesion rarely progresses to melanoma.

items.section_title: 6.5 · Objective b — Varicella and herpes zoster
items.html: Cause of herpes zoster. It results from reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus, which stays latent in cranial-nerve or dorsal-root ganglia; risk rises with age and impaired cell-mediated immunity.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 91

src.question: What causes herpes zoster, and what raises the risk?
src.key: Reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus; risk rises with age and impaired cell-mediated immunity
src.explanation: Correct — the virus stays latent in cranial-nerve or dorsal-root ganglia.

items.section_title: 4.1 · Objective a — Acne vulgaris
items.html: First-line topical acne therapy. Topical retinoids (adapalene, tazarotene, tretinoin) are typical first line for comedonal and inflammatory acne; they are comedolytic, normalize hyperkeratinization and are generally the most effective for mild disease.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 20

src.question: Which class is the typical first-line topical therapy for comedonal and inflammatory acne?
src.key: Topical retinoids, which are comedolytic and normalize hyperkeratinization
src.explanation: Correct — adapalene, tazarotene and tretinoin, generally the most effective for mild disease.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Löfgren syndrome. Erythema nodosum, bilateral ankle arthritis and hilar lymphadenopathy on chest radiograph indicate sarcoidosis presenting as Löfgren syndrome, which has the best prognosis of all sarcoidosis presentations, with over 90% spontaneous remission.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: A 30-year-old woman has erythema nodosum, bilateral ankle arthritis and hilar lymphadenopathy on chest radiograph. Which is the most likely underlying diagnosis?
src.key: Sarcoidosis presenting as Löfgren syndrome
src.explanation: and it has the best prognosis of all sarcoidosis presentations, with over 90% spontaneous remission.

items.section_title: 2.3 · Objective c — Vesiculobullous disease
items.html: Nikolsky sign. A positive sign is when the top layers of skin slip away or slough off from the lower layers when rubbed; it is positive in pemphigus and negative in bullous pemphigoid.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 130

src.question: What is a positive Nikolsky sign?
src.key: The top layers of skin slip away or slough off from the lower layers when rubbed
src.explanation: Correct — positive in pemphigus, negative in bullous pemphigoid.

items.section_title: 9.6 · Objective 1 — Kaposi sarcoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
items.html: Classic Kaposi sarcoma. The classic form affects older men, has a chronic indolent course, is rarely fatal, and is related to age-associated immune senescence.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 63

src.question: An 80-year-old man of Mediterranean origin has slowly progressive purple plaques on both lower legs over several years. He is not immunosuppressed. Which form of Kaposi sarcoma is this?
src.key: Classic — older men, chronic course, rarely fatal, related to age-associated immune senescence
src.explanation: Correct — the chronic indolent form.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Lice causing pediculosis. Pediculus humanus capitis affects the scalp, Pediculus humanus humanus the trunk, and Phthirus pubis pubic skin; the body louse is about 30% larger than the head louse.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 23

src.question: Which three lice cause pediculosis, and which body regions do they affect?
src.key: Pediculus humanus capitis on the scalp, Pediculus humanus humanus on the trunk, Phthirus pubis on pubic skin
src.explanation: The body louse is about 30% larger than the head louse.

items.section_title: 4.1 · Objective a — Acne vulgaris
items.html: Combination acne products against antibiotic resistance. BenzaClin (clindamycin with benzoyl peroxide) and Benzamycin (erythromycin with benzoyl peroxide); both pair a topical antibiotic with benzoyl peroxide.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 24

src.question: Which two combination topical products are named for reducing antibiotic resistance in acne?
src.key: BenzaClin (clindamycin with benzoyl peroxide) and Benzamycin (erythromycin with benzoyl peroxide)
src.explanation: Both pair a topical antibiotic with benzoyl peroxide.

items.section_title: 6.3 · Objective b — Nails, distant reactions, and steroid-altered tinea
items.html: Choosing a vehicle for barrier preparations. Ointments are more occlusive than creams (or lotions). Emollients and barrier preparations are foundational for many inflammatory conditions, including xerosis, eczema, irritant dermatitis and diaper dermatitis.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 40

src.question: A 79-year-old man has severe xerosis of both lower legs and a barrier preparation is being chosen for him. What consideration should guide the choice of vehicle?
src.key: Ointments are more occlusive than creams
src.explanation: Emollients and barrier preparations are the foundation of treatment for many inflammatory conditions, and ointments are generally more occlusive than creams or lotions. Common uses include xerosis, eczema, irritant dermatitis, and diaper dermatitis.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective c — Alopecia
items.html: Non-scarring patchy hair loss with exclamation point hairs and nail pitting, in children. Topical corticosteroids are first line in children 10 years old and younger, avoiding the discomfort of intralesional injection in a young child.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 140

src.question: An 8-year-old boy has three smooth, non-scarring patches of hair loss on the scalp with exclamation point hairs at the margins and fine pitting of several fingernails. A potassium hydroxide preparation of plucked hairs is negative. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
src.key: Topical corticosteroids
src.explanation: Topical steroids are first line in children 10 years old and younger. The child is 8, which places him in that group and avoids the discomfort of intralesional injection in a young child.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Urticaria versus erythema multiforme. Urticarial wheals are pruritic, migratory and blanch fully, with no fixed target lesions; wheals migrate and last under 24 hours. Fixity over days identifies erythema multiforme.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 10

src.question: A 28-year-old woman has an annular eruption of the forearms and the clinician is distinguishing erythema multiforme from urticaria. What feature most reliably separates them?
src.key: Wheals migrate and last under 24 hours
src.explanation: The differential states that urticarial wheals are pruritic, migratory, and blanch fully, with no fixed target lesions and individual lesions lasting less than 24 hours. Fixity over days is what identifies erythema multiforme.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Allergic contact dermatitis. It is an immunologic cell-mediated, delayed, type IV hypersensitivity reaction, most often to urushiol, the sap of Toxicodendron species (poison ivy, sumac, oak); roughly 50 to 75 percent of people in the United States are allergic.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 85

src.question: A 19-year-old man develops an intensely pruritic vesicular eruption in linear streaks two days after clearing brush. What immunological mechanism underlies allergic contact dermatitis, and what is its most common cause in the United States?
src.key: Delayed type IV reaction, most often to urushiol
src.explanation: Allergic contact dermatitis is an immunologic cell-mediated, delayed, type IV hypersensitivity reaction. Urushiol sap of Toxicodendron species, found in poison ivy, poison sumac, and poison oak, is the most common cause, and roughly 50 to 75 percent of people in the United States are allergic to these plants.

items.section_title: 6.5 · Objective b — Varicella and herpes zoster
items.html: Phases of a dermatomal grouped-vesicle eruption. Pre-eruptive (dysesthesia or pain in the dermatome, lesions by 48 to 72 hours), acute eruptive (grouped herpetiform vesicles on erythematous base, new lesions over 3 to 5 days), and postherpetic neuralgia (chronic).
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 97

src.question: A 68-year-old woman describes three days of burning pain in a band across her left flank, followed by an eruption. Examination shows grouped vesicles on an erythematous base confined to a single band that stops abruptly at the midline. What are the three clinical phases of this condition?
src.key: Pre-eruptive, acute eruptive, postherpetic neuralgia
src.explanation: The pre-eruptive phase is characterized by dysesthesia or pain within the affected dermatome with lesion onset by 48 to 72 hours; the acute eruptive phase produces grouped herpetiform vesicles on an erythematous base with new lesions forming over 3 to 5 days; and postherpetic neuralgia is the chronic phase.

items.section_title: 9.5 · Objective 1 — Malignant melanoma
items.html: Melanoma re-excision margins by thickness. Definitive local margins are 0.5 to 1 cm in situ, 1 cm under 1 mm, and 1 to 2 cm over 1 mm; expert-center referral applies to melanoma deeper than 1 mm or with lymph node involvement.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 52

src.question: A 58-year-old woman has a melanoma on the calf with a Breslow thickness of 1.4 mm and is being planned for definitive local treatment. What are the recommended re-excision margins for melanoma by thickness?
src.key: 0.5 to 1 cm in situ, 1 cm under 1 mm, 1 to 2 cm over
src.explanation: Definitive local treatment uses a 0.5 to 1 cm margin for in situ disease, 1 cm for tumors under 1 mm, and 1 to 2 cm for tumors over 1 mm. Expert-center referral applies to melanoma deeper than 1 mm or with lymph node involvement.

items.section_title: 1.7 · Objective h — Recall counseling strategies to help patients adhere to treatment plans
items.html: Barriers to treatment and medication adherence. Cost and affordability of medications or services, low health literacy or lack of understanding, and cultural or religious considerations.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 29

src.question: A 61-year-old woman has not been taking a medication prescribed for her three months ago and is reluctant to say why. Which barriers to treatment and medication adherence should be considered?
src.key: Cost, health literacy, and culture
src.explanation: Barriers to treatment and medication adherence include the cost and affordability of medications or services, low health literacy or lack of understanding, and cultural or religious considerations.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Scabies transmission and itch timing. Transmission is by close contact for 15 to 20 minutes, and also from the bedding or underclothing of an infested individual; itch appears 4 to 6 weeks after infestation, and many patients have no symptoms for up to 3 months.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 5

src.question: A 26-year-old man develops severe nocturnal itching six weeks after his partner was treated for scabies. How is scabies typically transmitted, and how long after infestation does pruritus appear?
src.key: Close contact 15 to 20 minutes; itch at 4 weeks
src.explanation: Scabies is transmitted by close physical contact for 15 to 20 minutes and may also be acquired from the bedding or underclothing of an infested individual. Pruritus appears 4 to 6 weeks after initial infestation, and many patients do not develop symptoms for up to 3 months.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objective a — Follicular and glandular infections
items.html: Furuncle. A deep-seated abscess of a hair follicle and the adjacent subcutaneous tissue; Staphylococcus aureus is the commonest organism.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 59

src.question: What is a furuncle?
src.key: A deep-seated abscess of a hair follicle and the adjacent subcutaneous tissue
src.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is the commonest organism.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
items.html: Impetigo. A superficial epidermal infection, most often Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes; it is very contagious and autoinoculable, and common in infants and children.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 85

src.question: What level of the skin does impetigo infect, and which organisms cause it?
src.key: A superficial epidermal infection, most often Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes
src.explanation: It is very contagious and autoinoculable, and common in infants and children.

items.section_title: 6.7 · Objective b — Molluscum contagiosum and warts
items.html: Variations of verruca. Five variants are recognized: verruca vulgaris, verruca plana, verruca plantaris, mosaic warts, and genital warts.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 138

src.question: Which variations of verruca are recognized?
src.key: Verruca vulgaris, verruca plana, verruca plantaris, mosaic warts, and genital warts
src.explanation: Correct — five variants.

items.section_title: 6.7 · Objective b — Molluscum contagiosum and warts
items.html: Verruca vulgaris. It occurs most often between 5 and 20 years, with spontaneous resolution; common warts usually resolve on their own.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 140

src.question: At what ages does verruca vulgaris occur most often, and what is its natural history?
src.key: Most often between 5 and 20 years, with spontaneous resolution
src.explanation: Correct — common warts usually resolve on their own.

items.section_title: 6.2 · Objective b — The dermatophytes, by body site
items.html: Tinea manuum. On the dorsum of the hand it shows an annular plaque like tinea corporis; the palm is hyperkeratotic like tinea pedis (thickened, dry and scaly), and palms and soles can be infected at once.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 54

src.question: How does tinea manuum present on the dorsum of the hand compared with the palm?
src.key: The dorsum shows an annular plaque like tinea corporis; the palm is hyperkeratotic like tinea pedis
src.explanation: Correct — the palm becomes thickened, dry and scaly, and both palms and soles can be infected at once.

items.section_title: 6.2 · Objective b — The dermatophytes, by body site
items.html: Variations of tinea pedis. Interdigital, hyperkeratotic and vesiculobullous; all three are caused by Trichophyton species, and the interdigital form is the most common.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 37

src.question: What are the three named variations of tinea pedis?
src.key: Interdigital, hyperkeratotic, vesiculobullous
src.explanation: Correct — all three are caused by Trichophyton species, and the interdigital form is the most common.

items.section_title: 6.3 · Objective b — Nails, distant reactions, and steroid-altered tinea
items.html: Onychomycosis. Trichophyton rubrum causes most cases (dermatophytes cause most, though yeasts and molds also occur); distal lateral disease produces debris, onycholysis, thickening and crumbling, with discoloration.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 47

src.question: Which organism causes most onychomycosis, and what does distal lateral disease produce?
src.key: Trichophyton rubrum; debris, onycholysis, thickening and crumbling
src.explanation: Correct — with discoloration too. Yeasts and molds also occur, but dermatophytes cause most cases.

items.section_title: 6.5 · Objective b — Varicella and herpes zoster
items.html: Varicella contagious period. The child is contagious from 1 to 2 days before the rash until all lesions have crusted; contagiousness begins before the rash is visible.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 89

src.question: A parent asks when her child with varicella may return to normal activities. Which is the most appropriate response?
src.key: The child is contagious from 1 to 2 days before the rash until all lesions have crusted
src.explanation: Correct — contagiousness begins before the rash is visible.

items.section_title: 5.4 · Objective a — Spider bites
items.html: Hobo spider. It is found in the Pacific Northwest, where it is the predominant cause of necrotic arachnidism and is mistaken for the brown recluse; it is brown with a gray herringbone pattern and bites from July to September.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 63

src.question: Where is the hobo spider found and what is it often mistaken for?
src.key: The Pacific Northwest, where it is the predominant cause of necrotic arachnidism and is mistaken for the brown recluse
src.explanation: Correct — it is brown with a gray herringbone pattern and bites from July to September.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Objective a — Tick-borne illness
items.html: Oral antibiotics for Lyme disease. Doxycycline is first line, with amoxicillin as the alternative first line for early erythema migrans; macrolides such as azithromycin are second line.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 79

src.question: What is the first-line oral antibiotic for Lyme disease, and what is used in children and pregnancy?
src.key: Doxycycline first line, with amoxicillin as the alternative first line for early erythema migrans
src.explanation: Correct — macrolides such as azithromycin are second line, over a ten to fourteen day course.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Objective a — Tick-borne illness
items.html: Attached tick. Remove the tick immediately, then watch for the rash and constitutional symptoms; antibiotics are indicated once the disease is diagnosed, at all stages.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 79

src.question: A 45-year-old woman finds an attached tick on her leg after gardening in Maine. Which is the most appropriate immediate action?
src.key: Remove the tick immediately, then watch for the rash and constitutional symptoms
src.explanation: Correct — antibiotics are indicated once the disease is diagnosed, at all stages.

items.section_title: 5.2 · Objective a — Bedbugs, fleas, stings and caterpillars
items.html: Mild local reaction to a bee sting. Treat with cleaning, ice, and possibly injection of local anesthetic for pain control; management is graded to the severity of the reaction.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: A 34-year-old woman has a mild local reaction to a bee sting with pain and a small area of redness. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
src.key: Cleaning, ice, and possibly injection of local anesthetic for pain control
src.explanation: Correct — management is graded to the severity of the reaction.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Objective a — Tick-borne illness
items.html: Rocky Mountain spotted fever without rash. It can present without a rash in about 20% of patients; the full triad is present in only about 60%, and the rash follows the fever.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 85

src.question: A 55-year-old man from a rural area has fever, severe headache, nausea and calf pain for five days but no rash. Which is the most appropriate consideration?
src.key: Rocky Mountain spotted fever can present without a rash in about 20% of patients
src.explanation: Correct — the full triad is present in only about 60% and the rash follows the fever.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Burrow ink test for scabies. When scraping is difficult, blue or black ink is applied to a suspected lesion, looking for a zigzag line running across and away from the lesion.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 14

src.question: A 27-year-old woman with suspected scabies has heavily excoriated hands and no intact burrow visible. Which test is most appropriate?
src.key: The burrow ink test, looking for a zigzag line running across and away from the lesion
src.explanation: Correct — blue or black ink is applied to a suspected lesion when scraping is difficult.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Drugs causing acanthosis nigricans. Niacin, corticosteroids, oral contraceptives and protease inhibitors; drug-induced disease sits alongside the insulin-resistant and malignant forms.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 22

src.question: Which drugs are named as causes of acanthosis nigricans?
src.key: Niacin, corticosteroids, oral contraceptives and protease inhibitors
src.explanation: Correct — drug-induced disease sits alongside the insulin-resistant and malignant forms.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Biologic for refractory chronic urticaria. Omalizumab, an anti-immunoglobulin E antibody given every four weeks, is approved for refractory chronic urticaria.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 39

src.question: Which biologic is approved for refractory chronic urticaria?
src.key: Omalizumab, an anti-immunoglobulin E antibody given every four weeks
src.explanation: at 300 mg subcutaneously.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective c — Alopecia
items.html: First-line treatment of alopecia areata by age. Topical steroids are first line in children ten and under; intralesional steroids are first line in adolescents and adults, since injections are avoided in young children.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 140

src.question: How does first-line treatment of alopecia areata differ between children and adults?
src.key: Topical steroids first line in children ten and under; intralesional steroids first line in adolescents and adults
src.explanation: Correct — injections are avoided in young children.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Common acquired nevus color. It is skin colored, brown or pink, with a homogenous surface and color, whereas a dark brown or black nevus on light skin is suspicious; it is usually under 6 mm, round to oval, and sharply demarcated.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 36

src.question: A dark brown or black naevus on light skin is described as suspicious. What is the expected color of a common acquired naevus?
src.key: Skin colored, brown or pink, with a homogenous surface and color
src.explanation: Correct — they are usually under 6 mm, round to oval, and sharply demarcated.

items.section_title: 8.3 · Objective a — Vitiligo
items.html: First-line vitiligo treatment. Topical therapy suits under five percent involvement, ideally combined with phototherapy; calcineurin inhibitors are useful where steroids cannot be applied, such as face and neck.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 24

src.question: A 29-year-old has depigmented patches over roughly three percent of her body surface, mostly on her hands and around the mouth. Which first-line approach fits?
src.key: Topical therapy, with calcineurin inhibitors useful where steroids cannot be applied such as face and neck
src.explanation: Correct — topical therapy suits under five percent involvement, ideally combined with phototherapy.

items.section_title: 8.5 · Objective b — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Small congenital melanocytic nevus. Observation, since management balances melanoma risk with cosmetic and functional considerations; smaller lesions carry lower melanoma risk than larger ones.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 31

src.question: A 3-year-old has a small congenital melanocytic naevus on the forearm with no neurological symptoms. Which is the most appropriate management?
src.key: Observation, since management balances melanoma risk with cosmetic and functional considerations
src.explanation: Correct — smaller lesions carry lower melanoma risk than larger ones.

items.section_title: 9.5 · Objective 1 — Malignant melanoma
items.html: Melanoma stages 0 to II. Stage 0 is melanoma confined to the epidermal region of the skin; stage I is localized disease, only in skin and very thin; stage II is localized disease thicker than stage I. All three are still local.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 53

src.question: In the Stages of Melanoma diagram, what are stage 0, stage I and stage II?
src.key: Stage 0 is melanoma confined to the epidermal region of the skin; stage I is localized disease, only in skin and very thin; stage II is localized disease thicker than stage I
src.explanation: Correct — 0, I and II are all still local.

items.section_title: 9.1 · Objective 1 — Describe before you name
items.html: Examining a suspected malignant skin lesion. Use good lighting, dermoscopy when trained, and a total-body skin survey when indicated; examine palms, soles and nails, the oral mucosa when Kaposi sarcoma is possible, and regional nodes for invasive or high-risk disease.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 4

src.question: Which examination priorities apply to a suspected malignant cutaneous lesion?
src.key: Good lighting, dermoscopy when trained, and a total-body skin survey when indicated; palms, soles and nails; oral mucosa when Kaposi sarcoma is possible; regional nodes for invasive or high-risk disease
src.explanation: Correct — note the oral mucosa is tied specifically to Kaposi sarcoma.

also.key: Palms, soles and nails in all; the oral mucosa specifically when Kaposi sarcoma is possible; regional nodes for invasive or high-risk disease
also.explanation: Correct — the oral examination is tied to Kaposi sarcoma.

items.section_title: 9.5 · Objective 1 — Malignant melanoma
items.html: Melanoma subtype with delayed diagnosis. Acral lentiginous melanoma is frequently delayed in diagnosis, so early reporting is critical: patients report new pigment, widening bands or periungual pigment promptly.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 56

src.question: Which melanoma subtype is frequently delayed in diagnosis, making early reporting critical?
src.key: Acral lentiginous melanoma
src.explanation: Correct — which is why patients are told to report new pigment, widening bands or periungual pigment promptly.

items.section_title: 9.5 · Objective 1 — Malignant melanoma
items.html: Melanoma deeper than 1 mm. A thickness over 1 mm calls for a 1 to 2 cm re-excision margin and referral to an expert center; the same threshold governs both.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 52

src.question: A 63-year-old's melanoma is reported at 1.8 mm Breslow thickness. Which re-excision margin applies, and what else does that thickness trigger?
src.key: A 1 to 2 cm margin, and referral to an expert center because the lesion is deeper than 1 mm
src.explanation: Correct — the same threshold governs both.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: Nevus simplex. Most common on the head and neck and more noticeable with crying; it appears as pink to erythematous blanchable macules or patches, single or multiple.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 84

src.question: Where is nevus simplex most common, and what makes it more noticeable?
src.key: Head and neck; crying
src.explanation: Correct — pink to erythematous blanchable macules or patches, single or multiple.

items.section_title: 1.7 · Objective h — Recall counseling strategies to help patients adhere to treatment plans
items.html: Barriers to treatment and medication adherence. Mental health challenges or cognitive impairment are listed among the barriers, alongside cost, low health literacy, cultural or religious beliefs, fear of side effects, transportation and poor follow-up.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 29

src.question: Mental health challenges or cognitive impairment fall under which heading?
src.key: Barriers to treatment and medication adherence
src.explanation: They are listed among the barriers, alongside cost, low health literacy, cultural or religious beliefs, fear of side effects, transportation and poor follow-up.

items.section_title: 1.7 · Objective h — Recall counseling strategies to help patients adhere to treatment plans
items.html: FRAMES elements. Responsibility of the patient is the element that places the decision to change with the patient; FRAMES also includes feedback, advice, a menu of options, an empathetic style and promoting self-efficacy.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 28

src.question: Which element of FRAMES places the decision to change with the patient?
src.key: Responsibility of the patient
src.explanation: FRAMES includes responsibility of the patient as a distinct element, alongside feedback, advice, a menu of options, an empathetic style and promoting self-efficacy.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Objective d — Discuss clinical principles and decision-making
items.html: Good clinical decision-making. Remember you are often wrong, and consider the immediate implications; also slow down, weigh base rates, consider what data is truly relevant, and seek alternatives.
cites: 1. svClinical Reasoning and Problem Solving.pptx, Slide 26

src.question: Which of the following supports good clinical decision-making?
src.key: Remember you are often wrong, and consider the immediate implications
src.explanation: This appears alongside slowing down, weighing base rates, considering what data is truly relevant, and seeking alternatives.

items.section_title: 4.3 · Objective a — Impetigo, erysipelas, cellulitis and abscess
items.html: Cellulitis. Warm, tender erythema whose border fades out rather than stopping; the infection is deeper.
