cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 105

src.question: Name the condition shown.
src.key: Cellulitis
src.explanation: Warm, tender erythema whose border FADES OUT rather than stopping — the infection is deeper.

items.section_title: 4.4 · Objective a — Paronychia and necrotizing fasciitis
items.html: Acute paronychia. A red, swollen, acutely tender nail fold, with the nail plate itself still normal.
cites: 4.  Cutaneous Bacterial Infections.pptx, Slide 117

src.question: Name the condition shown.
src.key: Acute paronychia
src.explanation: A red, swollen, acutely tender NAIL FOLD, with the nail plate itself still normal.

items.section_title: 6.6 · Objective b — Herpes simplex and herpetic whitlow
items.html: Herpes simplex virus. A tight group of vesicles and erosion at the vermilion border, recurring in the same place.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 113

src.question: Name the condition shown.
src.key: Herpes simplex virus
src.explanation: A tight GROUP of vesicles and erosion at the VERMILION BORDER, recurring in the same place.

items.section_title: 7.2 · Objective a — Abnormal wound healing: keloid and hypertrophic scar
items.html: Keloid. Scar tissue that has grown beyond the boundaries of the original wound.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 13

src.question: Name the condition shown.
src.key: Keloid
src.explanation: Scar tissue that has grown BEYOND the boundaries of the original wound.

items.section_title: 7.7 · Objectives a & b — Neurofibromatosis, and the remaining lesions
items.html: Xanthelasma. Soft, flat yellow plaques near the inner canthus, prompting a lipid profile.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 104

src.question: Name the condition shown.
src.key: Xanthelasma
src.explanation: Soft flat YELLOW plaques near the inner canthus, prompting a lipid profile.

items.section_title: 9.2 · Objective 1 — Actinic keratosis
items.html: Squamous cell carcinoma. A firm nodule with heaped keratin or ulceration, on chronically sun-damaged skin.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 19

src.question: Name the condition shown.
src.key: Squamous cell carcinoma
src.explanation: A firm nodule with heaped KERATIN or ulceration, on chronically sun-damaged skin.

items.section_title: 8.4 · Objective a — The melanocytic naevi
items.html: Dysplastic melanocytic nevus. Diagnosis is by biopsy; management is observation, biopsy of all changing or developing lesions, excision where melanoma is a concern, and sun protection. Melanoma risk rises with the number of nevi present.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 44

src.question: How is dysplastic melanocytic naevus diagnosed and managed?
src.key: Diagnosis is by biopsy; management is observation, biopsy of all changing or developing lesions, excision where melanoma is a concern, and sun protection
src.explanation: Correct — melanoma risk rises with the number of naevi present.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Objective a — Tick-borne illness
items.html: Preventing tick-borne illness. Avoid tick habitat, use DEET, PMD or picaridin reapplied about every two hours, and treat clothing with pyrethrins; there is no human vaccine, though one exists for dogs.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 80

src.question: A 36-year-old woman who hikes in an endemic area asks how to protect herself. Which is the most appropriate advice?
src.key: Avoid tick habitat, use DEET, PMD or picaridin reapplied about every two hours, and treat clothing with pyrethrins
src.explanation: Correct — there is no human vaccine, though one exists for dogs.

items.section_title: 9.5 · Objective 1 — Malignant melanoma
items.html: Melanoma re-excision margin. A melanoma under 1 mm Breslow thickness with no adverse features takes a 1 cm margin.
cites: Premalignant and Malignant Cutaneous Lesions - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 52

src.question: A 52-year-old's melanoma is reported at 0.6 mm Breslow thickness with no adverse features. Which re-excision margin applies?
src.key: A 1 cm margin
src.explanation: Correct — lesions under 1 mm take a 1 cm margin.

items.section_title: 8.1 · Objective a — Ephelides, lentigines and solar lentigo
items.html: Solar lentigines. Arise from basal melanocyte proliferation with more melanin production. They are strongly associated with older age (about 90 percent by age 50), sun damage, tanning, a history of ephelides, and birth control use.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 13

src.question: A 63-year-old man has multiple light to dark brown macules with well-defined but irregular borders that tend to coalesce over his shoulders, where he has had severe sunburns. What is the underlying process and its epidemiological association?
src.key: Basal melanocyte proliferation with more melanin
src.explanation: Solar lentigines arise from proliferation of basal melanocytes with increased melanin production and are strongly associated with older age, present in about 90 percent by age 50, along with sun damage, tanning, a history of ephelides, and birth control use.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Erythematotelangiectatic rosacea. The most common subtype: persistent central facial erythema, flushing, and telangiectasias with sensitive, stinging skin, and specifically no papules or pustules.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 66

src.question: A 45-year-old fair-skinned woman reports facial flushing that worsens with sun exposure, hot drinks, and alcohol. Examination shows persistent central facial erythema with telangiectasias across the cheeks and nose, and she describes her skin as stinging easily. There are no papules, no pustules, and no comedones. What subtype does she have?
src.key: Erythematotelangiectatic rosacea
src.explanation: The erythematotelangiectatic subtype produces persistent central facial erythema, flushing, and telangiectasias with sensitive stinging skin, and specifically no papules or pustules. It is the most common subtype.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Toxic epidermal necrolysis disposition. Admission to a burn unit or intensive care unit is mandatory for all cases, together with immediate discontinuation of all suspect drugs, fluid resuscitation estimated as for major burns, and non-adhesive biological dressings.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 90

src.question: A 57-year-old man has confirmed toxic epidermal necrolysis with epidermal detachment of 45 percent of his body surface area. What is the mandatory disposition?
src.key: A burn unit or intensive care unit
src.explanation: Burn unit or intensive care admission is mandatory for all cases of toxic epidermal necrolysis, together with immediate discontinuation of all suspect drugs, fluid resuscitation estimated as for major burns, and non-adhesive biological dressings.

items.section_title: 6.4 · Objective b — The yeasts: candidal intertrigo and pityriasis versicolor
items.html: Candidal intertrigo treatment. Well-demarcated erythematous patches with satellite papules and pustules are treated with a topical azole, which covers both Candida and dermatophytes, whereas topical nystatin treats Candida only.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 72

src.question: A 61-year-old woman with obesity has a well-demarcated erythematous patch in the inframammary fold with several small papules and pustules on adjacent skin just beyond the main area of redness. What topical choice covers both possibilities?
src.key: A topical azole
src.explanation: Satellite papules and pustules accompany the well-demarcated erythematous patches of candidal intertrigo. Topical nystatin treats Candida only, whereas topical azoles treat both Candida and dermatophytes.

items.section_title: 5.4 · Objective a — Spider bites
items.html: Hobo spider. Also called the aggressive house spider, it is the predominant cause of necrotic arachnidism in the Pacific Northwest. The bite is painless, with induration and paresthesia within 30 minutes, a large erythematous area, and vesicles during the first 36 hours.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 64

src.question: A 38-year-old man in Oregon has a painless bite on the forearm that has become indurated with a large surrounding erythematous area. In which region of the United States is the hobo spider the predominant cause of necrotic arachnidism?
src.key: The Pacific Northwest
src.explanation: The hobo spider, also called the aggressive house spider, is the predominant cause of necrotic arachnidism in the Pacific Northwest. The bite is painless, with induration and paresthesia of the bite site within 30 minutes, a large erythematous area, and vesicle formation during the first 36 hours.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Generalized granuloma annulare screening. Fasting glucose and hemoglobin A1c screen for diabetes, alongside a lipid panel and thyroid studies for associated systemic disease.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 51

src.question: A 46-year-old man is found to have hundreds of small papules over the trunk and extremities consistent with generalized granuloma annulare. What screening is most appropriate?
src.key: Fasting glucose and hemoglobin A1c
src.explanation: Fasting glucose and hemoglobin A1c are used to screen for diabetes in generalized granuloma annulare, alongside a lipid panel and thyroid studies for associated systemic disease.

items.section_title: 7.6 · Objective a — The vascular lesions
items.html: Hemangioma complications. Hemangiomas may cause compression of vital structures, block vision, interfere with feeding or respiration, obstruct the external auditory canal, and occur at extracutaneous sites.
cites: 7. Benign Skin Lesions Prof Griffenkranz 8-25-2025-2.pptx, Slide 71

src.question: A 5-month-old girl has a large hemangioma of the face lying close to the eye and the corner of the mouth. What complications should be considered?
src.key: Compression of vital structures
src.explanation: Hemangiomas may compress vital structures, block vision, interfere with feeding or respiration, obstruct the external auditory canal, and occur at extracutaneous sites.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Objective a — Reactive and immune-mediated conditions
items.html: Epidermolysis bullosa diagnosis. Skin biopsy with transmission electron microscopy is the gold standard for the level of cleavage. Immunofluorescence antigen mapping localizes missing or reduced proteins; genetic testing is confirmatory and guides prognosis and family counseling.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 31

src.question: A 3-month-old infant with blistering at sites of minor friction is being investigated to establish where in the skin the split is occurring. What diagnostic test is considered the gold standard for establishing the level of cleavage in epidermolysis bullosa?
src.key: Skin biopsy with transmission electron microscopy
src.explanation: Skin biopsy with transmission electron microscopy is the gold standard for determining the cleavage plane. Immunofluorescence antigen mapping localizes missing or reduced proteins, and genetic testing is confirmatory and guides prognosis and family counseling.

items.section_title: 6.6 · Objective b — Herpes simplex and herpetic whitlow
items.html: Herpes simplex virus infection. A first episode gives painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base, for example on the vulva, that become shallow painful ulcers, with a systemic prodrome of fever, headache and tender inguinal nodes.
cites: 6. Fungal and Viral Skin Infections - Jaquith.pptx, Slide 119

src.question: A 24-year-old has a first episode of painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the vulva, which have broken down into shallow ulcers. She has fever, headache and tender inguinal nodes. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
src.key: Herpes simplex virus infection
src.explanation: Correct — grouped vesicles becoming shallow painful ulcers, with a systemic prodrome.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Topical azelaic acid in rosacea. At 15 to 20%, it is anti-inflammatory and anti-keratinizing, and is effective for both papulopustular and erythematotelangiectatic rosacea.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 69

src.question: Which forms of rosacea does topical azelaic acid treat?
src.key: Papulopustular and erythematotelangiectatic
src.explanation: Correct — azelaic acid 15 to 20% is anti-inflammatory and anti-keratinizing, and it is effective for both papulopustular and erythematotelangiectatic rosacea.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective a — Photoreactions and photodermatology
items.html: Classic causes of phototoxicity. Tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, amiodarone and thiazides, alongside furosemide, voriconazole, some nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and psoralens.
cites: 3. Dermatology  II.pptx, Slide 98

src.question: Which drug classes are classic causes of phototoxicity?
src.key: Tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, amiodarone and thiazides
src.explanation: alongside furosemide, voriconazole, some nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and psoralens.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Objective c — Papulosquamous disease
items.html: Four Ps of lichen planus. Pruritic, purple, polygonal, papules or plaques: flat-topped, pink to violaceous and shiny, coalescing into larger plaques.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 176

src.question: What are the four Ps of lichen planus?
src.key: Pruritic, purple, polygonal, papules or plaques
src.explanation: Correct — flat-topped, pink to violaceous and shiny, coalescing into larger plaques.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Patch testing. It is the diagnostic test for atypical, adult-onset or treatment-resistant eczema, and eyelid and hand involvement raises contact allergy.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 56

src.question: A 32-year-old woman has adult-onset eczema that has not responded to appropriate topical therapy over several months. Her rash involves the eyelids and hands. Which is the most appropriate diagnostic test?
src.key: Patch testing
src.explanation: Correct — patch testing is indicated for atypical, adult-onset or treatment-resistant disease, and eyelid and hand involvement raises contact allergy.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective c — The eczema and dermatitis family
items.html: Irritant contact dermatitis. The eyelids and face are among the commonest sites, from makeup and masks, with a glazed, well-demarcated appearance.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 81

src.question: A 38-year-old woman has a glazed, well-demarcated dermatitis over both eyelids that began after she started using a new cosmetic. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
src.key: Irritant contact dermatitis
src.explanation: Correct — the eyelids and face are among the commonest sites, from makeup and masks, and the glazed well-demarcated appearance fits.

items.section_title: 6.1 · Objective a — Reading a potassium hydroxide preparation
items.html: Testing round, scaly plaques. The initial test is a potassium hydroxide preparation, because tinea corporis is the main differential and is excluded by it; absent central clearing already argues against tinea corporis.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 74

src.question: A 62-year-old man has several intensely itchy round plaques on his lower legs, 2 to 4 cm across, light pink with scale and crusting. The plaques are uniform throughout without any central clearing. Which is the most appropriate initial diagnostic test?
src.key: Potassium hydroxide preparation
src.explanation: Tinea corporis is the main differential and is excluded by potassium hydroxide, though the absent central clearing already argues against it.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective c — Alopecia
items.html: Alopecia areata treatment. Intralesional corticosteroids are first line in adolescents and adults; topical steroids are first line for children aged ten and under.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 140

src.question: A 27-year-old man with two patches of alopecia areata on the scalp asks about treatment. Which is the most appropriate first-line option?
src.key: Intralesional corticosteroids
src.explanation: Correct — first line in adolescents and adults; topical steroids are first line for children aged ten and under.

items.section_title: 6.1 · Objective a — Reading a potassium hydroxide preparation
items.html: Diaper rash with fold involvement. Fold involvement and satellite lesions suggest Candida; the test is a potassium hydroxide preparation, where budding yeast or pseudohyphae supports it.
cites: 2. General Dermatology I.pptx, Slide 108

src.question: A 10-month-old has a diaper rash involving the inguinal folds with satellite papules beyond the main area. Which is the most appropriate diagnostic test?
src.key: Potassium hydroxide preparation
src.explanation: Correct — fold involvement and satellite lesions suggest Candida, and identification of budding yeast or pseudohyphae supports it.

items.section_title: 8.5 · Objective b — Care strategies in adults and the elderly
items.html: Cosmetic removal of solar lentigines. Retinoids, cryotherapy or quality-switched laser; treatment is not necessary as the lesions are benign.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 15

src.question: Which agents are used for cosmetic removal of solar lentigines?
src.key: Retinoids, cryotherapy or quality-switched laser
src.explanation: Correct — treatment is not necessary as the lesions are benign.

items.section_title: 8.1 · Objective a — Ephelides, lentigines and solar lentigo
items.html: Agminated lentigines. A grouping of small light brown macules, one of the named lentigo types.
cites: CMS I Pigmented Skin Lesions - Shahsv-2.pptx, Slide 11

src.question: A 7-year-old boy has a cluster of small light brown macules grouped closely together on one forearm. Which term describes this pattern?
src.key: Agminated lentigines
src.explanation: Correct — a grouping of small light brown macules, one of the named lentigo types.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objective a — Scabies and lice
items.html: Scabies not cleared by individual therapy. The regimen is ivermectin every two weeks for two to three doses, with topical permethrin every three days to weekly, the same regimen used for hyperkeratotic or immunosuppressed disease.
cites: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 19

src.question: A patient's scabies has not cleared after individual therapy. Which regimen is described?
src.key: Ivermectin every two weeks for two to three doses, with topical permethrin every three days to weekly
src.explanation: Correct — the same regimen used for hyperkeratotic or immunosuppressed disease.
